title: Quiz "Check" button label is invisible until an answer is picked
problem: The quiz drill's footer CTA stacks a hardcoded grey fill and white text on top of the Button primitive's own disabled styling. `Button` already applies `disabled:opacity-40 disabled:shadow-none` (src/components/ui.tsx:108), so the whole element renders at 40% opacity with `#C7D0CE` behind `#FFFFFF` text. White-on-#C7D0CE is 1.57:1 before the opacity multiply; composited over the sand page at 40% it lands near 1.1:1.
userImpact: On every recognise/recall drill the learner sees a near-blank grey bar where the primary action should be. They cannot read the word "Check", so the footer looks broken or disabled-for-no-reason until they happen to tap an answer.
evidence: src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:572 `className={`h-[54px] rounded-[17px] ${picked === null ? "!bg-[#C7D0CE] !text-white" : ""}`}` on a `<Button ... disabled={picked === null}>`; src/components/ui.tsx:108 adds `disabled:opacity-40` to every Button. #C7D0CE is not a palette colour (tailwind.config.js has no such token).
proposedFix: Delete the `!bg-[#C7D0CE] !text-white` override entirely and let `Button`'s built-in disabled state handle it, or if a distinct disabled skin is wanted, add a real `disabled` variant to `variantClasses` in src/components/ui.tsx using `bg-line text-muted` (4.9:1) and drop `disabled:opacity-40` for that variant so opacity is not applied twice.

title: "Free camera" hub tile prints paper-white text on gold at 1.8:1
problem: The shared tile text classes hardcode `text-paper` for the title and `text-white/80` for the subtitle, then one of the five tiles is filled `bg-gold`. Paper (#FBF7EF) on gold (#E6B24C) is 1.81:1; the subtitle at 80% alpha is worse. Both button systems in the codebase pair gold with ink for exactly this reason (`gold: "bg-gold text-ink extruded-gold"` in ui.tsx:67 and `gold: "bg-gold text-ink spring-gold"` in dc.tsx:36), so this tile breaks an already-established pairing rule.
userImpact: On the Practise tab, one of the four always-visible hub tiles has an unreadable label and description. The learner sees a blank yellow square and has to tap it to find out what it does.
evidence: src/screens/PractiseChooser.tsx:31 `const TILE_TITLE = "...text-paper text-start"`, :32 `const TILE_SUB = "...text-white/80..."`, :93 `className={`${TILE_BASE} bg-gold`}`. Same file:30 `const CHIP = "...bg-white/20 ...text-paper"` puts the 📷 glyph in the same unreadable pairing.
proposedFix: Make TILE_TITLE/TILE_SUB/CHIP take the foreground as a parameter rather than baking `text-paper`, and give the gold tile `text-ink` / `text-ink/70` / `bg-ink/10 text-ink`. The other four tiles (teal, coral-deep, teal-deep) keep paper.

title: Home path's Start sheet CTA uses the pre-H15 coral that fails AA
problem: The bottom-sheet action button is styled with raw inline hex: `#E8654C` fill under `#FBF7EF` 16px/700 text = 3.07:1, and the locked state is `#EDE3D2` under `#8FA09D` at 85% opacity ≈ 2.1:1. The design system already fixed this: tailwind.config.js:10 keeps `coral.DEFAULT` for fills but both button primitives switched their text-bearing surface to `coral-deep` (#B54834, 4.99:1 on paper) precisely because "white-on-coral (DEFAULT #E8654C) measured 3.28:1 — below AA" (src/components/ui.tsx:62-63). The Home sheet never got migrated.
userImpact: The single most important call to action in the app — the "Start" button on the current lesson node — has washed-out, hard-to-read text, and the "Locked" label on locked nodes is close to invisible in daylight.
evidence: src/screens/Home.tsx:578 `const btnBg = locked ? "#EDE3D2" : st === "done" ? "#0F6E6A" : "#E8654C";` and :637 `color: locked ? "#8FA09D" : "#FBF7EF", opacity: locked ? 0.85 : 1`. Compare src/components/ui.tsx:65 `primary: "bg-coral-deep text-white extruded-coral"`.
proposedFix:
Replace the whole inline-styled sheet button with `<Button variant={st === "done" ? "secondary" : "primary"} size="lg" full disabled={locked}>`. That picks up coral-deep/teal, the extruded shadow, the 56px size and the disabled treatment from one place. If the inline route must stay, at minimum swap `#E8654C`→`#B54834`, `#C54F3A`→`#9C3D2C`, and `#8FA09D`→`#566B68`.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The hex swap (#E8654C→#B54834, #C54F3A→#9C3D2C, #8FA09D→#566B68) is the right fix and is the one to do. Do NOT swap in `<Button>`: it would change the sheet CTA's geometry (rounded-2xl 24px vs the sheet's 16px, 6px extrusion vs the sheet's 5px, min-h-[56px] vs its 15px padding) and Button's `disabled:opacity-40` would make the 'Locked' label fainter than it is today, not better.

title: text-gold on gold tint renders icons and labels at ~1.6:1 in four places
problem: Four separate surfaces pair the gold *fill* token with a gold *tint* background: `bg-gold/20 text-gold`, `bg-gold/10 text-gold`, `border-gold/20 bg-gold/10 text-gold`. Gold (#E6B24C, L=0.49) on a 10–20% gold wash over paper (L≈0.83) is 1.6–1.8:1. The palette has `gold.deep` (#7F621F) added specifically as the AA-safe gold foreground and it is used correctly in 16 other spots (`text-gold-deep`), so this is an unmigrated minority, not a missing token.
userImpact: The trophy icon on the Family milestone card, its forward chevron, the "due" hourglass badge on Progress review rows, and the shield icon on the privacy page all read as faint smudges. On the Family card the trophy is the only visual, so the card looks empty.
evidence: src/screens/Family.tsx:434 `<span className="...rounded-xl bg-gold/20 text-gold">` and :451 `<Icon name="arrow_forward_ios" className="text-gold rtl:rotate-180" />`; src/screens/Progress.tsx:849 `tone === "due" ? "bg-gold/10 text-gold" : "bg-teal/5 text-teal"`; src/screens/InfoPages.tsx:251 `iconTone === "gold" ? "border-gold/20 bg-gold/10 text-gold" : ...`.
proposedFix: Change `text-gold` to `text-gold-deep` at all four sites. Then add a lint-visible rule in DESIGN-SYSTEM.md: gold is a fill-only token; `gold-deep` is the only gold permitted as a foreground on a light surface.

title: "gold-deep" and "coral-deep" name two different colours each
problem: The rebuild contract (design/rebuild-source/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:31) defines `gold-deep` as #C89A3D and `coral-deep` as #C54F3A. The H15 contrast pass then redefined the Tailwind tokens to `gold.deep: "#7F621F"` and `coral.deep: "#B54834"` — completely different colours — without migrating the ~14 places that had already inlined the old hex. The result: `text-gold-deep` in a class paints dark olive #7F621F, while `boxShadow: "0 4px 0 #C89A3D"` two lines away paints the original gold. The same drift exists for `muted`: the token is #566B68 but #5C726F is still inlined in Home.
userImpact: A learner sees two visibly different "deep golds" on the same screen — for example the AllSigns detail play button's edge (#C89A3D) beside the mastered-status caption (#7F621F). Nobody can reason about the palette from the token names any more, so every future colour edit reintroduces drift.
evidence: tailwind.config.js:15 `gold: { DEFAULT: "#E6B24C", soft: "#F0C879", deep: "#7F621F", mid: "#E6B24C" }` vs design/rebuild-source/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:31 "`gold-deep` `#C89A3D`". #C89A3D still hardcoded at src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:66, :564, :654, src/screens/Progress.tsx:340,352,423,550, src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:428, src/screens/Home.tsx:220,267, src/styles.css:96,108. #C54F3A still hardcoded at src/screens/Home.tsx:189 and :579. #5C726F at src/screens/Home.tsx:629.
proposedFix:
Rename the AA-safe values to what they are: `gold.ink` (#7F621F) and `coral.ink` (#B54834) for text/foreground, and keep `gold.deep`/`coral.deep` as the #C89A3D/#C54F3A edge tones the extrusions actually use. Then replace every inline #C89A3D → `gold-deep`, #C54F3A → `coral-deep`, #5C726F → `muted`, and update DESIGN-SYSTEM.md §1 to match. Add `edge` tokens for #9C3D2C / #0A4F4C / #C9993E so styles.css stops hardcoding them too.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The rename as written is a regression risk: renaming #7F621F from `gold.deep` to `gold.ink` and giving `gold-deep` back to #C89A3D silently repaints all 16 existing `text-gold-deep` call sites (Home.tsx:372,452,546; Progress.tsx:707; LessonPlayer.tsx:353,840; Words.tsx:143,159; Fingerspell.tsx:369; Settings.tsx:245; AllSigns.tsx:32,34; Onboarding.tsx:442; CameraTrainer.tsx:480,552) back to the 2.26:1 gold H15 removed. The migration of those sites to the new name must land in the same commit, and the fix does not mention it. Cheaper and safer: leave the tokens alone, add `gold.edge`/`coral.edge`/`teal.edge` for #C89A3D/#9C3D2C/#0A4F4C, and correct DESIGN-SYSTEM.md §1 to the shipped values.

title: Two parallel button systems with colliding variant names and opposite meanings
problem: `Button` (ui.tsx) and `SpringButton` (dc.tsx) are both live: 9 files import one, 5 import the other. They disagree on almost everything. `Button`'s default emphasis colour is coral (`primary`), `SpringButton`'s is teal. `ghost` in ui.tsx is transparent with a 2px teal border; `ghost` in dc.tsx is a filled sand chip with a 1px hairline. Light text is `text-white` in one and `text-paper` in the other. The extrusion depth is 6px in one (`extruded-*`) and 5px in the other (`spring-*`), and the gold edge tone even differs (`#c9993e` vs `#c89a3d`). Sizes disagree too — ui `md` is `rounded-2xl px-6 py-3.5 min-h-[48px]`, dc `md` is `rounded-xl px-7 py-4 min-h-[48px]`.
userImpact: Inside a single lesson the "Continue →" button is coral on the watch step and teal on the quiz and results steps, so the learner cannot learn "the coloured button moves me forward". Across screens the same-looking action presses down by different amounts and has two different corner radii.
evidence: src/components/ui.tsx:64-76 (`primary: "bg-coral-deep text-white extruded-coral"`, `ghost: "bg-transparent text-teal border-2 border-teal/30"`) vs src/components/dc.tsx:33-44 (`teal: "bg-teal text-paper spring spring-teal"`, `ghost: "bg-sand text-ink border border-line"`). src/styles.css:37 `0 6px 0 0 #9c3d2c` vs :93 `0 5px 0 #9c3d2c`; :51 `#c9993e` vs :96 `#c89a3d`. Drift in use: src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:372 `variant="primary"` for Continue, :570 and :887 `variant="secondary"` for the same Continue action.
proposedFix:
Pick `SpringButton` (it is what DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:96 documents as canonical), re-express `Button` as a thin alias that maps primary→coral, secondary→teal, gold→gold, ghost→ghost, and delete `variantClasses`/`sizeClasses`/`extruded-*` from ui.tsx and styles.css. Then make one pass over LessonPlayer so every forward action uses the same variant.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Aliasing `Button` onto `SpringButton` cannot be a straight variant map: dc's `ghost` is a FILLED sand chip (`bg-sand text-ink border border-line`, dc.tsx:37) while ui's `ghost` is transparent with a teal border. The ghost call sites that sit on dark surfaces or on sand would break — CameraTrainer.tsx:576 and :586 render ghost buttons over the camera stage (:586 already fights the primitive with `!border-0 !min-h-0 !text-teal`), and Words.tsx:173 uses ghost as a dismiss on a sand sheet. Either keep ui's ghost as a fifth SpringButton variant, or hand-audit those three sites. The single-variant sweep of LessonPlayer's forward action is the valuable half and can be done on its own in minutes.

title: Three documented primitives are exported and never used; screens re-implement them by hand
problem: `Tile` ("the ONE selectable affordance… replaces the per-screen coral-vs-gold-vs-nothing selection drift") has zero call sites. `OnDeviceBadge` ("place on every camera frame") has zero call sites. `ConfidenceRing` has zero call sites. Meanwhile there are 22 hand-rolled `aria-pressed` selection controls across 8 screens, CameraTrainer hand-draws the confidence ring in inline SVG, and CameraTrainer renders the privacy badge twice in two different visual treatments.
userImpact: Selecting something means a different thing on every screen: teal fill in Onboarding personas and Settings language, gold fill for the "deaf" persona and for Settings daily-goal, teal border + teal check in Settings hand, coral fill in Tile's own Chip, teal fill + hard shadow in AllSigns filters and Progress tabs. The user never learns one "this is chosen" signal. The on-device privacy promise also looks like two different components on the same camera screen.
evidence: `grep -rE "<Tile[ />]"` and `<OnDeviceBadge` and `<ConfidenceRing` over src return zero hits outside their definitions (src/components/Tile.tsx:11, src/components/dc.tsx:199, dc.tsx:247). Hand-rolled equivalents: src/screens/Settings.tsx:198-199 (teal border select), :240-241 (gold border select), src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:425-431 (teal fill / gold fill), src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:210-213, src/screens/Progress.tsx:173-178. Ring re-implemented at src/components/CameraTrainer.tsx:783-797 with the identical `#E6B24C` arc. Privacy badge re-implemented at CameraTrainer.tsx:609-614 (sand pill) and :718 (bare white text).
proposedFix:
Adopt `Tile`/`Chip` in Settings (hand + goal), Onboarding (persona, hand, goal, language), AllSigns filters and Progress tabs — one selected treatment, one check badge. Replace CameraTrainer:783-797 with `<ConfidenceRing>` and both privacy chips with `<OnDeviceBadge>`. If any of the three primitives genuinely does not fit, delete it rather than leave a documented-but-dead API.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: `ConfidenceRing` is not a drop-in for CameraTrainer.tsx:783-797. That ring is the hold-to-confirm TIMER (it fills from `holdProgress` and centres a check icon); ConfidenceRing renders a live percent readout with role="progressbar". Substituting it would print a percentage where the design deliberately shows none, and would announce a bogus progressbar to screen readers. Either delete ConfidenceRing or point it at the real confidence meter (CameraTrainer.tsx:838-848), and leave the hold ring alone.

title: 295 hardcoded hex colours across src, 30 distinct values outside the palette
problem: Colour is written as literal hex in 295 places (208 of them in src/screens), spanning 43 distinct values of which 30 do not exist in tailwind.config.js at all. Home.tsx (44 inline `style={{…}}` blocks) and Progress.tsx (40) are the epicentres — both were built by transcribing .dc.html mockups literally rather than through tokens. Off-palette values include a whole undeclared teal ramp (#12817B, #148580, #3E9A93, #9DC6C2, #C9E0DC, #E6F0EE), an undeclared grey ramp (#8F9C99, #8FA09D, #94A5A2, #A9B8B5, #B8C4C1, #C7D0CE), and an undeclared tint set (#FBF3EF/#F5C9BE coral, #FBEFE6 gold) that duplicates what `bg-coral/10` and `bg-gold/10` already do.
userImpact: A brand change is no longer a token flip — it is a 295-site find-and-replace, and any site that is missed leaves a visibly off-brand patch. It is also how the contrast failures in this report got in: the greys were never checked against a scale because they were never named.
evidence: `grep -rhoE "#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}" src | wc -l` → 295; distinct → 43; 30 of those match no key in tailwind.config.js:9-26. Representative: src/screens/Home.tsx:181 `background: "#0F6E6A", boxShadow: "0 5px 0 #0A4F4C"`; :193 `background: "#F6EFE3", boxShadow: "0 4px 0 #D9CBB2"`; src/screens/Progress.tsx:542 `const shades = ["#EDE3D2", "#9DC6C2", "#3E9A93", "#0F6E6A"]`; src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:65-66 `{ backgroundColor: "#E6F0EE", color: "#0F6E6A" } : { backgroundColor: "#FBEFE6", color: "#C89A3D" }`.
proposedFix: Two passes. (1) Add the missing ramps as real tokens: `teal.100/.300/.500` for #E6F0EE/#9DC6C2/#3E9A93, `slate.300/.500` for the greys, and drop the tint hexes in favour of the existing `/10 /20` alpha mechanism. (2) Convert Home.tsx and Progress.tsx from inline `style` objects to Tailwind classes — those two files alone are 84 of the 105 inline style blocks in src.

title: An unnamed grey (#94A5A2, 2.4:1) is used for placeholder, dim and unearned text
problem: `text-[#94A5A2]` appears as an arbitrary Tailwind value in six places to mean "de-emphasised text". On sand/paper it measures ~2.4:1, well under the 4.5:1 AA floor. The palette already carries `muted` (#566B68) which was explicitly re-tuned in H15 to clear AA (tailwind.config.js:23-25), and AppNav.tsx:138 records that the sibling greys #B8C4C1/#8F9C99 were removed for exactly this reason — but these sites were missed.
userImpact: After answering a quiz question the three non-chosen answers become almost unreadable, so the learner cannot review what the wrong options were. The dictionary search field's placeholder is barely visible. On Progress, every not-yet-earned achievement label is a grey blur.
evidence: src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:605 and :666 `dim: "bg-sand text-[#94A5A2]"`, :672 `dim: "bg-ink/5 text-[#94A5A2]"`, :690 `state === "dim" ? "text-[#94A5A2]"`; src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:424 `placeholder:text-[#94A5A2]`; src/screens/Progress.tsx:657 `color: a.earned ? "#16302E" : "#94A5A2"` and :661 `text-[#94A5A2]`. Compare tailwind.config.js:23-25 which documents #5C726F being rejected at 4.49:1.
proposedFix: Replace all six `#94A5A2` occurrences with `text-muted`, and `border-[#94A5A2]/40` (LessonPlayer.tsx:626) with `border-muted/40`. If the dim state genuinely needs to sit below `muted`, add a `disabledText` token at a measured 4.5:1 rather than inventing a hex at the call site.

title: The "watch only" honesty badge on dictionary cards is 2.3:1
problem: `TypeBadge` renders the graded/motion disclosure with two inline colour pairs. The motion variant is `#C89A3D` on `#FBEFE6` = 2.28:1, at 9px uppercase with 0.04em tracking. tailwind.config.js:13-14 records this exact measurement ("#C89A3D on sand (#F6EFE3) was 2.26:1 for the 'HINT' label text") as the reason `gold.deep` was darkened — but this badge was not migrated.
userImpact: Every A1 word card in the dictionary carries a "watch & practise" badge that the learner cannot read. That badge is the disclosure that the sign has no camera grading, which is the honesty commitment the whole content story rests on. It reads as decorative noise instead.
evidence: src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:62-67 `className="...font-mono text-[9px] font-bold uppercase..."` with `style={ gradable ? { backgroundColor: "#E6F0EE", color: "#0F6E6A" } : { backgroundColor: "#FBEFE6", color: "#C89A3D" } }`. tailwind.config.js:13-15 documents the same colour failing at 2.26:1 and replacing it with #7F621F at 5.01:1.
proposedFix: Replace the inline style with the Pill primitive: `<Pill tone={gradable ? "teal" : "gold"}>` (src/components/dc.tsx:128-135 already gives `bg-gold/20 text-ink` at 12:1 and `bg-teal/10 text-teal`). Also raise the size off 9px — the smallest text elsewhere in the app is 10px.

title: Every Settings row's forward chevron is at 1.5:1
problem: The row chevron uses `text-[#C7D0CE]`, an arbitrary hex not in the palette. On paper (#FBF7EF) that is 1.47:1 — below the 3:1 floor for a meaningful non-text graphic. The same colour is used as a step separator arrow in InfoPages.
userImpact: Settings rows lose their "this goes somewhere" affordance; the list reads as static labels. On the privacy explainer the → arrows between the three flow steps are effectively missing, so the sequence does not read as a sequence.
evidence: src/screens/Settings.tsx:532 `className="text-[#C7D0CE] transition-transform group-hover:translate-x-1 ..."`; src/screens/InfoPages.tsx:146 `className="px-1 font-display text-base font-bold text-[#C7D0CE]"`.
proposedFix: Use `text-muted` (4.97:1) for both, or `text-teal/60` if a lighter affordance is wanted — either clears 3:1.

title: At least 15 distinct card treatments, with two contradictory elevation languages
problem: Two card components ship (ui.tsx `ScreenCard`, dc.tsx `Card`) and neither is the only one in use. Radii for the same "content card" concept run 32px (rounded-3xl), 24px (rounded-2xl), 22px, 20px, 18px, 16px, 15px and 14px. Worse, elevation is expressed two contradictory ways: `ScreenCard variant="elevated"` uses `shadow-soft` = `0 18px 40px -22px rgba(15,110,106,.45)`, a blurred floating drop shadow; every other raised card uses a hard, zero-blur `0 2px 0 #EDE3D2` paper edge. The hairline itself is drawn three ways — `border border-line`, `shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_#EDE3D2]` (10 sites) and inline `border: "1px solid #EDE3D2"`.
userImpact: Home's cards float above the page while Settings', Family's and Progress's cards sit flat on it. Scrolling from Learn to Progress feels like two different apps with different physics, which is a large part of "it doesn't make sense".
evidence: src/components/ui.tsx:117-121 (`elevated: "bg-paper border border-line shadow-soft"`, `rounded-3xl` at :145) vs src/components/dc.tsx:89 `const CARD_SHADOW = { boxShadow: "0 2px 0 #EDE3D2" }` + :102 `rounded-[20px]`. Further variants: src/screens/Progress.tsx:372 `rounded-[16px] border border-line bg-paper` no shadow, :162-163 `rounded-[18px]` + inline hard shadow, :830-833 `rounded-[16px]` + inline hard shadow, :729-730 `rounded-[15px]` + inline border; src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:483 `rounded-2xl border bg-white` + inline hard shadow, :257 `rounded-[20px]` no shadow; src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:56-57 `rounded-2xl` + `shadow-[0_2px_0_#EDE3D2]`; src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:602 `shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_#EDE3D2]`; src/screens/Words.tsx:201 `rounded-2xl border border-line` no shadow; src/screens/Home.tsx:608 `borderRadius: "26px 26px 0 0"`.
proposedFix:
Commit to the hard-edge language (it is what the .dc.html source and the majority of screens use): change `shadow-soft`'s definition to `0 2px 0 #EDE3D2` or retire `ScreenCard variant="elevated"` in favour of dc's `Card`. Set `Card` to a single radius token (`rounded-2xl`) and replace all eight arbitrary card radii with it. Ban the inset-shadow hairline — `border border-line` only.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Do not redefine `shadow-soft` globally. It is also consumed by FlagPicker.tsx and CameraTrainer.tsx, where a blurred lift over a dark/camera surface is deliberate; flattening the token to `0 2px 0 #EDE3D2` would make those read as unstyled. Retire `ScreenCard variant="elevated"` at the Home/LessonPlayer call sites instead and leave the token for the surfaces that want a float.

title: 24 arbitrary font sizes and 11 different page-title sizes across 15 screens
problem: `Title` exists and its docblock claims "one type ramp instead of per-screen ad-hoc sizes", but it is used in only 8 places. Screens set type with arbitrary Tailwind values instead: 24 distinct `text-[Npx]` values are in use (9, 10, 11, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 30, 32, 34, 56 px) alongside the standard scale. Page titles alone come in 11 sizes and 4 weights: `text-[21px]`, `[22px]`, `[24px]`, `text-2xl`, `[25px]`, `[26px]`, `[27px]`, `[28px]`, `text-3xl`, `[32px]`, `[34px]`, with `font-bold`, `font-extrabold`, `font-black` and an inline `fontWeight: 800`. Line-height is equally loose — 12 distinct arbitrary `leading-[…]` values.
userImpact: Moving between screens the heading size shifts by a point or two every time with no rhythm — Home's greeting is 21px, Family's title 25px, PractiseChooser's 26px, Onboarding's splash 34px, LessonPlayer's result 27px. Nothing signals hierarchy consistently, so the app reads as assembled rather than designed.
evidence: src/components/ui.tsx:265 `<As className={`font-display text-2xl font-bold leading-tight text-ink md:text-3xl ...`}>` with only 8 call sites. Ad-hoc titles: src/screens/Home.tsx:257 `style={{ fontWeight: 800, fontSize: 21 }}`, src/screens/FirstSign.tsx:258 `text-[21px]`, :240 `text-[22px]`, src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:409 `text-[24px]`, :260 `text-[34px]`, :276 `text-[32px]`, src/screens/Progress.tsx:295 `text-[25px]`, src/screens/PractiseChooser.tsx:51 `text-[26px]`, src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:816 `text-[27px]`, src/components/NoProfileFallback.tsx:37 `text-[28px]`, src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:663 `text-2xl font-black`.
proposedFix: Define a 6-step ramp in tailwind.config.js (`display-lg` 32, `display` 26, `title` 22, `body` 15, `caption` 13, `micro` 11) with matching line-heights, extend `Title` with a `level` prop that maps to it, and convert every `<h1>`/`<h2>` in src/screens to `<Title>`. Then sweep the remaining `text-[Npx]` values to the nearest ramp step.

title: Nine different focus-ring recipes, none matching the global base rule
problem: styles.css:14-16 sets a single global focus style (`ring-4 ring-gold/60 ring-offset-2 ring-offset-sand`), then almost every interactive element overrides it with its own. In use: `ring-2 ring-teal` (28), `ring-4 ring-gold/60` (12), `ring-2 ring-gold` (11), `ring-4 ring-teal/40` (8), `ring-4 ring-teal/30` (6), `ring-2 ring-coral/50` (2), `ring-4 ring-coral/30` (2), `ring-4 ring-teal/20` (1), plus `outline outline-2 outline-offset-2 outline-gold` (2). Offsets and offset-colours vary independently.
userImpact: A keyboard user tabbing through the app sees the focus indicator change colour and thickness on nearly every control, and some (the `/20` and `/30` alphas over a light card) are faint enough to lose track of where focus is.
evidence: src/styles.css:14-16 `:focus-visible { @apply outline-none ring-4 ring-gold/60 ring-offset-2 ring-offset-sand rounded-lg; }`; overridden at src/components/ui.tsx:108 (`ring-2 ring-teal ... ring-offset-paper`), :153 (`ring-2 ring-teal`), src/components/dc.tsx:80 (`ring-4 ring-gold/60 ... ring-offset-sand`), :111 (`ring-4 ring-gold/60`, no offset), src/components/Tile.tsx:30 (`ring-2 ring-teal`), src/screens/Settings.tsx:174 (`ring-4 ring-teal/40`), :240 (`ring-4 ring-gold/40`), :156 (`ring-4 ring-teal/20`), :521 (`ring-4 ring-teal/30`), src/screens/Progress.tsx:790 (`outline-2 outline-gold`).

VERIFIER CORRECTION: 'Delete every per-component ring and rely on the base rule' does not work as written. The base rule hardcodes `ring-offset-sand`, so every focused control on a paper card, on the teal Home app bar, or over the camera stage would draw a sand-coloured offset gap against the wrong background; and a gold/60 ring is invisible on the gold surfaces it would land on (PractiseChooser.tsx:93, Button `variant="gold"`, Onboarding.tsx:428). title: Six different progress-meter treatments for one concept
problem: The horizontal progress bar appears six times with no shared component. Track colours: `bg-ink/10`, `bg-teal/10`, `bg-line`, inline `#EDE3D2`, `bg-white/20`. Heights: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10px. title: Eight declared tokens and utilities have zero usages; two are exact aliases
problem: The token layer carries dead weight that makes it untrustworthy as documentation. Zero usages: `danger` (#C0492F), `teal.ink900` (#0A1F1D), `ease-enter`, `ease-exit`, `animate-shimmer` (plus its `shimmer` keyframe), `animate-confetti` (plus its `confetti` keyframe — Confetti.tsx uses a canvas instead), `.extruded-paper` and `.extruded-teal-pressed` in styles.css. title: font-mono is used 21 times but no mono font is defined or self-hosted
problem: `fontFamily` extends only `sans` (Readex Pro) and `display` (Rubik). `font-mono` therefore resolves to Tailwind's default `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, …` — a system stack that is not part of the brand and is not among the fonts vendored into public/fonts/. Yet `font-mono` is applied 21 times, including in the `MonoLabel` primitive whose docblock claims it renders "11px/700 uppercase mono (HANDOFF §Type · mono)" as if a mono token existed.
userImpact: Every eyebrow label, badge and section marker in the app renders in whatever monospace font the device happens to have — SF Mono on iPhone, Roboto Mono or Droid Sans Mono on Android, Consolas on Windows. Letterforms, weight and width change per device, so the brand's small-caps labels look different on every phone and undercut the fully-offline self-hosted-fonts promise in fonts.css:1-7.
evidence: tailwind.config.js:35-39 defines only `sans` and `display`; src/fonts.css vendors only Readex Pro, Rubik and Material Symbols. `font-mono` at src/components/dc.tsx:177 (MonoLabel), src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:62, :625, src/screens/Fingerspell.tsx:144, :279, :308, src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:338, :353, :848, src/screens/Progress.tsx:566, src/screens/Words.tsx:57, :143, src/screens/InfoPages.tsx:206, src/screens/Family.tsx:104, src/components/SignDemo.tsx:124, src/components/CameraTrainer.tsx:435, :454, :480, :568, :704, :749.
proposedFix: Either vendor one mono face (e.g. the same subsetting treatment used for Material Symbols) and add `mono: ["<Face>", "ui-monospace", "monospace"]` to tailwind.config.js, or — simpler and consistent with the rest of the brand — drop `font-mono` entirely and let these labels use `font-display` (Rubik) with the existing uppercase + tracking treatment, which is already how `Eyebrow` (src/components/ui.tsx:277) renders the same idea.

title: Back buttons and the Arabic keypad fall below the documented 44px hit target
problem: The design contract states SpringButton has a "≥44px hit target" (DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:118) and `ui.tsx`'s size scale floors at `min-h-[40px]`, but hand-rolled controls ignore both. There are three different back-button sizes — 34px in Words and Fingerspell, 40px in the shared ScreenShell header — and the on-screen Arabic keypad's 29 letter keys are 40×40px.
userImpact: On the Words and Fingerspell screens the back arrow is a 34px target, noticeably harder to hit with a thumb than the identical-looking 40px back arrow on Settings, Progress and the lesson player. The Arabic keypad's 40px keys with a 6px gutter make mistyping likely when spelling a name.
evidence: src/screens/Words.tsx:85 `className="flex h-[34px] w-[34px] shrink-0 ... rounded-full bg-sand"`; src/screens/Fingerspell.tsx:132 same 34px; src/components/ScreenShell.tsx:57 `className="flex h-10 w-10 ... rounded-full text-teal"` (40px); src/screens/Fingerspell.tsx:168 `className="flex h-10 w-10 ... rounded-xl bg-paper"` for each keypad key. Compare src/components/dc.tsx:41-43 `min-h-[44px]`/`min-h-[48px]`.
proposedFix:
Extract the circular back button into one component (or just use ScreenShell's takeover header on Words and Fingerspell — both currently hand-roll a header inside `chrome="tabs"`), sized `h-11 w-11` (44px). Raise the keypad keys to `h-11 w-11` and let them wrap to fewer per row.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Leave the keypad alone. 40x40 keys with a 6px gutter are in line with system Arabic keyboards, they already exceed the AA floor, and raising 29 keys to 44px forces fewer per row and pushes the letter pad and the spelled-word strip below the fold on a small phone — a worse trade than the mis-tap it prevents. Unifying the two 34px back buttons to the shared 40px ScreenShell header is the whole fix.
