title: Dictionary detail's Watch / play / "Watch & practise" buttons do nothing — for the 19 word signs it is the only action on the screen
problem: `handleWatch` only calls `setWatched(true)`, and `watched` is used for nothing except swapping the button label from "Watch" to "Watch Again". Three separate controls are wired to it: the centred Watch chip, the gold play FAB, and — for non-gradable signs — the primary "Watch & practise" CTA. The detail panel never mounts `SignDemo`; it renders a static `SignGlyph` medallion which, for 18 of the 19 A1 words, is the same generic `sign_language` icon.
userImpact: Tapping any word in the Dictionary opens a panel whose big gold primary button, centred Watch chip, and play button all visibly do nothing. There is nothing to watch and no way forward — the screen is a dead end, and the only difference after a tap is that the label now says "Watch Again". The Words screen (Words.tsx:133) shows the same signs correctly via `SignDemo`, so two screens for the same content behave completely differently.
evidence: AllSigns.tsx:544 `const [watched, setWatched] = useState(false)`; :568 `const handleWatch = () => setWatched(true);`; :641 and :651 both `onClick={handleWatch}`; :724 `<SpringButton variant="gold" ... onClick={handleWatch}>{t("signWatchPractise")}` is the ONLY CTA in the `!sign.cameraGradable` branch. `watched` appears nowhere else (grep confirms lines 544/568/641/645/651/652/724 only). AllSigns imports SignGlyph, never SignDemo (:20). SignGlyph.tsx:62 returns `<Icon name="sign_language"/>` for every word sign.
proposedFix:
Replace the medallion + Watch controls in `DetailPanel` with `<SignDemo sign={sign} lang={lang}/>` (the same component Words.tsx and LessonPlayer's WatchDrill use) — it already carries the replay chip, the honest instruction stage for footage-less words, and the provenance footnote. Then make the non-gradable primary CTA do something real: record a watch drill (`recordDrillResult(id, "good", { watch: true })`) plus a self-mark, matching Words.tsx:41-48.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Dropping SignDemo in also requires gating the panel's own hint block (AllSigns.tsx:690-711) behind `!demoShowsHint(sign)` — Words.tsx:136 does exactly this — or the hint prints twice, once inside SignDemo's instruction stage and once below it. The A1 provenance note at AllSigns.tsx:706-710 would also duplicate SignDemo.tsx:206-214. The second half of the fix is wrong: `recordDrillResult(id, "good", { watch: true })` is not what Words does and would not work — app.ts:371 skips SRS rating entirely when `opts.watch`, and app.ts:388-389 caps mastery at 1 for watch drills. Words.tsx:44 uses `recordDrillResult(id, "hard", { selfMark: true })`; match that.

title: Routing a non-gradable sign to the camera drops it into teach-mode, then grades it against the learner's own guess and can mint mastery 3
problem: `CameraTrainer` opens in `teach` mode whenever the MLP does not know the sign and the learner has no samples. Two screens still route non-gradable signs there: Progress's Coming Up rows and Constellation (`onSign` / `onTap` → `go({name:"camera", targetSignId: id})`), and CameraPractice's letter strip, which renders all 31 ALPHABET entries including the three `cameraGradable: false` edge forms (ة، لا، ال). The learner then records 24 samples of a handshape they do not know, and the KNN grades them against those samples — a guaranteed match, which flows through `recordDrillResult({camera:true, matched:true})` and increments `cameraHits`.
userImpact: A learner who self-marks "milk" in the Words hub sees it come due in Progress, taps it, and is asked to teach the camera a sign the app itself says has no verified reference. The camera then congratulates them for copying their own guess, awards a real match, and can push the sign to mastery 3 — which feeds "signs planted", the milestone ladder, the Family honeycomb and the Stats accuracy tile with a fabricated success. Home, Family, FlagPicker and the Dictionary all correctly gate this (they route non-gradable signs to `allSigns`); Progress and the letter strip do not.
evidence: CameraTrainer.tsx:75-78 `const knowsModel = modelKnows(sign.id); const [mode] = useState(knowsModel || isTrained(sign.id) ? "grade" : "teach")`. classifier.ts:44 `modelKnows` only returns true for the 28 seeded letters; knn.ts:177 `isTrained` is false with no samples. Ungated routes: Progress.tsx:208 `onSign={(id) => go({name:"camera", targetSignId: id})}` used at :500 (due rows) and :515 (upcoming) and :445/788 (Constellation, which iterates all 31 ALPHABET entries). CameraPractice.tsx:129 `ALPHABET.map(...)` includes the edge forms (signs.ts:67-69 `cameraGradable: !edge`). Gated correctly elsewhere: Home.tsx:432-436, Family.tsx:73-76, FlagPicker.tsx:324-328, AllSigns.tsx:716. Mastery 3 path: app.ts:382-393 `cameraHits + (opts.camera && opts.matched ? 1 : 0)` … `cameraHits >= 2` → `mastery = 3`.
proposedFix:
Apply the existing H5 gate in the two remaining places. In Progress.tsx:208 change `onSign` to `(id) => { const s = signById(id); s?.cameraGradable ? go({name:"camera", targetSignId:id}) : go({name:"allSigns", signId:id}); }`. In CameraPractice.tsx:129 filter the strip to `ALPHABET.filter(s => s.cameraGradable)` (or render the edge forms as non-selectable reference chips). Separately, harden CameraTrainer: when `!sign.cameraGradable`, never enter teach mode — render the watch/self-mark path only.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The edge-letter half is milder than stated: ة/لا/ال do carry a real signer photo (signs.ts:34) shown as the reference chip (CameraTrainer.tsx:398), so the learner is copying a reference, not purely their own guess. The A1-word route through Progress has no reference at all and is the serious one. Also note filtering the CameraPractice strip to gradable letters removes the edge forms from the only screen that displays them — render them as non-selectable reference chips rather than deleting them, or the dictionary becomes the sole place they exist.

title: Flagging signs does nothing visible for a single-profile household — the default state after onboarding
problem: `toggleFlag` seeds a due-now SRS card into every profile EXCEPT the raiser, and both Home and the nav badge filter out flags the current profile raised. Onboarding creates exactly one profile, so in the default household the person flagging is always the only person there.
userImpact: A solo learner opens Family → "Flag signs we need", is told "Flag the signs your family needs — everyone's queue follows", taps several signs, sees "3 signs flagged for your family" and taps Done. Home shows no flagged section, the profile badge shows no count, and their review queue is unchanged. The one screen the app frames as its structural centrepiece produces no observable effect for the majority first-run case.
evidence: app.ts:554-560 `if (!alreadyDone) { for (const p of s.profiles) { if (p.id === byProfileId) continue; ... srs[p.id] = {...} } }` — the raiser never gets a card. Home.tsx:103-105 `pinnedFlagSigns(app, profile.id).filter((f) => f.raisedByProfileId !== profile.id)`. AppNav.tsx:60-62 applies the identical filter for the badge count. Onboarding.tsx:130-137 creates a single profile; Family.tsx:117 handles `app.profiles.length === 1`. FlagPicker.tsx:146-149 renders the "everyone's queue follows" promise unconditionally.
proposedFix:
In `toggleFlag`, seed the raiser's own SRS card too when the household has no other hearing member (`s.profiles.filter(p => p.role !== "deaf").length <= 1`), so a solo learner's own queue actually follows their flags. Then either drop the `raisedByProfileId !== profile.id` filter on Home/AppNav for solo households, or gate the FlagPicker entry point behind `app.profiles.length > 1` and show the "add a family member first" empty state that Progress's LeagueTab already has (Progress.tsx:704-719).

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The impact statement overstates it — the effect is not unobservable. Family.tsx:253-266 lists self-raised flags with the byline "You flagged it — for your family" (:263), and FlagPicker's own summary rail shows them. The real defect is narrower: the queue promise is false and the two review surfaces (Home, nav badge) hide them. Gating the FlagPicker entry behind `profiles.length > 1` would be wrong — it is also the solo learner's only way to build a personal list; seed the raiser's own card instead.

title: "Free camera · Sign anything" and "Alphabet" open the exact same screen, pre-targeted on Alif
problem: Tile 3 calls `go({name:"camera"})` with no target. `CameraPractice` defaults `signId` to `"alpha-alif"`, so it renders identically to tile 1, which explicitly passes `targetSignId: "alpha-alif"`. There is no free-signing mode anywhere in the app.
userImpact: Half of the Practise hub's four tiles land on the same screen. A learner who taps "Free camera — sign anything" gets "Sign: ا" with the alphabet strip and the Alif reference photo, exactly what the Alphabet tile gave them. The hub reads as broken and the promise "sign anything" is not something the app can do — the model only knows 28 letters.
evidence: PractiseChooser.tsx:62 `onClick={() => go({ name: "camera", targetSignId: "alpha-alif" })}` vs :92 `onClick={() => go({ name: "camera" })}`. CameraPractice.tsx:30 `const [signId, setSignId] = useState(initialSignId ?? "alpha-alif")`. App.tsx:152-159 passes `initialSignId={screen.targetSignId}` — the only difference is the React `key`, which changes nothing visible. i18n.ts:305-306 `practiseFreeCamera: "Free camera" / practiseFreeCameraSub: "Sign anything"`.
proposedFix:
Either remove tile 3 and let the hub be three honest destinations, or give it a real distinct behaviour: open CameraPractice with a `free` flag that shows the live MLP's top prediction across all 28 letters (`classify(vec)` from classifier.ts:68 already returns the global argmax) instead of grading against one target — that is a genuine "sign anything" mode and reuses existing code.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: `classify()` (classifier.ts:68) alone is not a safe basis for a "sign anything" mode: it is a bare softmax argmax and will confidently name a letter for any random hand. gradeWithModel (:104-110) deliberately adds the OOD conjunct (`nearestSeedDistance` vs `OOD_GATE`, M1) for that exact reason. A free mode must reuse that gate and show "not a letter I know" below it, or it fabricates recognition — the failure mode this codebase repeatedly guards against. Removing the tile is the safer option.

title: Home's unit banner claims "Unit 1 · The Arabic Alphabet" but the trail below it renders all 8 lessons, four of which are Unit 2
problem: `unitIdx` is derived from the current lesson only, then the banner renders one unit title. But `pathNodes` is built from the whole `LESSONS` array — four alphabet lessons and four A1 word lessons — with no unit grouping or separator.
userImpact: On first run the learner sees a teal banner reading "UNIT 1 / The Arabic Alphabet" and, directly beneath it, eight nodes titled "Alif to Kha", "Dal to Sad", "Dad to Qaf", "Kaf to Ya", "First connections", "Everyday needs", "Home & people", "People around you". The last four are the word unit filed under the alphabet heading, so the path's structure reads as arbitrary. Tapping a word node also shows "New sign · camera-graded" (pathNewSign) even though no A1 word is camera-gradable.
evidence: Home.tsx:117-119 `const unitIdx = Math.max(0, UNITS.findIndex((u) => u.id === nextLesson.unitId)); const unit = UNITS[unitIdx];` then :294-306 renders one banner. Home.tsx:108-129 `const nodes = LESSONS.map(...)` over all of signs.ts:202-236 (8 lessons across `alpha-u1` and `a1-u1`). signs.ts:189 `UNITS = [UNIT_ALPHA, UNIT_A1_U1]`. Home.tsx:570 `st === "current" ? t("pathNewSign", lang)` and i18n.ts:222 `pathNewSign: "New sign · camera-graded"`.
proposedFix: Group `pathNodes` by `lesson.unitId` and emit a banner per group, so the trail reads Unit 1 → 4 alphabet nodes → Unit 2 → 4 word nodes → milestone. Also make the sheet meta unit-aware: use a watch-and-copy string instead of `pathNewSign` when the lesson has no `cameraGradable` sign (Home.tsx:38 `lessonCameraTarget` already computes that).

title: The alphabet is counted as 28 or 31 depending on the screen, and two counters can read past their own denominator
problem: ALPHABET holds 31 signs (28 seeded + 3 reference-only edge forms). AllSigns' alphabet grid renders all 31 but divides by 28 and captions "of 28 learned"; Progress's achievement divides a 31-capable numerator by 28; Progress's Constellation divides by 31; PractiseChooser filters to the gradable 28. Nothing agrees.
userImpact: A learner who practises the edge forms (reachable from the CameraPractice strip and the Constellation) sees "30 of 28 learned" under a progress bar clamped at 100%, an achievement reading "31 / 28", and a Constellation reading "31 / 31" — three contradictory statements about the same thing on two screens. "Whole alphabet" can also unlock with only 28 of the 31 shown cells lit, or before all 28 real letters are done.
evidence: AllSigns.tsx:149 `alphaSigns = ALL_SIGNS.filter(s => s.tier === "alphabet")` (31); :150 `alphaLearned` over that set; :152 `alphaPct = Math.min(100, Math.round((alphaLearned / 28) * 100))`; :299 renders `alphaLearned` next to i18n.ts:364 `signsAlphaProgress: "of 28 learned"`; the section heading is i18n.ts:363 `signsAlphaBody: "All 28 Arabic letters."` above a 31-cell grid (:301-315). Progress.tsx:79-82 `alphaTaught` over all 31; :618-619 `${alphaTaught} / 28` with `earned: alphaTaught >= 28`; :778 Constellation shows `alphaTaught / ALPHABET.length` (31). PractiseChooser.tsx:43-45 filters `s.cameraGradable` (28). signs.ts:38-70 defines 31 entries, 3 with `edge = true`.
proposedFix: Pick one denominator and one numerator. Recommend: everywhere the alphabet is counted as progress, restrict to the 28 seeded letters — `ALPHABET.filter(s => s.cameraGradable)` — matching PractiseChooser and milestones.ts:25-27, which already do this deliberately. Export a `SEEDED_ALPHABET` const from signs.ts (it exists privately at signs.ts:169) and use it in AllSigns.tsx:149-152, Progress.tsx:79-82 and Progress.tsx:778. Show the 3 edge forms in the grid as a separate labelled "reference only" row that does not count.

title: Back buttons on Words, Fingerspell and CameraPractice go to fixed screens, not where the user came from
problem: The UI router (`store/ui.ts`) keeps no history stack, so every back affordance hard-codes a destination. Words always returns to PractiseChooser, Fingerspell and CameraPractice always return to Home — but all three are reachable from both the Practise tab and from Home cards.
userImpact: From the Practise tab a learner taps Fingerspell, then back — and lands on the Learn tab, having silently changed tabs. From Home they tap "Everyday words", then back — and land on the Practise hub, a screen they have never seen. The back arrow is unpredictable, which on a tabbed app reads as the navigation being broken.
evidence: Fingerspell.tsx:130 `onClick={() => go({ name: "home" })}`; CameraPractice.tsx:107 `onClick={() => go({ name: "home" })}`; Words.tsx:83 `onClick={() => go({ name: "practiseChooser" })}`. All three are reachable from PractiseChooser.tsx:80/92/103 AND from Home.tsx:353/369/385. store/ui.ts:26-32 `go` just does `set({screen})` — no previous-screen tracking.
proposedFix: Add a one-slot `prev` to the ui store: `go: (screen) => set((s) => ({ screen, prev: s.screen }))`, plus a `back()` that returns to `prev` (falling back to `home`). Point the three back buttons at `back()`. Cheap, and it makes every takeover screen's close behave correctly too.

title: The app never touches browser history, so the Android system back button exits it from every screen
problem: The router is a plain Zustand atom with no `pushState`/`popstate` wiring anywhere in the codebase. The manifest ships `display: "standalone"`, so on Android the system back gesture is the primary back affordance for an installed PWA.
userImpact: A learner mid-lesson, mid-camera-drill, or deep in Settings who uses the phone's back gesture is thrown out of the app entirely rather than back one screen. Any unsaved drill position is gone. On desktop, browser Back leaves the app too.
evidence: store/ui.ts:26-32 is the whole router; `grep -rn "pushState|popstate|replaceState" src/` matches only Onboarding.test.tsx:23,30. vite.config.ts:52 `display: "standalone"`. No hashchange handler either.
proposedFix: In the ui store's `go`, call `window.history.pushState({ screen }, "")`, and register a single `popstate` listener at app init that sets `screen` from `event.state?.screen ?? { name: "home" }`. Ten lines, no routing library, and GH-Pages-safe because it never changes the path.

title: The Progress oasis promises a world that grows with your signs, but the scene is hard-coded and never changes
problem: The Oasis tab's headline and body say "The world you're building / Every sign you learn plants something new", and the two tiles beneath count "signs planted" and "palms grown". The scene above them is a fixed illustration: exactly two palms, one sprout, one pool, `aria-hidden`, with nothing bound to `mastered` or `alphaTaught`.
userImpact: This is the default tab of the app's reward screen. A learner at 0 signs and a learner at 20 signs see byte-identical artwork. The "7 palms grown" tile sits directly under a picture containing two palms. The screen's entire premise — the thing it names itself after — is not delivered.
evidence: Progress.tsx:295-296 renders `prOasisTitle`/`prOasisBody` (i18n.ts:315-316 "The world you're building" / "Every sign you learn plants something new."). Progress.tsx:299-368 is the scene: `aria-hidden="true"`, one sun, one sand mound, one pool, palm 1 (:335-346), palm 2 (:347-358), one sprout (:359-363), Fanan (:364-367) — no reference to any progress value. Progress.tsx:372-381 renders the `mastered` and `alphaTaught` tiles labelled i18n.ts:317-318 `prPlanted: "signs planted"` / `prPalmsGrown: "palms grown"`.
proposedFix: Bind the scene to the numbers already in scope. Render `Math.min(6, alphaTaught)` palms by mapping over an array instead of two hard-coded blocks, and `Math.min(8, mastered)` sprouts, with a small deterministic x/scale offset per index. That is a ~20-line change to the existing markup and makes the tiles true.

title: The streak celebration tells you that you are going to be proud of yourself
problem: The motivational band interpolates `profile.displayName` — the active learner's own name — into a sentence whose subject was clearly meant to be the Deaf family member. The Arabic branch also hard-codes the masculine `فخوراً`, and the English and Arabic strings are split around the name differently.
userImpact: On the full-screen celebration a learner named Aisha reads: "You've mastered 5 signs so far. Aisha is going to be so proud." It is the app's most emotionally loaded screen and the copy is nonsense — and the household has no field naming the person being learned for, so there is no name to substitute.
evidence: Progress.tsx:966-974 `{pick(lang, `You've mastered ${mastered} signs so far. `, ...)}<bdi>{profile.displayName}</bdi>{pick(lang, " is going to be so proud.", " فخوراً جداً بك.")}` where `profile` is the active profile (Progress.tsx:65 `activeProfile(app)`, passed at :237). The same screen already greets the learner as "you" at :931-933 (`${n} days of showing up for ` + displayName), which is also second-person-then-name.
proposedFix: Drop the name. Use a name-free line: EN "You've mastered N signs so far. That's N more ways to be understood." / AR equivalent, and add both to i18n.ts rather than inlining bilingual literals. If a "who you're learning for" name is wanted later, add an optional `learningForName` to Profile in Onboarding's persona step and interpolate that instead.

title: "Which hand do you sign with?" is asked in onboarding and toggled in Settings, but nothing in the app reads it
problem: `dominantHand` is written by Onboarding and Settings and normalised on rehydrate, but is never read outside those two write sites. The recognizer canonicalises handedness per-frame from MediaPipe's own `detectedHand`, so the stored preference is inert.
userImpact: A left-handed learner is given a dedicated onboarding step promising "So the camera reads your hands fairly", picks Left, and nothing changes — not the reference photos, not the grading, not the mirroring. In Settings the same control sits under Preferences with a selected-state check mark that means nothing. It is a whole onboarding step and a Settings card that are pure theatre.
evidence: `grep -rn dominantHand src/` (excluding tests) returns only: types.ts:14, Settings.tsx:69/191/196, Family.tsx:93, Onboarding.tsx:133, app.ts:67/235/323/331 — all declarations, writes, or normalisation. The recognizer derives handedness itself: CameraTrainer.tsx:179 `const mirror = frame.detectedHand === "Left"` → normalize.ts. i18n.ts:27-28 `obHandTitle: "Which hand do you sign with?" / obHandSub: "So the camera reads your hands fairly."`.
proposedFix: Either use it or cut it. Cheapest honest fix: delete the `hand` step from Onboarding's `STEP_ORDER` (Onboarding.tsx:150-161) and the `HandCards` block from Settings (Settings.tsx:185-222, :282-287), keeping the field for future use. If it should be real, feed `profile.dominantHand` into CameraTrainer as a tie-break when MediaPipe's handedness is low-confidence, and mirror the reference photo to match.

title: "Add to Daily Review" is desktop-only and Share is mobile-only in the Dictionary detail
problem: The one shared `DetailPanel` renders its action row twice with opposite visibility classes: the Add-to-Daily-Review button is `hidden md:inline-flex`, the Flag+Share row is `md:hidden`, and the favourite/heart in the header is `hidden md:flex`.
userImpact: On a phone — the app's primary form factor — there is no way to add a sign to daily review from the Dictionary at all, even though `addToReview` is wired and imported. On desktop there is no Share. The same screen offers different capabilities depending on window width, with no indication either exists.
evidence: AllSigns.tsx:736-745 `<SpringButton ... onClick={onAddReview} className="hidden gap-2 md:inline-flex">`; :748 `<div className="flex gap-3 md:hidden">` containing the Flag button and the Share button; :599 header favourite `className="hidden ... md:flex"`. `addToReview` is a real store action (app.ts:476-488) reachable nowhere else in the app.
proposedFix: Collapse to one action stack shown at every width: primary CTA (camera or watch), then a row of Flag / Add to Daily Review / Share. Remove the `hidden`/`md:hidden` pairs at AllSigns.tsx:599, :741 and :748 and let the row wrap.

title: "Which sign means…" for word signs shows four identical generic hand icons
problem: `ChoiceTile` renders `SignGlyph` as the answer face. For A1 word signs SignGlyph falls through every branch to a single generic `sign_language` Material icon, so every word choice in a recall drill draws the same picture. Only the truncated 38-character hint distinguishes them.
userImpact: In a word lesson or a review session the learner is shown a meaning and asked "Which sign means…" over four tiles that are visually identical. The drill's whole premise — recognise the sign — is impossible; the learner is reduced to speed-reading four clipped sentences. It reads as a rendering bug.
evidence: LessonPlayer.tsx:519-531 `<ChoiceTile ... sign={choice} hint={choice.type === "alphabet" ? undefined : pick(lang, choice.hintEn, choice.hintAr)}/>`; :685-687 `<SignGlyph sign={sign} .../>`. SignGlyph.tsx:32-62: `sign.photo` (words have none), `id === "iloveyou"`, `type === "alphabet"` — else `<Icon name="sign_language"/>`. signs.ts:94-158: 18 of 19 A1 signs have no `photo`, no `media`, and `type` static/dynamic. Recall drills are generated for non-gradable signs at engine.ts:62, :71-73 and :153.
proposedFix:
Until real footage lands, make word tiles legible without a picture: render the sign's `emoji` as a labelled meaning cue plus the full (untruncated) hint, and drop the generic hand icon entirely for signs where `SignGlyph` would return the fallback. Words.tsx:208-210 already does exactly this and marks the emoji `aria-hidden` as a meaning cue, so reuse that treatment.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: One tile in a word drill can still differ: `iloveyou` renders the stitch-34 brand image (SignGlyph.tsx:41-43), so the set is not always four identical faces. That does not change the fix, but note stitch-34 is a relative path and would need to survive whatever treatment replaces the glyph.

title: The treasure-chest node's sheet says "Clear Unit 1" no matter which milestone it represents, and every locked node announces itself as camera practice
problem: The milestone node's title is the live `nextMilestone` label, but its sheet body is a fixed string about Unit 1. Separately, every path node — locked, done and milestone alike — carries `aria-label={node.title + " — " + practiceCamera}`, and the milestone/locked sheet button is a disabled "Locked" with no route forward.
userImpact: A learner whose next milestone is "5 signs your whole family can do" taps the chest and is told "Clear Unit 1 to open the reward chest" — two unrelated goals in one sheet. Screen-reader users hear "Kaf to Ya — Practise on camera" on a node that opens a disabled Locked button. Tapping the chest or any locked node is a guaranteed dead end.
evidence: Home.tsx:131 `pathNodes.push({ id: "__milestone", status: "milestone", title: ms.label, ... })` where `ms` comes from milestones.ts:35-52 (six possible labels). Home.tsx:573 `st === "milestone" ? t("pathChestMeta", lang)` and i18n.ts:225 `pathChestMeta: "Clear Unit 1 to open the reward chest."`. Home.tsx:326 `aria-label={`${node.title} — ${t("practiceCamera", lang)}`}` applied to every node. Home.tsx:567 `const locked = st === "locked" || st === "milestone"` → :634 `disabled={locked}` with :576 `btnLabel = ... t("pathLocked")`.
proposedFix: Make the chest sheet describe its own milestone: pass `ms.progress` through and render "{done} of {target} — {ms.label}" instead of the fixed key. Give `aria-label` a per-status suffix (`pathLocked` / `pathDoneMeta` / `practiceCamera`). For the milestone node, replace the disabled button with a live route to whatever advances that milestone (camera for the alphabet rungs, `family` for the family rungs) so it is never a dead tap.

title: The "Arabic Alphabet · Ready" onboarding card finishes setup instantly, so the profile is named "Me" and roled "parent"
problem: Tapping the first learning-path card calls `finish()` with a camera destination but no `skipAll`, four steps before the name step. `displayName` falls back to "Me"/"أنا", `persona` stays at its `useState` default of `"parent"`, and `goal` at `"regular"` — none of which the learner chose.
userImpact: The most prominent, most obviously-correct card on the onboarding path ("Arabic Alphabet — READY — 28 core letters, camera-graded") permanently names the learner "Me". Home then greets "Marhaba, Me" with an "M" avatar, the Family screen lists a member called Me with role Parent, and the Progress league ranks "Me". Nothing in the flow tells them a name was skipped or where to change it.
evidence: Onboarding.tsx:335-339 `onClick={() => finish({ destination: { name: "camera", targetSignId: "alpha-alif", autoStart: true } })}` — no `skipAll`, so :132-135 use `persona` (default `"parent"`, set at :117), `hand` and `goal`. :129 `const displayName = name.trim() || (lang === "ar" ? "أنا" : "Me")` and `name` is still `""` (:120) because the `name` step (:630) has not run. Home.tsx:258-259 renders `Marhaba, ` + displayName; :140 `const initial = profile.displayName.trim().charAt(0)`.
proposedFix: Route the Alphabet card to the `name` step with the destination stashed, e.g. `setPendingDestination({name:"camera", targetSignId:"alpha-alif", autoStart:true}); setStep("name")`, and have the name form's `finish()` use it. One extra screen preserves the practice-first intent while keeping the learner's name. Same treatment for the header Skip at :241.

title: Every flagged-sign row and the "Practise these" CTA show a camera icon but always open the dictionary
problem: FlagPicker only lists `A1_SIGNS`, and every A1 sign is `cameraGradable: false`. So `firstFlaggedGradable` is always `undefined` and both the row handler and the CTA always take the `allSigns` branch — while both render a `videocam` icon.
userImpact: The learner flags signs, sees a coral "Practise these" button with a camera glyph and rows each ending in a camera glyph, taps one expecting the camera, and lands on a Dictionary detail page whose own primary button does nothing (see the Watch no-op finding). Two mislabelled controls in a row leading to a dead screen.
evidence: FlagPicker.tsx:82 `A1_SIGNS.filter(...)` is the only source of taggable signs; signs.ts:94-158 sets `cameraGradable: false` on all 19. FlagPicker.tsx:111 `const firstFlaggedGradable = flaggedSigns.find((s) => s.cameraGradable)?.id` → undefined; :390-393 falls to `go({ name: "allSigns", signId: flaggedSigns[0]?.id })` while :397 renders `<Icon name="videocam" />`. Row: :324-328 same gate, :336 `<Icon name="videocam" className="text-xl text-coral" />`.
proposedFix:
Swap the icon per branch — `videocam` when `s.cameraGradable`, `visibility` otherwise — at FlagPicker.tsx:336 and :397, and change the CTA label to "Watch these" when nothing flagged is gradable. Better still, let the picker offer alphabet signs too (`ALL_SIGNS` with a group for letters), which would make the camera branch reachable at all.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: "`firstFlaggedGradable` is always undefined" is not accurate and should not go in the report as stated. FlagPicker.tsx:100-103 resolves flags through `signById` specifically so flagged ALPHABET signs resolve (the #M3 comment says so), and AllSigns' DetailPanel lets any sign be flagged, including the 28 gradable letters. So the camera branch is reachable; the defect is that the icon is drawn before the branch is known, not that the branch is dead.

title: The Dictionary tags every word sign "Unit 1" while the app's own unit list puts words in Unit 2
problem: `categoryTags` hard-codes "Unit 1 / الوحدة ١" for every non-alphabet sign, and `STATUS_META.unit` uses the same string as a status caption. But `UNITS = [UNIT_ALPHA, UNIT_A1_U1]`, and Home numbers units by index+1, so the alphabet is Unit 1 and the words are Unit 2.
userImpact: A word card in the Dictionary shows the caption "UNIT 1" and its detail panel shows an "ALPHABET"-coloured "Unit 1" chip, while Home's banner calls Unit 1 "The Arabic Alphabet". The same 19 signs belong to two different units depending on which screen you are on.
evidence: AllSigns.tsx:42-48 `if (sign.tier === "alphabet") tags.push({label: "Alphabet"}) else tags.push({label: pick(lang, "Unit 1", "الوحدة ١")})`; :36 `unit: { en: "Unit 1", ar: "الوحدة ١", ... }`; :113 `return sign.tier === "A1" ? "unit" : "new"`. signs.ts:189 `UNITS = [UNIT_ALPHA, UNIT_A1_U1]` with UNIT_A1_U1 titled "Family & First Words" (:179-185). Home.tsx:297 renders `Unit ${unitIdx + 1}`.
proposedFix: Derive the label instead of hard-coding it: look the sign up via `UNITS.find(u => u.signIds.includes(sign.id))` and render `Unit ${index + 1}` plus the unit's own title. Same for `STATUS_META.unit` — or rename that status to something unit-free like "In progress", since it is really a mastery state, not a unit.

title: Home calls the profile's XP "gold"; every other screen calls the same number XP
problem: The Home app-bar's second stat chip renders `profile.xp` under the label `homeGoldStat` ("gold"). Progress, the lesson results card and the family league render the identical value labelled `xp` ("XP").
userImpact: A learner sees "120 gold" on Home and "120 XP" on Progress and at the end of every lesson, with no gold currency anywhere in the app — nothing is bought, earned or spent as gold. It reads as two separate broken counters that happen to match.
evidence: Home.tsx:155-157 `value: num(profile.xp, lang), label: t("homeGoldStat", lang)` and i18n.ts:216 `homeGoldStat: { en: "gold", ar: "ذهب" }`. Same value as `xp` at Progress.tsx:411 `{num(xp, lang)} {t("xp", lang)}`, Progress.tsx:750 (league), LessonPlayer.tsx:836 `t("lsXpEarned")`, Home.tsx:138 `t("xp", lang)` in the goal label — i18n.ts:158 `xp: { en: "XP", ar: "نقطة" }`.
proposedFix: Change `homeGoldStat` to the `xp` label (or rename the key's value to "XP"/"نقطة") so one number has one name across the app. If a gold currency is genuinely planned, it needs its own store field, not a second label on `profile.xp`.

title: "Lesson complete!" fires on a lesson that did not complete — the path node never changes
problem: buildAlphabetQueue and buildDrillQueue both hard-cap the queue at MAX_DRILLS = 12 by dropping non-watch drills from the END. A 7-sign lesson generates 17 drills (7 watch + 7 camera + 3 checkpoints), so the trim removes the 3 checkpoints and the last 2 camera drills — the final two letters get a watch and nothing else. Watch drills can only reach masteryLevel 1 (store/app.ts:388-393), but Home marks a node `done` only when every sign is >= 2 (Home.tsx:109). LessonPlayer still calls recordLessonComplete() + celebrate() and renders the "Lesson complete!" results card the moment the truncated queue runs out (LessonPlayer.tsx:109-114).
userImpact: A brand-new user finishes their very first real lesson (Alif→Kha), gets confetti, "Lesson complete!", XP and a list of all 7 letters they supposedly learned — then lands back on Home and the node is still the pulsing coral "START" circle, every later node still padlocked, the unit banner unchanged. Nothing they did registered. This hits all four alphabet lessons (the entire primary path) and the 7-sign word lesson a1-u1-l3, i.e. 5 of 8 lessons.
evidence: engine.ts:122-124 `for (let i = queue.length - 1; queue.length > MAX_DRILLS && i >= 0; i--) { if (queue[i].type !== "watch") queue.splice(i, 1); }` — simulating 7 signs: indices 16,15,14 (recognise), 13 (camera #7), 11 (camera #6) are spliced, leaving 7 watch + 5 camera. engine.ts:84-88 does the same in the word path via `rest.slice(0, MAX_DRILLS - watches.length)`. store/app.ts:388-393 `opts.watch ... ? Math.max(prev, 1)`. Home.tsx:109 `const complete = lesson.signIds.every((id) => (prog[id]?.masteryLevel ?? 0) >= 2)`. LessonPlayer.tsx:110-112 `app.recordLessonComplete(); celebrate();`.
proposedFix:
Make the queue cover every sign in the lesson before it caps. Either raise MAX_DRILLS to `max(12, signIds.length * 2)` for lessons, or trim by dropping the *extra* drills (checkpoints, the MAX_RECALL top-ups, the injected review cards) first and never the primary per-sign productive drill. Additionally, gate the celebratory end card: if `lesson.signIds.some(id => mastery < 2)`, render a "part 1 of 2 — X letters still to practise" continuation card with a "keep going" button that rebuilds the queue, instead of "Lesson complete!".

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Do NOT raise MAX_DRILLS or reorder the trim to preserve every per-sign productive drill — the two-pass truncation is a pinned design decision (engine.ts:92-96) and is asserted by src/lesson/curriculum.test.ts:105-129 (`completes in two passes`, `pass1.some(recognise) === false`, `every(mastery>=2) === false` after pass 1). That half of the fix would break the suite. The correct fix is the end-card half only: in LessonPlayer.tsx, when `lesson.signIds.some(id => mastery < 2)` after the queue drains, suppress celebrate()/recordLessonComplete()/`lsLessonDone` and render a "part 1 — X letters still to practise" continuation card, and restrict the `learned` chip list (LessonPlayer.tsx:119-121) to the signs actually drilled this pass rather than the whole lesson manifest. Also note the impact statement overreaches: 5 of 7 letters DO reach mastery 2, XP and streak are recorded, and pass 2 completes the node — the defect is the false completion claim, not lost progress.

title: The Dictionary detail's "Watch & practise" button does nothing, and it is the only action word signs have
problem: DetailPanel's `handleWatch` only sets a local `watched` boolean, which is read nowhere except to relabel the button "Watch" → "Watch Again". The medallion is a static SignGlyph — no video, no animation, no SignDemo, no store write. For non-gradable signs (all 19 A1 words) this inert button IS the primary full-width gold CTA, and the camera CTA is hidden. AllSigns is also the only screen that records no drill results at all.
userImpact: Every family-flag route ends here: Home's flag card, Family's flag rows and FlagPicker's "Practise these" all send non-gradable signs to `allSigns` — and FlagPicker only ever offers A1 word signs, so 100% of flags land on this screen. The user taps the one big button repeatedly, the label changes to "Watch Again", nothing happens, and there is no way to mark the sign done, so the flag never archives. On mobile there isn't even the "Add to Daily Review" escape hatch — it is `md:` only.
evidence: AllSigns.tsx:544 `const [watched, setWatched] = useState(false);` · :568 `const handleWatch = () => setWatched(true);` · :645 and :652 are the only reads (button label) · :724 `<SpringButton variant="gold" size="lg" full onClick={handleWatch}>{t("signWatchPractise", lang)}` · :741 `className="hidden gap-2 md:inline-flex"` on Add to Daily Review. Routes in: Home.tsx:432-436, Family.tsx:73-76, FlagPicker.tsx:324-327, FlagPicker.tsx:390-393. FlagPicker.tsx:82 `let list = A1_SIGNS.filter(...)` — only word signs are flaggable.
proposedFix:
Replace the medallion + dead Watch button in DetailPanel with the existing `<SignDemo sign={sign} lang={lang} />` component (Words.tsx:133 already does exactly this — it renders the instruction stage for footage-less words and a real replay for letters). Then give non-gradable signs the same self-mark action Words.tsx:41-48 uses (`recordDrillResult(sign.id, "hard", { selfMark: true })`), so a flagged word can actually be completed and the flag can archive. Move "Add to Daily Review" out of the `md:` gate and give it a confirmation state.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Two claims in the finding are wrong and change the fix. (1) "there is no way to mark the sign done, so the flag never archives" — Words.tsx:41-48 already provides exactly that self-mark (`recordDrillResult(id,"hard",{selfMark:true})` -> mastery 2 -> the M8 auto-archive at app.ts:441-456 fires), and Words is reachable from Home.tsx:366-379 and PractiseChooser. So the flag CAN archive today; the fix should route or reuse that path, not invent a new one. (2) "100% of flags land on this screen" is overstated — FlagPicker.tsx:82 only offers A1 words, but AllSigns' own DetailPanel flag control (:591-606, :749-768) can flag alphabet letters, which are gradable and route to the camera. The correct minimal fix is to swap the inert medallion+button for `<SignDemo sign={sign} lang={lang} />` (Words.tsx:133 pattern — its instruction stage teaches footage-less words and it hides its own Replay chip when it would do nothing, SignDemo.tsx:141) and add the Words self-mark to the sheet; ungating "Add to Daily Review" from `md:` is a separate, smaller win.

title: Practising a word lesson on camera silently opens the letter Alif instead
problem: `lessonCameraTarget()` returns undefined for lessons with no camera-gradable signs (every A1 word lesson). The Home path sheet's "Review →" action for a done node, and both camera buttons on the lesson results card, pass that undefined straight to `go({name:"camera", targetSignId: undefined})`. CameraPractice then falls back to its default `alpha-alif` (CameraPractice.tsx:30). The Home sheet gates its *secondary* camera button on the same value being defined, but the primary `done` action does not.
userImpact: A user finishes "Home & people" (mum, dad, sleep, thank you…), taps the dominant "Practise on camera" button on the results card — or taps a chip labelled "Mum · ماما — Practise on camera" — and is dropped into camera practice for the Arabic letter ا, which has nothing to do with what they just learned. Same thing when they tap "Review →" on a completed word node from the path.
evidence: Home.tsx:38-39 `lesson.signIds.map(signById).find((s) => s?.cameraGradable)?.id` · Home.tsx:588-590 `} else if (st === "done" && openNode.lesson) { go({ name: "camera", targetSignId: lessonCameraTarget(openNode.lesson) }); }` (ungated, unlike the `cameraTarget &&` guard at :643) · LessonPlayer.tsx:856 `onClick={() => onPractice(s.cameraGradable ? s.id : undefined)}` with `aria-label={...} — ${t("practiceCamera")}` at :857 · LessonPlayer.tsx:878 `onClick={() => onPractice(firstGradable?.id)}` · CameraPractice.tsx:30 `useState(initialSignId ?? "alpha-alif")`.
proposedFix: Apply the H5 rule already used for flags: when there is no gradable target, route to the sign's own surface instead of the camera. In Home.tsx:588-590 and LessonPlayer's ResultsCard, branch on `cameraGradable` — gradable → `{name:"camera", targetSignId}`, otherwise → `{name:"words"}` for A1 word lessons (or `{name:"allSigns", signId}` for a single sign). Also drop the "Practise on camera" aria-label from chips that cannot open the camera.

title: The last milestone rung can never be reached, so the treasure node sits at 0% permanently
problem: The final rung targets `A1_SIGNS.length` (19) signs at mastery 3. Mastery 3 requires `cameraHits >= 2`, and cameraHits only increments when a drill is recorded with `{camera: true, matched: true}`. No route in the app can ever pass an A1 word sign to CameraPractice: the target switcher only lists ALPHABET, AllSigns gates its camera CTA on `cameraGradable`, the flag CTAs pick `firstGradableFlag`, and Words has no camera path at all. So `a1Mastered` is structurally pinned at 0 and `nextMilestone` can never return null.
userImpact: Once a learner masters the alphabet — the app's stated headline achievement — the Home milestone card and the path's treasure chest permanently display "All the word unit mastered" with a 0%-filled bar and a chest sheet that says "Clear Unit 1 to open the reward chest". There is no "you have finished the content" state anywhere; the most advanced user's reward for finishing everything is a goal bar frozen at zero.
evidence: milestones.ts:20 `const a1Mastered = A1_SIGNS.filter((s2) => (prog[s2.id]?.masteryLevel ?? 0) >= 3).length;` · :51 `{ at: A1_SIGNS.length, value: a1Mastered, ... en: "All the word unit mastered" }` · store/app.ts:382 `const cameraHits = (prevP?.cameraHits ?? 0) + (opts.camera && opts.matched ? 1 : 0);` and :383-387 the mastery-3 gate. All eleven `recordDrillResult` call sites: only CameraPractice/FirstSign/Fingerspell/LessonPlayer's CameraDrill pass `camera: true`, and none of them can be handed a word sign. Home.tsx:539-558 + :131 render `ms` unconditionally; i18n.ts:225 `pathChestMeta: "Clear Unit 1 to open the reward chest."`.
proposedFix:
Make the word-unit rung count mastery >= 2 ("practised", the ceiling non-gradable signs can actually reach) instead of >= 3, or drop the rung until word signs become gradable. Also handle `nextMilestone() === null`: Home should render a "you've finished the current content" completion card and a completed chest node rather than nothing. Fix pathChestMeta to describe the milestone the chest actually represents (`ms.label`).

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The central evidence claim is false: word signs CAN reach CameraPractice. Progress.tsx:208 `onSign={(id) => go({name:"camera", targetSignId: id})}` is wired to the Coming-Up forecast rows (Progress.tsx:487-517) and the due list, which contain any word sign with an SRS card (seeded by Words' self-mark or AllSigns' addToReview). CameraTrainer.tsx:75-78 then opens un-seeded signs in TEACH mode, and a teach-mode hold emits `onResult("match")` at :298, which CameraPractice.tsx:56-61 records as `{camera:true, matched:true}` — so cameraHits does increment and mastery 3 is attainable. The rung is impractical, not structurally impossible, and `nextMilestone()` can return null. Because of that, the fix should be the low-risk pair: (a) fix pathChestMeta to render `ms.label` (a real defect regardless of this finding), and (b) handle `nextMilestone() === null` on Home. Changing the rung to mastery >= 2 is optional polish, and note Progress.tsx:75 already uses `>= 2` for its own a1Done count, so that change would at least align the two surfaces.

title: "Whole alphabet" achievement counts 31 letters against a denominator of 28, so it can read "31 / 28" and unlock early
problem: `alphaLit`/`alphaTaught` are built from the full ALPHABET array (31 entries: 28 seeded letters plus the three reference-only edge forms ة، لا، ال). The achievement compares that count to a hard-coded 28. milestones.ts and PractiseChooser both correctly filter on `cameraGradable` first; Progress does not.
userImpact: A learner who practises only 25 real letters plus the three edge forms (all three are tappable in CameraPractice's chip strip and reachable via Fingerspell/Dictionary) is told "Whole alphabet — Unlocked" while three real letters are untouched. A learner who touches all 31 sees the nonsensical counter "31 / 28". The same inflated number drives the "palms grown" tile.
evidence: Progress.tsx:79-82 `const alphaLit = new Set(ALPHABET.filter((s) => (prog[s.id]?.masteryLevel ?? 0) >= 1).map((s) => s.id)); const alphaTaught = alphaLit.size;` — ALPHABET has 31 entries (content/signs.ts:38-70, three created with `edge = true`) · Progress.tsx:617-620 `status: `${toLocaleDigits(alphaTaught, lang)} / ${toLocaleDigits(28, lang)}``, `earned: alphaTaught >= 28` · Progress.tsx:378 uses alphaTaught for prPalmsGrown. Contrast milestones.ts:25-27 `ALPHABET.filter((s2) => s2.cameraGradable && ...)` and PractiseChooser.tsx:43-45.
proposedFix: Add `s.cameraGradable &&` to the alphaLit filter at Progress.tsx:80 so it matches milestones.ts. Keep the Constellation's `/ ALPHABET.length` denominator honest by giving it its own count of all 31, or switch the Constellation to the 28 seeded letters too.

title: The weekly streak grid and month heatmap use UTC dates while activity is recorded in local dates
problem: `dayKey()` in Progress derives its key with `toISOString().slice(0,10)` (UTC), but `activeDays` entries are written by the store's `todayKey()`, which uses local `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate`. The two disagree by one day whenever local time is ahead of UTC and the clock is before the offset. The weekday index `todayDow` is also computed locally, so the whole grid shifts.
userImpact: In Qatar (UTC+3) — the target market — between 00:00 and 03:00 local, the "today" dot on the weekly streak stays a hollow dashed circle no matter how much the learner practises, yesterday's dot lights up instead, and the 35-day heatmap is shifted by one cell. A late-night learner's contribution grid silently records the wrong day.
evidence: Progress.tsx:49-53 `function dayKey(back: number) { const d = new Date(); d.setDate(d.getDate() - back); return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10); }` vs store/app.ts:33-38 `export function todayKey(d = new Date()) { const y = d.getFullYear(); ... return `${y}-${m}-${day}`; }` (the value pushed into `activeDays` at app.ts:411-413). Consumed at Progress.tsx:104-108 (`activeSet.has(key)`) and :116 (heatmap).
proposedFix:
Delete Progress's local `dayKey` and import `todayKey` from `../store/app`, calling it with an offset date: `const dayKey = (back: number) => { const d = new Date(); d.setDate(d.getDate() - back); return todayKey(d); }`. One shared date-key helper for the whole app.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Display-only and time-boxed: the mismatch exists only between local midnight and the UTC offset (3 hours/day in Qatar, 1 hour in UK summer). The stored streak, activeDays and streakFor() are all local-key based and stay correct — nothing is 'silently recorded on the wrong day', only rendered on the wrong cell.

title: The full-screen streak celebration can never fire
problem: `lastStreak` is a useRef initialised to `profile.streak` at first render of the mount, and the effect only celebrates when `profile.streak > lastStreak.current`. On mount the two are always equal, and nothing inside Progress can raise the streak (no drill is recorded on this screen). Progress remounts on every navigation, so the ref resets every time.
userImpact: The entire StreakCelebration overlay — confetti, hero art, day dots, the "X days of showing up" moment, ~130 lines of code — is unreachable. The file's own header comment claims "the full-screen streak-celebration moment still fires on a fresh milestone"; it does not. Hitting a streak milestone produces no celebration anywhere in the app.
evidence: Progress.tsx:125-132 `const lastStreak = useRef(profile.streak); useEffect(() => { if (profile.streak > lastStreak.current && profile.streak > 1) { setCelebrating(true); } lastStreak.current = profile.streak; }, [profile.streak]);` — on mount `profile.streak === lastStreak.current`. Progress records no drills (no `recordDrillResult` call site in Progress.tsx, per grep of all 11 call sites). Header comment at Progress.tsx:17-18.
proposedFix: Persist the last-celebrated streak instead of deriving it from mount state: store `lastCelebratedStreak` per profile (localStorage or the app store) and fire when `streakFor(profile) > lastCelebratedStreak && streakFor(profile) > 1`, then write the new value back. Fire it from wherever the streak actually increments (the drill result path) rather than from a read-only screen.

title: The badged "Ready" alphabet card silently ends onboarding at step 4 of 10 with a nameless default profile
problem: On the "What do you want to learn?" step, the Arabic Alphabet card calls `finish()` directly. `finish()` without `skipAll` still reads the component state for persona, hand, goal and name — but none of those steps have been shown yet, so it creates the profile with persona "parent", dominantHand "R", dailyGoal "regular" and `name` empty, which falls back to the literal "Me" / "أنا".
userImpact: The most attractive option on the screen — teal, badged "Ready", the app's only genuinely graded content — silently terminates a 10-step setup at 40% progress. The user is never asked their name, handedness, daily goal, who they are learning for, or offered the calendar reminder. Home then greets them "Marhaba, Me", the daily-goal ring is set to a target they never chose, and the persona taglines and Family role wiring all default to "parent".
evidence: Onboarding.tsx:335-339 `<button ... onClick={() => finish({ destination: { name: "camera", targetSignId: "alpha-alif", autoStart: true } })}` · :125-141 `finish` — `const displayName = name.trim() || (lang === "ar" ? "أنا" : "Me"); createProfile({ displayName, role: overrides?.skipAll ? "parent" : persona, ... })` with persona/hand/goal still at their :117-119 defaults · :150-161 STEP_ORDER has 10 entries, `learn` is index 3 · Home.tsx:259 renders `<bdi>{profile.displayName}</bdi>`.
proposedFix: Make the alphabet card set a `learnPath` state and call `setStep("name")` (or continue through hand/goal/name) rather than `finish()`, keeping the camera destination in state and applying it after the name step. At minimum, jump straight to the name step so the profile is never created without a name.

title: Dominant-hand choice is collected twice and read by nothing
problem: `Profile.dominantHand` is written by onboarding and editable in Settings, but a repo-wide grep shows no consumer anywhere in the recognizer, lesson engine, camera trainer or any screen. The camera canonicalises both hands via `mirror = frame.detectedHand === "Left"`, so handedness genuinely has no effect on grading — but the app still asks for it as a full onboarding step and offers a Settings toggle.
userImpact: A dedicated onboarding screen ("Which hand do you sign with?") and a Settings control both change absolutely nothing. A left-handed user who carefully selects "Left" gets identical demonstrations, identical reference photos and identical grading — this is exactly the kind of control-that-does-nothing that makes the app feel incoherent.
evidence: `grep -rn dominantHand src` returns only: types.ts:14 (declaration), Settings.tsx:69/191/196 (writer), Family.tsx:93 (hard-coded "R"), Onboarding.tsx:133 (writer), store/app.ts:67/235/323/331 (plumbing). No reader. CameraTrainer.tsx:179 `const mirror = frame.detectedHand === "Left"; // canonicalise both hands (§6.8)`.
proposedFix:
Either use it — mirror the reference photo/HandSkeleton in SignDemo, SignGlyph and CameraTrainer's reference chip for left-handed profiles, and phrase the hint accordingly — or remove the onboarding step and the Settings toggle. Do not keep a stored preference nothing consumes.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Prefer removal over 'use it'. The reference imagery for every letter is a real ArSL21L signer photo (content/signs.ts:34, rendered by SignGlyph.tsx:32-40 and SignDemo.tsx:55-72) — horizontally flipping licensed source photography misrepresents the cited dataset and would contradict the app's own never-mirror rule for physical artwork. If handedness is kept, mirror only the synthetic HandSkeleton and the hint copy, never sign.photo.

title: The same word signs are "Unit 2" on Home and "Unit 1" in the Dictionary
problem: Home derives the unit number from the index in the UNITS array, where UNITS[0] is the alphabet and UNITS[1] is the A1 words — so words render as "Unit 2" and the alphabet as "Unit 1". AllSigns hard-codes the opposite: its "Unit 1" filter chip selects `tier === "A1"`, its category tag calls every non-alphabet sign "Unit 1", and STATUS_META.unit is "Unit 1" for A1 signs.
userImpact: A learner reading "Unit 2 · Family & First Words" on the Home banner then opens the Dictionary, taps "Unit 1", and gets exactly those same signs. Two screens give the same content two different unit numbers, and the alphabet — Unit 1 on Home — has no unit chip at all in the Dictionary.
evidence: Home.tsx:118 `const unitIdx = Math.max(0, UNITS.findIndex((u) => u.id === nextLesson.unitId));` · :297 `{`${t("homeUnit", lang)} ${num(unitIdx + 1, lang)}`}` with content/signs.ts:189 `export const UNITS: Unit[] = [UNIT_ALPHA, UNIT_A1_U1];` · AllSigns.tsx:161 `{ id: "unit1", en: "Unit 1", ar: "الوحدة ١" }` filtering `sign.tier !== "A1"` at :125 · AllSigns.tsx:46 `tags.push({ label: pick(lang, "Unit 1", "الوحدة ١") ... })` for non-alphabet · :36 `unit: { en: "Unit 1" ... }`.
proposedFix: Derive the label from the content layer in both places. Add a `number` or use `UNITS.findIndex` in AllSigns' `categoryTags`, STATUS_META and the filter chips so the alphabet reads "Unit 1" and the words read "Unit 2" everywhere. Replace the hard-coded "Unit 1" strings in AllSigns.tsx:36, :46 and :161.

title: After finishing every lesson the path silently restarts at lesson 1 with no completion state
problem: `nextLesson` is the first lesson with any sign below mastery 2, falling back to `LESSONS[0]`. Once all eight lessons are complete the fallback fires, and because the node status check tests `lesson.id === nextLesson.id` before `complete`, lesson 1 is rendered as "current" — coral, pulsing, with the START badge and Fanan cheering — instead of "done". The unit banner also reverts to Unit 1.
userImpact: A learner who works through the entire curriculum is shown the same "START — Alif to Kha" call to action they saw on day one, with Unit 1 back on the banner and the four completed alphabet nodes still visibly incomplete. There is no acknowledgement anywhere that the content is finished, and it reads as if their progress was lost.
evidence: Home.tsx:98-99 `const nextLesson = LESSONS.find((l) => l.signIds.some((id) => (prog[id]?.masteryLevel ?? 0) < 2)) ?? LESSONS[0];` · :110-111 `const status = lesson.id === nextLesson.id ? "current" : complete ? "done" : "locked";` — the current test wins over complete · :118-119 unit banner follows `nextLesson.unitId`.
proposedFix:
Compute `const allDone = !LESSONS.some(l => l.signIds.some(id => mastery < 2))`. When allDone, mark every node "done", keep the unit banner on the last unit, and render a completion state (the milestone chest as reached, plus a "keep it sharp" review/free-camera CTA) instead of resurrecting lesson 1 as current. Also reorder the status check so `complete` wins over `current`.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Endgame-only: this state requires mastery >= 2 on all 28 seeded letters and all 19 A1 words, i.e. a fully finished curriculum. No user reaches it before completing everything, so it is a missing completion state rather than an in-flight bug. Note also that the completed nodes still render "done" correctly — only lesson 1 is mislabelled — so 'the four completed alphabet nodes still visibly incomplete' overstates it (nodes 2-4 read done; node 1 reads current).

title: Word lessons ask the same sign as an identical recall question twice in one sitting
problem: In buildDrillQueue the teach block already pushes one drill per sign, and because no A1 word has a photo, media or handshape, `hasVisual()` is false for all of them so every one becomes a `recall`. The productive block then pushes up to MAX_RECALL = 2 more `recall` drills drawn from the same non-gradable set, with no exclusion of signs already queued.
userImpact: In "First connections" (4 signs) the learner answers, say, "Yes" and "Hello" twice with the same four-option grid inside one 10-drill lesson — and because the tiles for word signs are all the identical generic `sign_language` icon (SignGlyph falls through to the icon), the repeat is indistinguishable from the first ask. It reads as the lesson glitching or looping.
evidence: engine.ts:60-63 pushes one drill per signId, resolving to `recall` because `hasVisual` at :27-29 needs photo/handshape/media and A1 signs (content/signs.ts:87) have none — alphabet-shapes.json contains only the 28 `alpha-*` keys · engine.ts:70-73 `const nonGradable = lesson.signIds.filter((id) => !signById(id)?.cameraGradable); for (const signId of shuffle(nonGradable).slice(0, MAX_RECALL)) { queue.push({ type: "recall", signId }); }` — same ids, no dedupe · SignGlyph.tsx final `return <Icon name="sign_language" ... />` for all words except iloveyou.
proposedFix: Filter the productive top-up to signs not already queued: `const already = new Set(queue.map(d => d.signId)); const nonGradable = lesson.signIds.filter(id => !signById(id)?.cameraGradable && !already.has(id));`. For lessons where every sign is already drilled, drop the top-up entirely rather than repeating.

title: Skipping every camera drill in a lesson reports 100% accuracy
problem: `accuracy` defaults to 100 when `scored.current === 0`, and skip deliberately records nothing (`onDone({ xp: 0, scored: false, correct: false })`). In an alphabet lesson every non-watch drill is a camera drill, so a learner who skips all of them ends with zero scored drills.
userImpact: A frustrated learner who cannot get the camera to confirm anything skips every drill and is congratulated with "Great session! · 100% Accuracy" — while their path node has not moved at all. The number is fabricated at exactly the moment honesty matters most.
evidence: LessonPlayer.tsx:120-125 `const accuracy = scored.current === 0 ? 100 : Math.round((correctCount.current / scored.current) * 100);` · :404-408 `if (result === "skip") { onDone({ xp: 0, scored: false, correct: false }); return; }` · :828-832 renders it as `formatPercent(accuracy, lang)` under `t("accuracy")`.
proposedFix: Render an em dash or hide the accuracy tile when `scored.current === 0`, matching the honest "—" pattern already used in Progress's StatsTab (Progress.tsx:543-546) when `cameraAttempts === 0`.

title: A completed path node claims "Mastered" when it only requires "practised"
problem: A node is marked `done` at mastery >= 2 ("practised" per types.ts:81), but the sheet's meta line for a done node is `pathDoneMeta` = "Mastered · tap to review". Mastery 3 is a much harder gate requiring FSRS Review state, stability >= 2 days and two camera-confirmed hits.
userImpact: The path tells the learner a lesson's signs are mastered while Progress's "signs mastered" tile, the Constellation and the family board all still count them as unmastered — three surfaces disagreeing about the same signs.
evidence: Home.tsx:109 `const complete = lesson.signIds.every((id) => (prog[id]?.masteryLevel ?? 0) >= 2);` · Home.tsx:571-574 `st === "done" ? t("pathDoneMeta", lang)` · i18n.ts:223 `pathDoneMeta: { en: "Mastered · tap to review" ... }` · types.ts:81 `masteryLevel: number; // 0 none · 1 seen · 2 practised · 3 mastered` · store/app.ts:383-387 the mastery-3 gate.
proposedFix: Change pathDoneMeta to "Practised · tap to review" / "تمرّنت عليها · انقر للمراجعة", or raise the node's `complete` threshold to >= 3 (which, given the camera gate, would make the alphabet nodes far harder — the copy fix is the right one).

title: "Watch & practise" — the only action on every word sign — does nothing
problem: For non-gradable signs (all 19 A1 words), DetailPanel's primary gold CTA calls `handleWatch`, which is `const handleWatch = () => setWatched(true)`. `watched` is read in exactly two places: the label of the replay chip and the aria-label of the gold play FAB. So the dominant button on the screen flips the wording of a different button and does nothing else — no video, no hint reveal (the hint is already on screen), no drill recorded, no mastery change. The same screen position opens the camera for gradable signs, so the control teaches the user it is functional.
userImpact: This screen is the destination of every non-gradable deep link in the app: Home's flag card (Home.tsx:435), Family's flag rows (Family.tsx:76), FlagPicker's summary rows and its "Practise these" CTA (FlagPicker.tsx:327,393), and AllSigns' own "Practise your N flagged signs" button (AllSigns.tsx:240). A learner following the family-flag flow lands here, taps the one big button, and nothing happens. There is no self-mark on this screen (mobile shows only Flag + Share; "Add to Daily Review" is `hidden ... md:inline-flex`, desktop-only), so on a phone there is literally no way to progress a flagged word from the surface the app routed you to.
evidence: src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:568 `const handleWatch = () => setWatched(true);` · 724-727 `<SpringButton variant="gold" ... onClick={handleWatch}>{t("signWatchPractise", lang)}` ("Watch & practise") · 645/652 `watched ? "Watch Again" : "Watch"` are the only readers of the state · `grep -rn recordDrillResult src` returns no hit in AllSigns.tsx, so mastery/SRS can never move from here.
proposedFix:
Give the non-gradable branch the same never-hard-fail self-mark the rest of the app uses. Replace the gold CTA's handler with a real action: render `<SignDemo sign={sign} lang={lang} />` (which already teaches word signs via the hint stage, SignDemo.tsx:108-135) in place of the static SignGlyph medallion, then show the `camSelfMark`/`camSelfMarkSub` button that calls `recordDrillResult(sign.id, "hard", { selfMark: true })` exactly as Words.tsx:44 does, swapping to the `wordsMarked` confirmation. Move "Add to Daily Review" out of `md:` so mobile gets it too. If the demo/self-mark is not wanted here, instead route non-gradable flags to the Words sheet (add `signId?: string` to the `words` screen in store/ui.ts and open that card on mount) and delete this dead CTA.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The SignDemo swap works (SignDemo.tsx:108-135 renders the hint stage for footage-less words, and demoShowsHint() lets you drop the panel's duplicate hint block at :690-711). The self-mark part needs a guard: recordDrillResult(id,'hard',{selfMark:true}) is repeatable here for the same reason as in Words (see words-selfmark-repeatable), so derive the confirmation state from the store, not local state, before wiring it to a panel the user can reopen freely.

title: Flagging does nothing at all in a one-person household — the default after onboarding
problem: `toggleFlag` seeds the due-now SRS card into every profile EXCEPT the raiser (`if (p.id === byProfileId) continue;`). Home's pinned-flag section and the nav badge both filter out flags you raised yourself (`.filter(f => f.raisedByProfileId !== profile.id)`). Onboarding creates exactly one profile. So for a solo user, flagging a sign produces: no SRS card, no Home pin, no nav badge, no queue change anywhere — the only trace is the list on the Family tab and the FlagPicker summary.
userImpact: Family Mode's primary CTA ("Flag signs we need") opens a screen that promises "Flag the signs your family needs — everyone's queue follows" and "You direct what they learn". The user flags five signs, taps Done, returns to Home, and absolutely nothing has changed. This is the single loudest "doesn't make sense" in the app for the most common install state.
evidence: src/store/app.ts:554-560 (raiser skipped when seeding cards) · src/screens/Home.tsx:103-105 `pinnedFlagSigns(...).filter(f => f.raisedByProfileId !== profile.id)` · src/components/AppNav.tsx:60-62 (same filter for the badge) · src/screens/FlagPicker.tsx:146-149 the "everyone's queue follows" copy · src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:130 creates a single profile · src/store/family.test.ts:185-187 already pins the solo case at the store level (the flag can never archive).
proposedFix:
Two parts. (1) In `toggleFlag`, when `s.profiles.length === 1` (or more generally when the raiser is not a `deaf` role), also seed the raiser's own card — a hearing solo learner flagging a sign means "I want to learn this", so it must enter their queue. (2) In Family.tsx, when `app.profiles.length === 1`, replace the flag CTA's framing: either hide the household chrome behind an "Add someone" empty state, or relabel the CTA to "Pick the signs I need next" and stop filtering own-flags out of Home so the user sees the result. Do not ship the promise text to a household of one.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Gate the store change on `s.profiles.length === 1` only. The broader 'when the raiser is not deaf' variant contradicts the documented H4 contract and its test (family.test.ts:47-57 asserts `srs[raiser]` stays undefined) and would silently change multi-member households. Likewise gate the Home/AppNav un-filtering on the solo case — removing the raiser filter unconditionally would show a Deaf member their own flags as incoming requests.

title: FlagPicker's whole practise path shows camera icons for signs the camera cannot grade
problem: The picker only lists `A1_SIGNS`, and all 19 of them have `cameraGradable: false` (verified: 0/19 in src/content/signs.ts). Yet the CTA carries `<Icon name="videocam" />`, and every row in the flagged-sign summary renders a coral `videocam` icon as its trailing affordance regardless of gradability.
userImpact: The user taps a big coral "Practise these" button with a camera icon and gets a dictionary page with no camera on it — and (per the finding above) no working action either. The camera icon is a promise the content cannot keep, on every row and on the main CTA.

title: The Deaf member cannot flag any of the 31 letters — the only content the app can actually teach
problem: Both the group filter and the search read from `A1_SIGNS` only: `let list = A1_SIGNS.filter((s) => groupOf(s) === group)` and, when a query is present, `list = A1_SIGNS.filter(...)`. userImpact: The screen whose entire premise is "You direct what they learn" cannot direct anyone to the letters. A parent who wants "teach my child their name" or "work on ب" has no path; they can only flag ASL-adapted, watch-only, un-gradable words. evidence: src/screens/FlagPicker.tsx:81-96 (both branches use `A1_SIGNS`) · 32-51 `SIGN_GROUP` maps word ids only, `groupOf` defaults to "home" · src/content/signs.ts:38-70 ALPHABET (31 signs, 28 gradable, all with `photo`) · the summary at FlagPicker.tsx:101-103 deliberately uses `signById` "so flagged ALPHABET signs resolve too".

Add a fifth group `{ id: "letters", label: pick(lang, "Letters", "الحروف"), icon: "abc" }` whose list is `ALPHABET.filter(s => s.cameraGradable)`, and change the search branch to filter `ALL_SIGNS` (matching `glossEn`, `glossAr` and `code`) so typing "ب" or "ba" finds the letter. `groupOf` returns "letters" for `sign.tier === "alphabet"`. Everything downstream (toggleFlag, the summary, the camera CTA) already handles letters correctly.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Adding the group is right, but filter ALPHABET on `cameraGradable` as proposed AND keep the search branch honest: `code` matching is what makes typing 'ب' work, since glossEn for letters is 'Ba' and glossAr is the code itself. Note groupOf() is typed `Exclude<GroupId,"all">` and returns a hardcoded fallback, so it needs widening, not just a new case.

title: FlagPicker tells you that you flagged a sign for yourself, in the third person
problem: `heroRequestor` is `requestors.find((p) => p.id !== profile.id) ?? requestors[0]` — the `??` falls back to yourself. title: Every word sign draws the identical generic icon, so word grids carry no information

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Do NOT put the emoji back into these wells. docs/AUDIT-2026-07.md:45 (H14) and ENGINE-ROADMAP.md:52-57 record that emoji were deliberately purged from exactly these surfaces — FlagPicker tiles, Family honeycomb and board pills, LessonPlayer recall tiles — and routed through SignGlyph; the proposed fix reverses that decision on all four. title: Fingerspell's practise-along has no way out except skipping every remaining letter
problem: When `practising` is true the whole word view (letter strip, stage, play/speed controls, practise card) is replaced by a single `CameraTrainer`. The trainer's only controls are self-mark and Skip, and Skip advances to the next letter rather than ending the session. There is no Cancel/Stop. The only other exits are the header back button (leaves Fingerspell entirely; the typed word is component state and is lost on unmount) or typing in the input/backspace, which calls `onText` and silently kills the session while mutating the word.
userImpact: A user who spells a 6-letter name, starts practise-along and then wants to stop must tap "Skip" six times, or leave the screen and retype the word from scratch. Nothing on screen tells them either of those is the way out.
evidence: src/screens/Fingerspell.tsx:199-212 (the `practising && practiseSign` branch renders only CameraTrainer) · 104-109 `if (practiseIdx + 1 >= gradable.length) { setPractising(false); ... } else setPractiseIdx(i => i + 1)` · 69-76 `onText` resets `practising` · src/components/CameraTrainer.tsx:576-589 (only self-mark and skip are offered).
proposedFix: Render a ghost "Stop practising" / `t("close")` button directly under the trainer inside the `practising` branch: `onClick={() => { setPractising(false); setPractiseIdx(0); }}`. Keep the typed text untouched so the user returns to their word. Optionally show `exerciseLabel` progress alongside it (already computed at line 117).

title: Typing digits or punctuation shows "Type a word to begin" even though you typed one
problem: The stage falls back to the `fspEmpty` card ("Type a word to begin — try your name.") whenever `letters.length === 0`, without checking whether `steps` contains skipped characters. Input made only of digits (`123`, `١٢٣`), punctuation, or a bare hamza produces zero letter steps and N skipped steps, so the user sees the honest "we can't fingerspell these" note AND a stage telling them to type something — while their text sits in the box above.
userImpact: The screen contradicts itself and offers no next step: no play controls, no practise card, and an empty-state instruction the user has already followed. It reads as broken rather than as an honest limitation.
evidence: src/screens/Fingerspell.tsx:258 `{current && currentSign ? ... : (<ScreenCard>...{t("fspEmpty", lang)}` at 324-329 · 49-50 `letters`/`skipped` split · src/content/signs.ts:267-275 `fingerspellSequence` returns `skipped` steps for digits/Latin/punctuation · src/i18n.ts:389 `fspEmpty: "Type a word to begin — try your name."`.
proposedFix: Branch the empty stage on `steps.length`: when `letters.length === 0 && steps.length > 0`, show a distinct card — reuse `fspSkippedNote` as the headline plus a "try Arabic letters or English letters" line and the letter pad hint — instead of `fspEmpty`. Keep `fspEmpty` for a genuinely empty input.

title: The two Practise sub-screens have hardcoded, contradictory back buttons
problem: Words' header back button always goes to `practiseChooser`; Fingerspell's always goes to `home`. Both screens are reachable from both Home (Home.tsx:369, 385) and the Practise hub (PractiseChooser.tsx:80, 104), and AppNav marks both as belonging to the Practise tab. So each back button is wrong from one of its two entry points, and Fingerspell's is wrong in a worse way: it moves the user to a different tab than the one highlighted in the nav bar.
userImpact: Back does not go back. Entering Words from Home and pressing back lands on the Practise tab; entering Fingerspell from the Practise hub and pressing back lands on Learn. Two sibling screens in the same tab behave in opposite ways.

Better: add a one-field `from?: Screen["name"]` to the `words` and `fingerspell` routes in store/ui.ts, set it at the four call sites, and have the back button use `go({ name: from ?? "practiseChooser" })`.

Fixing only Fingerspell leaves the same contradiction between Words and the camera screen — change all three, or add the `from?` route field and set it at all six call sites.

title: The Words self-mark can be tapped unlimited times, farming XP and churning the SRS card
problem: `selfMark` is guarded only by the local `marked` flag, and `open()` resets `marked` to false every time a card is tapped. Closing and reopening the same word lets the user record another drill: +4 XP, another `drillsCompleted`/`selfMarks` metric increment, another day-active/streak write, and another FSRS `hard` rating that reshuffles the card's due date. Every other self-mark surface in the app is inside CameraTrainer, which finishes and unmounts, so it cannot repeat — Words is the only one that can.
userImpact: Tapping one word thirteen times completes a 50-XP daily goal without learning anything, which makes the goal ring and the honesty metrics meaningless. Repeated `hard` ratings on the same card also degrade its scheduling.
evidence: src/screens/Words.tsx:37-48 — `open` sets `setMarked(false)`, `selfMark` guards on `if (!selected || marked) return;` then `app.recordDrillResult(selected.id, "hard", { selfMark: true })` · src/store/app.ts:401-402 `xpGain = opts.watch ? 5 : success ? 10 : 4` (a `hard` self-mark yields 4 XP every time) · src/store/app.ts:436 `if (opts.selfMark) metrics.selfMarks += 1`.
proposedFix:
Derive the marked state from the store instead of local state, e.g. `const alreadyMarked = (app.progress[profile.id]?.[selected.id]?.masteryLevel ?? 0) >= 2` and render the `wordsMarked` confirmation (with a "Practise it again" ghost link) when it is true. If re-practising should be allowed, gate it per day: skip the call when `progress[...].lastSeen` is already today.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: `masteryLevel >= 2` is a valid derivation (a 'hard' non-watch outcome sets Math.max(prev,2) at app.ts:391-397) but it is not Words-specific: a word practised in a lesson or via a flag drill also reaches 2, so the sheet would open already showing 'Marked' for words the user never marked here. A per-day guard on `progress[id].lastSeen` is the cleaner rule, and it should be applied to CameraPractice too.

title: The prominent "Most Needed" toggle usually does nothing visible
problem: `mostNeeded` only sorts flagged signs ahead of unflagged ones inside the currently filtered list. It defaults to on, the group defaults to "home" (6 signs), and on a fresh install nothing is flagged — so toggling it re-renders an identically ordered grid. It only ever changes anything when at least one sign in the visible group is already flagged.
userImpact: A large bordered button sitting next to the search field appears to be a filter or a sort mode and produces no visible change on first use, which trains the user to distrust the controls on the screen.
evidence: src/screens/FlagPicker.tsx:88-93 `list = [...list].sort((a, b) => Number(flaggedIds.has(b.id)) - Number(flaggedIds.has(a.id)))` · 177-188 the toggle button · 58 `const [group, setGroup] = useState<GroupId>("home")`.
proposedFix: Either hide the toggle when `flags.length === 0`, or make it mean something real: change it to a "Flagged only" filter (`if (mostNeeded) list = list.filter(s => flaggedIds.has(s.id))`) with the flagged count in the label, which is a state the user can actually see change.

title: FlagPicker calls useMemo after a conditional early return (rules-of-hooks violation)
problem: `if (!profile) return <NoProfileFallback />;` sits at line 60, before `const signs = useMemo(...)` at line 81. React requires an identical hook count on every render; any render where `profile` is null runs three hooks instead of four. Today App.tsx gates the whole tree on `activeProfile` (App.tsx:128) so the null branch is unreachable and no crash occurs, but the file is one refactor — or one direct mount in a test/Storybook — away from "Rendered fewer hooks than expected". Words, Home, AllSigns and LessonPlayer all place their hooks correctly before the guard.
userImpact: None today. If the guard ever becomes reachable (profile deletion, a household import that clears `activeProfileId`, rendering the screen without App's gate), the screen throws instead of showing the fallback.
evidence: src/screens/FlagPicker.tsx:57-60 (three useState, then the early return) and 81 `const signs = useMemo(...)` · contrast src/screens/Words.tsx:28-34 and src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:83-176, where every hook precedes the guard.
proposedFix:
Move the `useMemo` (and the `q` derivation it depends on) above line 60, guarding inside the callback with `if (!profile) return [];`, or simply move `if (!profile) return <NoProfileFallback />;` to just before the `return (` at line 116. Enable `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` in the lint config so this cannot regress.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: 'Enable react-hooks/rules-of-hooks in the lint config' is not actionable — this project has no ESLint at all (no config file, no eslint package in package.json or node_modules), which is why the `// eslint-disable-next-line` at FlagPicker.tsx:95 is inert. Move the guard to just before the return, and treat adding ESLint as a separate decision.

title: The "Two hands" badge in the Words sheet shows a one-hand icon
problem: The badge in the word sheet's header always renders `<Icon name="front_hand" />` and only switches its text label between `wordsTwoHands` and `wordsOneHand`. The section headers on the same screen get this right, using `sign_language` for the two-hand section and `front_hand` for the one-hand section.
userImpact: Four two-handed signs (more, finished, help, name) show a single-hand pictogram next to the words "Two hands", contradicting the one piece of information the badge exists to convey.
evidence: src/screens/Words.tsx:127-130 `<Icon name="front_hand" ... /> {t(selected.hands === 2 ? "wordsTwoHands" : "wordsOneHand", lang)}` · contrast line 58 `<Icon name={titleKey === "wordsOneHand" ? "front_hand" : "sign_language"} ... />`.
proposedFix: Match the section header: `<Icon name={selected.hands === 2 ? "sign_language" : "front_hand"} className="text-xs leading-none" />`.

title: Meter reads up to 100% "Camera confidence" on frames the grader is rejecting, so the hold ring never starts and nothing explains why
