problem: `gradeWithModel` returns `confidence: targetP` unconditionally, even when the out-of-distribution seed gate rejects the frame. The KNN path does the opposite — `knn.ts:259` returns `confidence: gated ? targetShare : 0` — so the two graders disagree about what the number means. CameraTrainer pushes that raw softmax straight into the meter labelled "Camera confidence" (CameraTrainer.tsx:277, 520-548).
userImpact: The learner holds a handshape, watches the bar climb to 90-100%, and the gold hold-to-confirm ring never moves and never explains itself. This is the exact "it doesn't make sense" failure: the app says you are 100% right and simultaneously refuses to accept it. It also silently starves the soft-fail path of any explanation before the 20s "Still tricky" band fires.
evidence: classifier.ts:107-113 — `const seedD = nearestSeedDistance(vec, targetId); const inDistribution = seedD <= OOD_GATE; return { confidence: targetP, matched: r.classId === targetId && targetP >= MODEL_TAU && inDistribution }`. I ran the repo's own junk vector through it (`Array(42).fill(5)`, the case classifier.test.ts:45-56 already covers): result was `class alpha-ha matched false confidence shown to user = 100% seedD 29.58`. A noise sweep over the bundled seeds gave 137 of 224 non-matching frames displaying >=70% on the meter at moderate noise (amp 0.25), max 100%.
proposedFix:
Mirror knn.ts: `confidence: inDistribution ? targetP : 0` in `gradeWithModel`, and surface the OOD rejection as a distinct UI state in CameraTrainer (the coach already has a `{kind:"reference"}` advice — force it whenever `targetP >= MODEL_TAU && !inDistribution` so the learner is told "compare with the reference" instead of staring at a lying 100%). Update classifier.test.ts:41-56 to assert the zeroed confidence, not just `matched === false`.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The zeroing half is right, but the UI half of the fix cannot be written as proposed: `ModelGrade` exposes no `inDistribution` field and OOD_GATE is not exported, so CameraTrainer has no way to test `targetP >= MODEL_TAU && !inDistribution` — add `inDistribution: boolean` to ModelGrade (debug.seedD alone is not enough without the gate constant) before wiring the forced `{kind:"reference"}` advice. Also note zeroing `confidence` changes the post-match tile at CameraTrainer.tsx:930-937 only in the matched case (where inDistribution is true), so that stays correct.

title: If the seed chunk fails to load, grading is paused forever with no message, no coach, no soft-fail — only a permanently 0% meter
problem: Grading early-returns on every frame while `seedsReady.current` is false, and the only thing that ever sets it true is `ensureSeeds().then(...)`; its `.catch` is an empty block. On a rejected load (offline first camera use, or a hashed chunk 404 after the autoUpdate service worker swaps in a new deploy under an open tab) the flag stays false for the whole mount. The early return also skips `attemptFrames` and the soft-fail clock, so `showUnsure` and "Still tricky" can never fire either.
userImpact: The camera runs, the hand skeleton draws, the status pill says "Hand detected" and Fanan says "Ooh, nice…" while the meter sits at 0% forever. There is no error, no retry, no hint that grading is off. The learner's only escape is the self-mark button, which rates the card 'hard'.
evidence: CameraTrainer.tsx:206-212 `if (!seedsReady.current) { pushConfidence(0); pushHold(0); heldMs.current = 0; lastHoldTs.current = null; return; }`; CameraTrainer.tsx:324-337 `void ensureSeeds().then(...).catch(() => { /* offline & never cached — grading stays paused; the camera UI still works */ })`; seedStore.ts:36-39 rethrows after nulling `loadPromise`.
proposedFix:
Add a `seedsFailed` state set in the `.catch`. When true, render an honest band in `controls` ("Grading isn't available right now — you can still watch the reference and mark yourself") plus a Retry button that re-calls `ensureSeeds()`, and suppress the "Ooh, nice…"/"Hand detected" copy so the UI stops implying it is grading. A retry with backoff inside the effect (2-3 attempts) covers the transient-404 case.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Severity lowered because vite.config.ts precaches the seed chunk (globPatterns includes **/*.js with maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes 30MB), so this only bites on the very first camera use with a failed network fetch, or on a tab left open across an autoUpdate redeploy. The proposed fix is otherwise sound; the retry must also re-set seedsReady.current, not just clear the flag.

title: Onboarding asks which hand you sign with and promises "so the camera reads your hands fairly" — the recognizer never reads that answer
problem: `dominantHand` is collected as a mandatory onboarding step and is re-editable in Settings, but nothing in `src/recognizer/` or `CameraTrainer.tsx` ever reads `profile.dominantHand`. The mirror decision comes purely from MediaPipe's per-frame handedness label (`CameraTrainer.tsx:179`). A grep across src shows the field is only ever written (Onboarding, Family, Settings, store) and read once — to paint the selected state of the Settings card.
userImpact: The very first camera-related promise the app makes is false. A left-handed learner who picks "Left" gets identical behaviour to one who picks "Right", and if grading then feels unreliable they have no reason to suspect anything else — they already told the app about their hand. It is also a Settings control that visibly does nothing.
evidence: i18n.ts:26-27 `obHandTitle: "Which hand do you sign with?"`, `obHandSub: "So the camera reads your hands fairly."`; Onboarding.tsx:514-541 writes `hand`; Settings.tsx:184-218 `HandCards` writes `dominantHand`; `grep -rn dominantHand src/` returns no recognizer/camera consumer; CameraTrainer.tsx:179 `const mirror = frame.detectedHand === "Left"`.
proposedFix:
Either wire it in — pass `profile.dominantHand` into `CameraTrainer` and use it as the tie-break when MediaPipe's handedness score is low, and/or as the default when `res.handednesses` is absent (useHandTracker.ts:195-196 currently hard-defaults to "Right") — or, if the geometry genuinely doesn't need it, rewrite `obHandSub` and the Settings copy so they stop claiming a camera effect (e.g. "we'll show demos for your hand"), and only keep the step if something actually consumes it.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The "tie-break when MediaPipe's handedness score is low" option is not implementable as written — useHandTracker.ts:195-196 reads only `categoryName` and FrameInfo (66-71) carries no score, so the score would have to be plumbed through first. The default-when-absent option is a one-liner and works. Given normalize.ts already canonicalises both hands, the honest minimal fix is rewriting obHandSub + the Settings copy so they stop claiming a camera effect.

title: Standalone camera practice kills the camera after every single letter and does not restart it, so each letter needs a manual "Start camera" tap
problem: `CameraTrainer` calls `tracker.stop()` the moment a match confirms (line 289) and again in `finishResult` for self-mark/skip (line 352). `CameraPractice` then remounts the trainer with a new key for the next letter, passing `autoStart={autoStart}` — and `autoStart` is only ever true on the onboarding fast-path (`Onboarding.tsx:338`). Every other entry into the Practise tab (`PractiseChooser.tsx:62`, Settings, lesson end card) routes with `autoStart` undefined.
userImpact: Sign Alif correctly → celebration → the app auto-advances to Ba → the camera is off and the viewport shows the "Start camera" button again. Same after every self-mark. A 28-letter practice run means 28 manual restarts. The Lesson player and Fingerspell both pass `autoStart` and behave differently, so the same screen component feels broken in one place and fine in another.
evidence: CameraTrainer.tsx:289 `tracker.stop(); // release the camera the moment the match confirms`; CameraTrainer.tsx:347-353 `finishResult` also calls `tracker.stop()`; CameraPractice.tsx:153-160 `<CameraTrainer key={...} autoStart={autoStart} />`; App.tsx:157 `autoStart={screen.autoStart}`; PractiseChooser.tsx:62 `go({ name: "camera", targetSignId: "alpha-alif" })` (no autoStart); LessonPlayer.tsx:431 and Fingerspell.tsx:210 both pass `autoStart`.
proposedFix:
In `CameraPractice`, track whether the camera has been started once this session (`const [cameraLive, setCameraLive] = useState(autoStart)`, flipped to true in `handleResult`) and pass `autoStart={cameraLive}`. Do the same for the `choose()` strip taps. The permission is already granted so no new prompt fires.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: `useState(autoStart)` flipped in handleResult has a hole: handleResult also fires for selfMark/skip, which are reachable without the camera ever having been started (CameraTrainer.tsx:564-591 renders self-mark in every state). Flipping on that path would auto-open the camera — and trigger a first permission prompt — for a learner who deliberately never started it. Gate the flip on the trainer actually having run (e.g. only on result === "match", or track tracker status).

title: The three reference-only letters (ة، لا، ال) are offered in the practice strip and open into camera teach-mode, contradicting their own on-screen hint
problem: The letter strip maps over the whole `ALPHABET` (31), including the three edge forms whose `cameraGradable` is false and which the model does not know. Tapping one mounts `CameraTrainer`, where `knowsModel || isTrained(sign.id)` is false, so it opens in teach mode and invites the learner to record 24 samples of a shape the app itself says cannot be graded. `isDemo` is set from `!sign.cameraGradable` and only changes Fanan's pose to "wave" and the mascot line to "Wave with me!" — it does not stop grading.
userImpact: On the same screen the hint card reads "Edge form — reference only; no camera grading yet (awaiting a recorded signer)" while the overlay says "Teach Sawiyya this sign" and then grades the learner against their own recording. Fingerspell handles the identical letter honestly (`fspRefOnly`), so the app contradicts itself between two screens. Nothing is learned: the learner is graded for copying themselves.
evidence: signs.ts:23-30 `hintEn: edge ? "Edge form — reference only; no camera grading yet…"` and `cameraGradable: !edge`; signs.ts:67-69 the three edge letters; CameraPractice.tsx:129 `{ALPHABET.map((s) => (<Chip …>` (unfiltered); CameraTrainer.tsx:76-78 mode defaults to "teach"; CameraTrainer.tsx:366-373 `isDemo = !sign.cameraGradable` only affects pose/copy; Fingerspell.tsx:284-288 shows `fspRefOnly` for the same signs.
proposedFix: Filter the strip to `ALPHABET.filter(s => s.cameraGradable)` and, defensively, make `CameraTrainer` refuse teach mode when `!sign.cameraGradable` — render the reference photo plus the `fspRefOnly` note and the self-mark button instead of the teach overlay.

title: A failure after getUserMedia succeeds (e.g. video.play() rejecting) leaks the live camera stream — the light stays on and it can never be stopped
problem: `start()` assigns `stream.current = media` at line 126 and then awaits `video.play()`. If that rejects (Safari/iOS `AbortError: play() request was interrupted`, hidden document) — or `canvas.getContext` / `new DrawingUtils` throws — control lands in the outer catch, which sets `status: "error"` but never stops the acquired tracks. Worse, the "Try again" button calls `start()` again, which overwrites `stream.current` with a second stream, so the first one is unreachable and survives even the unmount `stop()`.
userImpact: The learner sees "No camera? No problem." while the OS camera indicator is lit, and it stays lit for the rest of the page session. For an app whose core pitch is "nothing leaves your device", a camera that stays on after it says it has no camera is the worst possible signal.
evidence: useHandTracker.ts:126-128 `stream.current = media; video.srcObject = media; await video.play();`; useHandTracker.ts:216-223 the catch sets `running.current = false; setStatus("error"); setError(...)` with no `getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())`. Compare useHandTracker.ts:158-167 `failLoop`, which does stop the tracks.
proposedFix: In the outer catch, before `setStatus("error")`: `stream.current?.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()); stream.current = null;` — and guard the stale-generation branch at line 129-133 so it only nulls `stream.current` when it still points at its own `media`.

title: The "the camera isn't sure" band and the sad mascot latch on permanently, so they contradict a filling hold ring
problem: `setShowUnsure(true)` fires once `attemptFrames` passes 140 and is never set back to false for the rest of the round (the only reset is the teach→grade transition at line 866). `showUnsure` drives both the coral encouragement band and the Fanan pose/mascot line.
userImpact: After roughly five seconds of trying, the learner gets a permanent "Almost — the camera isn't sure, but your hands might be right" card and a sad mascot saying "So close — again!". These stay on screen while the meter reads 100% and the gold hold ring is filling, so the app is discouraging the learner at the exact moment it is confirming them.
evidence: CameraTrainer.tsx:213-214 `attemptFrames.current += 1; if (attemptFrames.current > UNSURE_AFTER_FRAMES) setShowUnsure(true);`; CameraTrainer.tsx:365-384 `pose`/`mascotLine` branch on `showUnsure` ahead of the running/handVisible states; CameraTrainer.tsx:566-575 renders the band under `!matched`; the only `setShowUnsure(false)` is CameraTrainer.tsx:866 inside the teach "done" button.
proposedFix:
Clear it as soon as the learner starts accruing hold time: in the `if (matched)` branch call `setShowUnsure(false)` and reset `attemptFrames.current = 0`. Optionally gate the band on `holdProgress === 0` the same way the coach hint already is (line 551).

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Calling setShowUnsure(false) directly inside the per-frame `if (matched)` branch would push a React state update on every matching frame, breaking the deliberate no-churn discipline this file uses for pushConfidence/pushHold (lines 116-134). Guard it with a ref so it fires once per streak.

title: The gold ▶ button on the reference stage is a decorative span that does nothing, and the trainer has no other way to replay the reference
problem: The reference stage renders a 40px gold circle with a ▶ glyph, hard shadow and all the affordances of a play FAB, but it is a `<span aria-hidden="true">` with no handler. Every other screen that shows the same teal-stripe signer stage has a working replay control (`LessonPlayer.tsx:763-772` "Watch again", Fingerspell's playback controls).
userImpact: The learner taps the obvious play button on the "SIGNER" stage expecting the demo to play and nothing happens — on the one screen where seeing the reference again matters most. It also sets up a false expectation that motion is coming, on a stage that only ever shows a still photo or skeleton.
evidence: CameraTrainer.tsx:459-466 `▶` — no onClick, not a button. Contrast LessonPlayer.tsx:763-772, a real `
proposedFix:
Make it a real `<button>` that re-triggers the reference (bump a `replayKey` on the chip so `animate-pop-in` replays, and play `sign.media` if it ever exists), matching `DemoFace`'s "Watch again" pattern. If there is nothing to replay for letters, delete the glyph rather than leave a fake control.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: It is aria-hidden, so assistive tech is unaffected, and for letters the reference chip is a still photo permanently visible on the same stage — there is literally nothing to replay, so "make it a real button that bumps a replayKey" would only re-run animate-pop-in on an image the learner is already looking at. Deleting the glyph is the correct branch of the proposed fix here.

title: "Reached!" prints next to the live percentage on desktop at all times, including 0%
problem: The `camReached` sublabel is rendered unconditionally inside the meter block; the only gate is `hidden … md:block`, i.e. viewport width, not state.
userImpact: On desktop the meter reads "0% Reached!" from the moment the camera starts, and keeps saying "Reached!" at every value on the way up. It reads as a success claim attached to a failure number, which is precisely the kind of thing that makes the grading feel untrustworthy.
evidence: CameraTrainer.tsx:526-534 — the `{t("camReached", lang)}` sits beside `{formatPercent(meter * 100, lang)}` with no conditional; i18n.ts:85 `camReached: { en: "Reached!" }`.
proposedFix: Wrap it in `{meter >= 1 && ( … )}` (or `holdProgress >= 1`) so it only appears when the hold has actually completed, or replace it with a neutral caption such as the target letter.

title: "Matched your own recording" is shown for matches the bundled seed data actually carried
problem: The KNN fallback used when `userTaughtCount(sign.id) >= 8` is `classifyAgainst`, and `classifyAgainst` spans BOTH stores — `readStores()` returns `[getSeeds(), store()]`, i.e. 1,120 bundled real-signer vectors plus the learner's own. So `k.matched` can be true because the learner's hand landed near a *bundled seed*, yet `ownRecording = knowsModel && !modelMatchedInHold.current` reports it as the learner's own recording.
userImpact: The honest-disclosure line the owner deliberately added ("Matched your own recording") fires on matches that were nothing of the sort, and the same wrong flag is written into the SRS/metrics as `ownRecordingMatches`, which is the number DevMetrics presents as "…of which own-recording (KNN, not model)". A disclosure that is wrong is worse than none.
evidence: knn.ts:46-48 `function readStores(): SampleStore[] { return [getSeeds(), store()]; }`; knn.ts:202 `for (const layer of readStores())`; CameraTrainer.tsx:257-261 `if (userTaughtCount(sign.id) >= 8) { const k = classifyAgainst(vec, sign.id); … matched = matched || k.matched; }`; CameraTrainer.tsx:295 `const ownRecording = knowsModel && !modelMatchedInHold.current;`; DevMetrics.tsx row "…of which own-recording (KNN, not model)".
proposedFix:
Add a user-store-only variant (e.g. `classifyAgainstUser(vec, targetId)` that iterates `[store()]` instead of `readStores()`) and use that for the fallback, or have `classifyAgainst` tag each of the top-K neighbours with its source layer and set `ownRecording` only when the winning weight came predominantly from the user's store.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Severity lowered: the path needs userTaughtCount(sign.id) >= 8 AND every frame of the ~1.2s hold streak to be MLP-rejected (one mlpMatched frame sets modelMatchedInHold), and the consequence is a wrong sub-line plus a dev-only counter. Also, the `classifyAgainstUser` variant is not a drop-in: restricting the top-K to at most 48 own samples changes the neighbourhood the DISTANCE_GATE/MARGIN_GATE were calibrated against (knn.ts:19-27), so it would need re-sweeping. The source-tagging variant is the safe one.

title: One "Camera confidence" number is the max of two incompatible scales (MLP softmax vs KNN vote share)
problem: For a seeded letter with >=8 taught samples the meter takes `Math.max(MLP targetP, KNN targetShare)`. Those are different quantities with different thresholds — the MLP confirms at `MODEL_TAU = 0.5` (classifier.ts:32, model tau 0.5), the KNN at `TAU = 0.70` plus a 0.15 margin. The match card then prints whichever number happened to be larger under the single label "Camera confidence".
userImpact: The percentage jumps discontinuously as the two graders trade places, and the value at which it confirms changes depending on which grader won — 50% on one frame, 70% on another. The learner has no stable mental model of "how close am I", which is the whole job of that meter.
evidence: CameraTrainer.tsx:257-261 `const k = classifyAgainst(vec, sign.id); if (k.confidence > confidence) confidence = k.confidence; matched = matched || k.matched;`; classifier.ts:32 `export const MODEL_TAU = typeof tau === "number" ? tau : 0.5` (bundled model tau is 0.5); knn.ts:277 `export const TAU = 0.70`; CameraTrainer.tsx:930-936 prints `formatPercent(confidence * 100)` under `camConfidence`.
proposedFix:
Normalise before combining: display `Math.min(1, Math.max(targetP / MODEL_TAU, knnShare / TAU))` as a single "progress to confirm" value (1.0 = confirms), or keep the MLP softmax as the sole meter and let the KNN act only as a boolean confirm. Relabel the number to match whichever you pick.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Only reachable for learners who taught >=8 own samples of a seeded letter, so the affected population is small — hence low. More importantly the proposed normalisation is incomplete on its own: `Math.min(1, Math.max(targetP/MODEL_TAU, knnShare/TAU))` would read 100% on exactly the OOD-rejected frames from cam-ood-meter-lies and still refuse to confirm, making that finding worse. Fix the OOD gate first, then normalise.

title: "Re-teach" wipes existing training immediately, has no cancel back to grading, and appears to do nothing when the camera hasn't started
problem: Three problems in one control. (a) The link is only rendered while `mode === "grade"`, and clicking it sets `mode = "teach"`; the teach overlay is gated on `tracker.status !== "idle" && !== "error"` (line 814), so on the Practise tab — where the camera starts idle — the click makes the link vanish and produces no visible UI. (b) Once in teach mode there is no cancel: the only route back to grading is capturing all 24 samples and pressing "Now you try". (c) `startTeach` calls `clearClass(sign.id)` before a single sample exists, so an accidental start followed by leaving the screen destroys previously recorded training and leaves the class below the 8-sample floor the fallback needs.
userImpact: Tapping "Re-teach" on a letter the model already grades either does nothing visible, or traps the learner in a 24-sample recording session for a letter that never needed teaching, having already deleted whatever they had recorded before.
evidence: CameraTrainer.tsx:500-511 the button, rendered only under `mode === "grade"`; CameraTrainer.tsx:814 `{mode === "teach" && tracker.status !== "idle" && tracker.status !== "error" && (` gates the whole overlay; CameraTrainer.tsx:340-345 `const startTeach = () => { clearClass(sign.id); … }`; knn.ts:145-149 `clearClass` deletes and saves immediately; the only `setMode("grade")` is CameraTrainer.tsx:867 inside the teach-done button.
proposedFix:
Render the teach intro even when the tracker is idle/error (with the existing "Start camera" CTA inside it), add a "Cancel" that calls `setMode("grade")`, and move `clearClass` from `startTeach` to the first `addSample` call so an abandoned session cannot destroy prior training.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Two of the three sub-claims are substantially mitigated and the severity should reflect that. (a) is transient, not dead: the idle overlay's "Start camera" button (lines 712-720) is still on screen, and starting the camera reveals the teach intro — the only visible change on the tap is the link disappearing. (b) the learner is not trapped: the self-mark and skip buttons at lines 564-591 render whenever !matched, teach mode included, so finishResult is always one tap away; and in CameraPractice re-tapping any strip chip remounts into grade mode. The genuinely unmitigated part is (c) — clearClass firing before the first addSample, so an abandoned session destroys prior training and drops the class under the >=8 floor the fallback needs. Scope the fix to that plus a Cancel.

title: A MediaPipe wasm/model load failure is reported to the learner as "No camera? No problem."
problem: `start()` awaits `getLandmarker()` before touching the camera. Any failure there — wasm fetch failure, the GPU delegate refusing to initialise, a corrupted precache — is a plain Error, so `classifyError` buckets it as `"other"` and the UI renders the single blocked-camera panel. `errorKind` is computed and stored but the UI never branches on it (it is only printed behind `?debug`). There is also no CPU-delegate fallback for `delegate: "GPU"`.
userImpact: A learner whose camera works perfectly is told they have no camera, and is offered "Browse signs" as if the fix were hardware they don't have. On the devices most likely to fail the GPU delegate (older Android, locked-down browsers) that is the entire camera feature silently mislabelled.
evidence: useHandTracker.ts:113 `const landmarker = await getLandmarker();` inside the same try as getUserMedia; useHandTracker.ts:41 `baseOptions: { modelAssetPath: MODEL_URL, delegate: "GPU" }` with no fallback; useHandTracker.ts:58-64 `classifyError` returns "other" for anything that isn't a DOMException; CameraTrainer.tsx:727-754 renders `stNoCamTitle`/`stNoCamBody` for every `status === "error"`, with `tracker.errorKind` used only in the `DEBUG` block at line 748-752.
proposedFix:
Split the error panel on `errorKind`: "denied" gets permission copy, "notfound" gets the current no-camera copy, "other" gets a load-failure message plus a Retry (which already works — `getLandmarker` nulls `landmarkerPromise` on failure). Add a `delegate: "CPU"` retry inside `getLandmarker`'s catch before giving up.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The mislabelling is broader than the finding states and the fix should cover it: errorKind "denied" (a refused permission prompt, classifyError line 60) also gets "No camera? No problem." today, which is the most common of the three. Note too that the existing "Try again" button cannot re-prompt after a hard denial, so the denied branch must point at the browser's site-settings rather than offer a retry.

title: If the camera track ends mid-session the UI stays "running / Hand detected" forever on a frozen frame
problem: The rAF loop only calls `onFrame` when `video.currentTime !== lastVideoTime`. When the underlying track ends or is muted — USB webcam unplugged, another app grabs the camera, OS privacy toggle, laptop lid/wake — `currentTime` stops advancing, so `onFrame` is never called with either a frame or null. Nothing listens for `track.onended`, `track.onmute`, or `visibilitychange` (a grep for those tokens in this file returns nothing).
userImpact: The viewport freezes on the last frame, the status pill keeps saying "Hand detected", the FPS pill keeps ticking (it counts rAF, not video frames), and the confidence meter holds its last value indefinitely. Nothing in the app ever tells the learner the camera died, and the hold state is left mid-flight because the non-match reset path also never runs.
evidence: useHandTracker.ts:178-202 `if (video.currentTime !== lastVideoTime) { … onFrameRef.current(...) }` — the else path outside that `if` does nothing; useHandTracker.ts:207-213 `frames += 1; … setFps(...)` runs unconditionally, so FPS keeps reporting; no `onended`/`onmute`/`visibilitychange` listener exists anywhere in the file.
proposedFix: After acquiring `media`, attach `media.getVideoTracks()[0].addEventListener("ended"|"mute", …)` to call `failLoop`/`stop` with an honest status, and add a watchdog in the loop: if `video.currentTime` has not advanced for >2000 ms while `running.current`, treat it as device loss (stop the tracks, set an error state with retry) rather than spinning silently.

title: Practise tab: the camera shuts off and needs a manual restart after every match and every letter tap
problem: CameraPractice force-remounts CameraTrainer via `key={`${signId}-${round}`}` after every match (line 83), every skip (line 50) and every letter-chip tap (line 95), but passes through the route's `autoStart`, which is `false` for every entry point except onboarding. On match the trainer calls `tracker.stop()` (CameraTrainer.tsx:289) and the fresh instance mounts with `tracker.status === "idle"`, so the "Start camera" overlay covers the viewport again.
userImpact: On the Practise tab the learner signs Alif, gets the celebration, the app auto-advances to Ba — and the camera is dead. They must tap "Start camera" again for every single letter, and again every time they tap a different letter in the strip. The 2026-08-01 auto-advance feature lands the learner on a black viewport.
evidence: src/screens/CameraPractice.tsx:154-159 `<CameraTrainer key={`${signId}-${round}`} ... autoStart={autoStart} />`; :22 `autoStart = false` default; :83 and :95 `setRound((r) => r + 1)`. Every caller except Onboarding omits autoStart: PractiseChooser.tsx:62 `go({ name: "camera", targetSignId: "alpha-alif" })`, Home.tsx:353/487/509, AllSigns.tsx:167, FlagPicker.tsx:326. App.tsx:157 `autoStart={screen.autoStart}` → undefined. CameraTrainer.tsx:289 `tracker.stop()` on confirm; :317-320 the start effect only fires `if (autoStart)`.
proposedFix:
In CameraPractice pass `autoStart={autoStart || round > 0}` to CameraTrainer. `round` only ever increments from a user gesture inside the screen (match, skip, chip tap), so the browser's user-activation and camera-permission requirements are already satisfied and getUserMedia will not re-prompt. Fingerspell.tsx:210 and LessonPlayer's CameraDrill already pass `autoStart` unconditionally, which is why only this screen is affected.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: `autoStart={autoStart || round > 0}` works as described, but note the side effect: tapping a letter chip before ever starting the camera would now trigger getUserMedia (and a first-time permission prompt) without the learner asking for it. Gate on a "camera was running" ref instead, or accept that and say so.

title: Progress streak grid and heatmap read UTC dates while the store writes local dates
problem: `dayKey(back)` builds its key with `d.toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (UTC), but every key written into `profile.activeDays` comes from `todayKey()` in the store, which uses local `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate`. The two disagree whenever the local date and the UTC date differ.
userImpact: A learner in New York who practises at 8pm sees today's dot in the Weekly Streak as "missed" (dashed coral) immediately after finishing a session, and the whole 7-day row is shifted one day off. In Doha (UTC+3) the same happens for anyone practising between midnight and 3am. The month heatmap is shifted identically.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:49-53 `function dayKey(back) { ... return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10); }` vs src/store/app.ts:33-38 `todayKey` using `d.getFullYear()/getMonth()/getDate()`, written at app.ts:412 `activeDays: newDay ? [...p.activeDays, today].slice(-90)`. Verified by running both: `TZ=America/New_York` at 20:31 local → `todayKey()` = 2026-07-31, `dayKey(0)` = 2026-08-01, no match. `TZ=Asia/Qatar` at 03:31 → match (breaks below 03:00). Consumers: Progress.tsx:99-111 (`week`) and :115-118 (`heat`).
proposedFix:
Export `todayKey` from src/store/app.ts (already exported) and rewrite Progress's helper as `function dayKey(back: number) { const d = new Date(); d.setDate(d.getDate() - back); return todayKey(d); }`. `todayKey` already accepts a Date argument. Delete the local `dayKey` implementation. Add a test that pins TZ to America/New_York at 20:00 and asserts the today cell is `active` after a recorded drill.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Fix is right (todayKey already takes a Date, app.ts:33). Severity is lower than stated for this app's actual audiences: in Qatar (UTC+3) the mismatch window is 00:00 to 03:00 local, in UK summer 00:00 to 01:00, and only the dot grid and heatmap are wrong. The streak number itself is correct because streakFor uses todayKey (app.ts:659-663).

title: Onboarding "Skip" throws away every answer already given, including the Deaf persona
problem: `finish({ skipAll: true })` hardcodes `role: "parent"`, `dominantHand: "R"` and `dailyGoal: "regular"`, ignoring the `persona`, `hand` and `goal` state the user already set. The Skip button renders on every step from "meet" onward (9 of the 10 steps), so tapping it on the reminders step — where it reads as "skip the rest" — silently discards work already done.
userImpact: A Deaf user who picks "I'm Deaf — setting up my family" (the app's whole structural thesis) and then taps Skip is stored as `role: "parent"`. They lose flag ownership rights, their flagging no longer marks their active day, and they get counted into the hearing-only household streak and shared board. A left-handed learner who picked Left is stored as Right, which the camera guidance depends on.
evidence: src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:125-141 `finish` — `role: overrides?.skipAll ? "parent" : persona, dominantHand: overrides?.skipAll ? "R" : hand, dailyGoal: overrides?.skipAll ? "regular" : goal`. Skip button at :238-245 renders for `step !== "splash"`. Consequences of role: src/store/app.ts:507 `canDeactivate = existing.raisedByProfileId === byProfileId || by?.role === "deaf"`, :569 deaf-only streak credit, :716 and :740 hearing-only board/streak filters.
proposedFix:
Delete the `skipAll` overrides from src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:132-135 and call `createProfile` with the live `persona`/`hand`/`goal` state. Those state variables already hold the correct defaults (`parent`/`R`/`regular`) for steps the user never reached, so Skip still means "use defaults for what I haven't answered" — it just stops overwriting what they did answer. `overrides.skipAll` can then be removed entirely.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Drop the handedness half of the impact claim: dominantHand is inert everywhere except the Settings toggle that writes it (grep shows only types.ts:14, Settings.tsx:191-196, Family.tsx:93, Onboarding.tsx:133, app.ts). CameraTrainer canonicalises both hands itself (CameraTrainer.tsx:179), so no camera guidance depends on it. The role loss is the whole defect. The code fix as written is correct.

title: The full-screen streak celebration can never fire
problem: `lastStreak` is initialised with `useRef(profile.streak)` on mount, and the effect only sets `celebrating` when `profile.streak > lastStreak.current`. On mount the two are equal, and `profile.streak` can only increase inside `recordDrillResult` / `toggleFlag`, which are exclusively called from LessonPlayer, CameraPractice, FirstSign, Fingerspell, Words, AllSigns and FlagPicker — none of which are mounted at the same time as Progress (App.tsx renders exactly one screen). So the condition is never true.
userImpact: The confetti/streak takeover — a fully built ~130-line screen with its own focus trap, Confetti burst and copy — is dead UI that no user will ever see. The streak payoff the product promises simply doesn't happen.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:124-132 `const lastStreak = useRef(profile.streak); useEffect(() => { if (profile.streak > lastStreak.current && profile.streak > 1) setCelebrating(true); lastStreak.current = profile.streak; }, [profile.streak]);` and :235-244 the render gate. App.tsx:149-189 renders one screen per `screen.name`, so Progress unmounts before any drill screen mounts. `useDialog`, `Confetti` and `celebrate()` are all wired up at Progress.tsx:880-884.
proposedFix:
Persist the last celebrated streak instead of a per-mount ref: add `celebratedStreak: number` to Profile (defaulting via `finiteOr(pr.celebratedStreak, 0)` in normalizePersisted), set it when the celebration is dismissed, and fire on mount when `streakFor(profile) > profile.celebratedStreak && streakFor(profile) > 1`. That makes the celebration show the first time the learner opens Progress after extending a streak, which is the intended moment.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Fix approach is sound. Severity is low: nothing breaks and the learner never knows a celebration was intended; the cost is a missing payoff, not a broken flow.

title: The "7-day streak" achievement un-earns itself when the learner lapses
problem: AchievementsTab receives `streak={streakFor(profile)}`, the read-time derived streak, which returns 0 as soon as `lastActiveDay` is neither today nor yesterday. The badge's earned test is `streak >= 7`, so a learner who reached a 12-day streak and then missed two days loses the badge, and the header summary count drops.
userImpact: A learner who built a 12-day streak, missed a weekend, and opens Achievements sees the 7-day badge greyed back out and the summary drop from "3 of 6" to "2 of 6". Achievements are supposed to be permanent records of what happened; this one narrates a past event from a live counter.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:121 `const streak = streakFor(profile);`, :215-222 `<AchievementsTab ... streak={streak} ... />`, :606 `{ glyph: "🔥", name: t("prAch7Day", lang), status: t("prUnlocked", lang), earned: streak >= 7 }`, :622 `const earnedCount = items.filter((a) => a.earned).length;`. src/store/app.ts:659-663 `streakFor` returns `0` unless `lastActiveDay` is today or yesterday. (The neighbouring Stats tile is correctly labelled — i18n.ts:325 `prBestStreak: { en: "Current streak" }` — so only the achievement is wrong.)
proposedFix:
Add a `bestStreak: number` field to Profile, updated in `recordDrillResult` (`bestStreak: Math.max(p.bestStreak ?? 0, streak)`) and backfilled in `normalizePersisted` with `finiteOr(pr.bestStreak, finiteOr(pr.streak, 0))`. Feed AchievementsTab `bestStreak` while the Stats "Current streak" tile keeps `streakFor`.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Fix is correct. Severity is low: it affects one badge tile and the "n of 6" line inside the Achievements tab, with no effect on progress, scheduling or navigation.

title: A profile can be created but never deleted, and one stray member permanently zeroes the household streak and shared board
problem: AppState exposes `createProfile`, `switchProfile` and `updateProfile` but no delete, and Family's member row is add-only. `householdStreak` requires *every* hearing profile to have been active on each day, and `signsAllCanDo` is a strict intersection over every hearing profile's mastered set — so any profile added by mistake or for a one-off test is a permanent member of both computations.
userImpact: A parent taps "Add a family member", types a name to try it out, and the household streak drops to 0 and the "Signs we can all do" honeycomb empties — permanently, with no UI anywhere to undo it. The only recovery is the ErrorBoundary's "reset all app data", which wipes the entire household.
evidence: src/store/app.ts:64-72 (the AppState action surface — no remove/delete); src/screens/Family.tsx:88-99 `addMember` with no counterpart; src/screens/Family.tsx:133-185 renders the member row with only a switch handler and an add tile. src/store/app.ts:739-753 `householdStreak` — `daySets.every((set) => set.has(key))`; :715-734 `signsAllCanDo` — `[...first].filter((id) => rest.every((set) => set.has(id)))`.
proposedFix: Add `removeProfile: (id: string) => void` to the store: drop the profile from `profiles`, delete `progress[id]` and `srs[id]`, drop flags where `raisedByProfileId === id` and strip the id from every flag's `supporters`, and reassign `activeProfileId` to `profiles[0]?.id ?? null` if the removed profile was active. Surface it in Family.tsx behind a long-press or an edit affordance on the member tile with a `window.confirm`, matching the existing reset-training confirm pattern in Settings.tsx:74-92.

title: A soft-failed camera drill is recorded twice, inflating the honesty counters the app markets as honest
problem: After 20 seconds of hand-visible time without a match, CameraTrainer fires `onSoftFail`, and both LessonPlayer's CameraDrill and CameraPractice respond with a full `recordDrillResult(signId, "again", { camera: true, matched: false })`. When the learner then succeeds, `handleResult` records a second full drill result for the same attempt. `metrics.drillsCompleted` and `metrics.cameraAttempts` both increment twice for one physical attempt, while `cameraMatches` increments once.
userImpact: The Progress → Stats "Avg accuracy" tile and DevMetrics "Camera match rate" read 50% for a drill the learner actually got right, and "Drills completed" double-counts. In CameraPractice the soft fail refires on every remount, so a learner struggling with one letter adds one drill + one camera attempt every 20 seconds.
evidence: src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:399-402 `handleSoftFail` → `recordDrillResult(sign.id, "again", { camera: true, matched: false })` and :411-416 `handleResult` → `recordDrillResult(...)`; identical pair in src/screens/CameraPractice.tsx:56-61 and :89-90, and src/screens/FirstSign.tsx:83-98. src/store/app.ts:426-435 `drillsCompleted: s.metrics.drillsCompleted + 1` then `if (opts.camera) { metrics.cameraAttempts += 1; ... }`. Consumed at src/screens/Progress.tsx:543-551 and src/screens/DevMetrics.tsx:12-13.
proposedFix:
Give `recordDrillResult` an explicit `softFail?: boolean` option that rates the FSRS card and awards XP as today but skips the `drillsCompleted`/`cameraAttempts` increments (app.ts:426-431) — the eventual `handleResult` call is the one that closes the attempt. Pass `{ softFail: true }` from the three `handleSoftFail` sites. If the intent really is to count each 20-second window as an attempt, then `cameraMatches` needs the same treatment so the ratio stays meaningful.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The claim that CameraPractice refires the soft fail every 20 seconds is false: CameraTrainer.tsx:110 and :218-233 fire it once per mount (softFailFired latches), and handleSoftFail does not bump round, so no remount happens while the learner keeps struggling on the same letter. Counting a 20-second hand-visible non-match as a camera attempt is also defensible rather than clearly wrong; the unambiguous inaccuracy is drillsCompleted counting one drill twice, so fix that increment and leave the attempt accounting as a product call.

title: Alphabet progress counts 31 letters against a denominator of 28, so "Whole alphabet" can unlock with real letters unlearned
problem: `alphaLit` filters the full `ALPHABET` array, which holds 31 entries — the 28 seeded letters plus the three non-gradable edge forms ة / لا / ال. The resulting `alphaTaught` is then rendered against a hardcoded 28 in the achievement, against `ALPHABET.length` (31) in the Constellation badge, and against 28 again in AllSigns. The three denominators disagree and the numerator can exceed 28.
userImpact: A learner who touched the edge forms (reachable via "Add to Daily Review" in the dictionary, or by flagging ة) sees the achievement read "31 / 28", and can unlock the "Whole alphabet" badge while three real letters are still unlearned. Progress's Constellation and AllSigns' alphabet bar disagree with the badge for the same learner.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:79-82 `const alphaLit = new Set(ALPHABET.filter((s) => (prog[s.id]?.masteryLevel ?? 0) >= 1).map((s) => s.id)); const alphaTaught = alphaLit.size;` — `ALPHABET` is 31 entries (src/content/signs.ts:38-70, three built with `edge = true`). Rendered at Progress.tsx:618 `${toLocaleDigits(alphaTaught, lang)} / ${toLocaleDigits(28, lang)}` and :620 `earned: alphaTaught >= 28`, and at :778 `{num(alphaTaught, lang)} / {num(ALPHABET.length, lang)}`. Same defect at src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:149-152. The milestone ladder already guards against exactly this substitution (src/lesson/milestones.ts:25-27, tested at src/lesson/milestones.test.ts:72-85) — only the Progress/AllSigns surfaces missed it.
proposedFix:
Export the already-computed `SEEDED_ALPHABET` (src/content/signs.ts:169) from content/signs.ts and use it for both the numerator and the denominator: `ALPHABET.filter(s => s.cameraGradable)` in Progress.tsx:79 and AllSigns.tsx:149-152, and `SEEDED_ALPHABET.length` in place of the hardcoded 28 and `ALPHABET.length` at Progress.tsx:618/620/778.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Two corrections to the fix: SEEDED_ALPHABET at signs.ts:169 is currently module-private, so it must be exported before use; and the "Add to Daily Review" route named in the evidence does not itself set mastery (app.ts:476-488 seeds an SRS card only), so cite the Practise-tab chip strip or the resulting review drill as the reproduction path.

title: Finishing every lesson makes the path's first node pulse "START" again instead of showing done
problem: `nextLesson` falls back to `LESSONS[0]` when no lesson has an unmastered sign, and the node status ternary checks `lesson.id === nextLesson.id` *before* `complete`. So once every lesson is complete, lesson 1 renders as the coral, pulse-ringed "current" node with the START badge and Fanan cheering beside it.
userImpact: A learner who has finished the whole path is told to start Lesson 1 again, with no signal that they completed anything — the trail shows one "current" node and seven done nodes, and the bottom sheet offers "Start" rather than "Review".
evidence: src/screens/Home.tsx:98-99 `const nextLesson = LESSONS.find((l) => l.signIds.some((id) => (prog[id]?.masteryLevel ?? 0) < 2)) ?? LESSONS[0];` and :108-113 `const status = lesson.id === nextLesson.id ? "current" : complete ? "done" : "locked";`. Consumed by the pulse ring at :188-190, the START badge at :319-323 and the sheet CTA at :575-576.
proposedFix: Let `nextLesson` be `undefined` when everything is complete (`const nextLesson = LESSONS.find(...)`), guard the unit banner with `nextLesson ?? LESSONS[0]`, and reorder the status ternary to `complete ? "done" : lesson.id === nextLesson?.id ? "current" : "locked"`. With no current node the trail reads as fully done and the milestone/review cards below already carry the next action.

title: Editing the display name re-serialises the whole household to localStorage on every keystroke, and accepts an empty name
problem: The name input writes `updateProfile(profile.id, { displayName })` on every `onChange`. zustand's persist wraps every `set()` with a `setItem()` that runs `JSON.stringify` over the entire state — all profiles, every SRS card, every progress record, all flags and metrics — synchronously on the keystroke. The field also has no non-empty validation, unlike Family's add-member flow.
userImpact: Typing a 15-character name performs 15 full serialisations of the household blob on the main thread; on an older phone with a full SRS deck that is visible input lag. Clearing the field entirely leaves the profile with an empty name, so Home greets "Marhaba, " and the avatar renders the "•" placeholder, with no way to tell the user something is wrong.
evidence: src/screens/Settings.tsx:150-158 `<input value={profile.displayName} onChange={(e) => set({ displayName: e.target.value })} />` → :69-70 `app.updateProfile(profile.id, patch)` → src/store/app.ts:351-354. node_modules/zustand/esm/middleware.mjs:465-483 — `config((...args) => { set(...args); void setItem(); })` and `setItem` = `storage.setItem(options.name, { state: options.partialize({ ...get() }), version })` with the default identity `partialize`. Empty-name rendering at src/screens/Home.tsx:140 `profile.displayName.trim().charAt(0) || "•"` and :259 `<bdi>{profile.displayName}</bdi>`. Contrast src/screens/Family.tsx:89 `if (!newName.trim()) return;`.
proposedFix:
Hold the name in local component state and commit to the store on `blur` and on Enter, falling back to the previous name when the trimmed value is empty — the same non-empty rule Family already applies. That reduces the write to one per edit and removes the empty-name state entirely.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Drop the performance half of the rationale: the persisted blob is a handful of profiles plus at most 47 signs of progress and SRS per profile, so a stringify per keystroke is sub-millisecond and not observable input lag. The defect worth fixing is the empty name; commit-on-blur with a trimmed non-empty fallback covers it.

title: Dictionary detail sheet has no max-height or scroll — its top (close button, demo frame) is clipped off-screen on phones
problem: The mobile bottom-sheet panel is `fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0 … p-6 pb-10` with no `max-h` and no `overflow-y-auto`. `DetailPanel` renders a full-width `aspect-square` demo frame (~342px on a 390px viewport) plus header row, title, tag row, hint block and 2–3 action buttons — roughly 800px of content. Anchored to `bottom-0`, the panel grows upward past the top of the viewport and nothing scrolls it back.
userImpact: On any phone the close button and the whole sign demonstration are pushed above the top of the screen and cannot be reached — the user sees a sheet that starts mid-image with no visible way to dismiss it except tapping the backdrop. `useDialog` also sends initial focus to that off-screen close button, so a keyboard/screen-reader user lands somewhere invisible. The Words screen sheet, which does this correctly, is right there for comparison.
evidence: src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:373-380 `<div ref={sheetRef} role="dialog" … className="fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0 z-50 animate-rise rounded-t-3xl bg-paper p-6 pb-10 shadow-lift focus:outline-none">` — no max-height, no overflow. Contrast src/screens/Words.tsx:115 which uses `max-h-[88dvh] … overflow-y-auto`. The tall child is src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:620-658, `className="relative mb-6 flex aspect-square w-full …"`.
proposedFix:
Match the Words sheet: add `max-h-[88dvh] overflow-y-auto` to the panel at AllSigns.tsx:379 (and `overscroll-contain` so the page behind doesn't scroll). Wrap the mobile branch in the same flex-centred fixed wrapper Words uses so the panel can never exceed the viewport, and keep the close button in the first scroll position.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The fix is right, but note the escape hatches it implies are missing already exist: the backdrop button (AllSigns.tsx:367-372) and useDialog's Escape handler both dismiss the sheet, so this clips content rather than trapping the user.

title: The Dictionary's Watch / play / "Watch & practise" buttons do nothing at all
problem: `handleWatch` is `const handleWatch = () => setWatched(true)` (line 568). Three separate controls call it: the centred "Watch" chip (line 639), the gold play FAB (line 649) and — for every non-camera-gradable sign — the primary "Watch & practise" CTA (line 724). The demo frame they sit on is a static `SignGlyph` medallion with no key, no video, no animation, so pressing any of them changes only the chip's own label from "Watch" to "Watch Again".
userImpact: A learner opens a sign, taps the big gold play button expecting to see the sign demonstrated, and nothing happens — repeatedly. For the 19 watch-only word signs, "Watch & practise" is the *only* offered action on the screen and it is inert, so the detail panel is a dead end. This is exactly the kind of "controls that do nothing" that makes the app read as broken.
evidence: src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:566-568 `// Watch is a pure preview … const handleWatch = () => setWatched(true);`; consumers at :641, :651, :724. The medallion at :631-636 has no `key={…}` and no animation class, unlike LessonPlayer's `DemoFace` (src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:702-712) where `replayKey` actually remounts an `animate-pop-in` node.
proposedFix:
Give the medallion a `key={replayKey}` + `animate-pop-in` so a replay is visible (the LessonPlayer `DemoFace` pattern), and reuse the existing `SignDemo` component here instead of a bare `SignGlyph` so `sign.media` / `sign.photo` actually play. Drop the duplicate gold play FAB (:649) so there is one Watch affordance. For non-gradable signs, make the primary CTA the replay, not a second copy of it.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Swapping in SignDemo only fixes the 31 letters (they have `photo`, so the `key={replayKey}` branch at SignDemo.tsx:55-72 pops on replay). For the 19 A1 words SignDemo hits `demoShowsHint()` and suppresses its own replay button (SignDemo.tsx:12-14, :141), so 'Watch & practise' would still have nothing to do — the honest fix for those is to drop or relabel that CTA, or route it to the Words.tsx watch → self-mark sheet, not to add a replay.

title: The "Watch" type badge is 2.28:1 — unreadable, and it is on every non-graded sign card
problem: `TypeBadge` hardcodes `{ backgroundColor: "#FBEFE6", color: "#C89A3D" }` for the non-gradable branch. Measured contrast is 2.28:1 on 9px bold uppercase text — WCAG AA for small text is 4.5:1. The project already fixed exactly this colour once: tailwind.config.js:12-15 documents "#C89A3D on sand was 2.26:1 … #7F621F holds the same gold hue at 5.01:1", but this inline hex bypassed the token.
userImpact: The honest "Watch" vs "Graded" signal — the thing telling a learner whether the camera can actually grade a sign — is effectively invisible on every word-sign card and in every detail panel. Anyone with reduced contrast sensitivity, or anyone outdoors, cannot read it.
evidence: src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:62-70 `style={ gradable ? { backgroundColor: "#E6F0EE", color: "#0F6E6A" } : { backgroundColor: "#FBEFE6", color: "#C89A3D" } }`. Computed: #C89A3D on #FBEFE6 = 2.28:1. The teal branch (#0F6E6A on #E6F0EE) passes at ~5.4:1, so only the gold branch is broken.
proposedFix:
Change the non-gradable branch to the AA-tuned token: `color: "#7F621F"` (`gold-deep`) on `#FBEFE6` → ~5.0:1. Better, replace both inline style objects with Tailwind token classes (`bg-teal/10 text-teal` / `bg-gold/15 text-gold-deep`) so future palette changes carry.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Fix is sound. One addition: the `bg-gold/20 text-teal-deep` tag at :676 and the teal branch both pass, so only the one hex pair needs changing.

title: Progress tab renders its headline numbers in raw gold hex at 1.7–2.4:1
problem: Several live stat values are painted with literal hex that bypasses the AA-tuned `gold-deep` token: "palms grown" uses `style={{ color: "#E6B24C" }}` (1.81:1 on paper), "Drills completed" uses `color: "#C89A3D"` (2.41:1), and `ForecastRow`'s due badge uses `text-gold` on `bg-gold/10` (1.71:1). Even the large-text AA threshold is 3:1; these are all below it.
userImpact: The numbers that are the entire point of the Progress screen — palms grown, drills completed, the "Review due" badge on each forecast row — read as faint yellow smudges on the cream background. On a phone in daylight they are gone.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:377 `<div className="font-display text-[24px] font-extrabold leading-none" style={{ color: "#E6B24C" }}>`; :550 `{ … color: "#C89A3D" }` for `prDrillsDone`; :849 `tone === "due" ? "bg-gold/10 text-gold" : …`. Measured against `paper` #FBF7EF: 1.81 / 2.41 / 1.71. tailwind.config.js:12-15 already defines `gold.deep = #7F621F` at 5.36:1 on paper for precisely this reason.
proposedFix: Swap all three to the token: `className="text-gold-deep"` (drop the inline `style` colour at :377 and :550, change `text-gold` → `text-gold-deep` at :849). Keep `#E6B24C` only for fills/strokes (rings, bars), never for text.

title: In Arabic every dictionary card prints the same word twice ("ا · ا", "مرحبا · مرحبا")
problem: The card and detail titles render `{pick(lang, glossEn, glossAr)}` followed by `· {sign.code ? sign.code : sign.glossAr}`. For alphabet signs `glossAr === code` (src/content/signs.ts:21 `glossAr: code`), and A1 word signs have no `code` at all, so the fallback is `glossAr` again. In the Arabic UI both halves resolve to the same string.
userImpact: An Arabic reader — the app's primary audience — sees every one of the 31 letters and 19 words rendered as "ا · ا" / "سلام · سلام" on the Dictionary grid and again in the detail heading. It looks like a rendering bug and wastes the card's whole title line.
evidence: src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:502-505 `{label} · {sign.code ? sign.code : sign.glossAr}` where `label = pick(lang, sign.glossEn, sign.glossAr)` (:476); same pattern at :663-666. Content model: src/content/signs.ts:21 `glossAr: code` for every letter, and src/content/signs.ts:87 `S = (…) => ({ id, tier: "A1", glossEn, glossAr, … })` — no `code` field on words.
proposedFix: Render the *other* language as the secondary, the way Words.tsx:214-216 already does: `const secondary = pick(lang === "ar" ? "en" : "ar", sign.glossEn, sign.glossAr)`, then only emit the `· secondary` span when `secondary !== label`. Apply at both :504 and :665.

title: Locked achievement names and statuses render at 1.84:1 — four of six tiles are unreadable
problem: Locked achievement tiles combine `opacity: 0.72` on the container with `color: "#94A5A2"` for the name and a flat `text-[#94A5A2]` for the status line. #94A5A2 on paper is already 2.41:1; composited through 0.72 opacity over the sand page it lands at ~1.84:1. Text is 13px bold and 10px, so AA needs 4.5:1.
userImpact: On a fresh install only "First sign" is unlocked, so five of six achievement tiles show a grey blob with a name nobody can read. The screen looks corrupted rather than aspirational, and no user can find out what the locked achievements even are.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:636-661 — `style={{ … opacity: a.earned ? 1 : 0.72 }}` on the tile, `style={{ color: a.earned ? "#16302E" : "#94A5A2" }}` on the name (:657), `className="… text-[#94A5A2]"` on the status (:661). Measured: #94A5A2 on #FBF7EF = 2.41:1; blended at 0.72 over #F6EFE3 = 1.84:1.
proposedFix:
Drop the container `opacity` (keep the dashed border + `grayscale` filter on the glyph as the locked signal) and use the `muted` token (#566B68, 4.97:1 on sand) for both the locked name and the status line. Reserve #94A5A2 for non-text decoration only.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Incomplete as written: the status line at :661 uses #94A5A2 unconditionally, so EARNED tiles are also failing at 2.41:1 on paper. Both branches of :661 need the token, not just the locked one.

title: The alphabet Constellation grid is hard-locked to `dir="ltr"`, so the Arabic alphabet reads backwards
problem: `<div className="grid grid-cols-5 gap-4" dir="ltr">` forces the 31-letter grid to flow left-to-right even in the Arabic UI, placing Alif top-left and the numbered locked nodes 1→5 across from the left. Every other alphabet surface in the app deliberately does the opposite: CameraPractice.tsx:122-128 carries a comment explaining that the strip must be `dir="rtl"` "so the strip starts at Alif", and Fingerspell.tsx:161/:217 do the same.
userImpact: An Arabic-reading learner scanning their alphabet progress reads the letters in the wrong order — the sequence they know as starting at the top-right starts at the top-left, and the lit/unlit pattern of their progress traces backwards. It directly contradicts the strip on the Practise screen.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:781 `<div className="grid grid-cols-5 gap-4" dir="ltr">` wrapping `ALPHABET.map(...)`; inner lit cells even re-declare `dir="rtl"` on the glyph span (:797), showing the outer LTR was not intentional for content order. Compare src/screens/CameraPractice.tsx:128 `<div dir="rtl" className="no-scrollbar … overflow-x-auto …">` with its explaining comment at :122-126.
proposedFix: Remove `dir="ltr"` from Progress.tsx:781 and let the grid inherit the document direction (or set `dir="rtl"` explicitly, matching CameraPractice). Drop the now-redundant `dir="rtl"` on the inner span at :797.

title: The streak celebration shows Latin day initials M T W T F S S in the Arabic UI
problem: `StreakCelebration` renders the week dots with an inline `["M","T","W","T","F","S","S"]` array and wraps the row in `dir="ltr"`, ignoring the localized `DAY_LABELS_AR` constant that the very same file defines at line 44 and uses correctly in the Oasis tab (line 417).
userImpact: The app's biggest celebratory moment — a full-screen takeover after a streak milestone — shows an Arabic learner seven English letters in left-to-right order, when the weekly streak card two taps away shows إث ث أر خ ج س ح in Arabic order. It reads as an untranslated screen at the exact moment the product is trying to feel personal.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:941 `<div className="mb-12 flex justify-center gap-3" dir="ltr">` and :955 `{(["M", "T", "W", "T", "F", "S", "S"][i])}`. The correct source exists at :43-44 `DAY_LABELS_EN` / `DAY_LABELS_AR` and is consumed properly at :417 `const label = (rtl ? DAY_LABELS_AR : DAY_LABELS_EN)[i];`.
proposedFix:
Pass `lang`/`rtl` down (it is already a prop on `StreakCelebration`) and use `(rtl ? DAY_LABELS_AR : DAY_LABELS_EN)[i]` at :955; remove the `dir="ltr"` on :941 so the week mirrors like the Oasis card.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Severity is overstated because the surface is effectively unreachable: Progress.tsx:125-131 only sets `celebrating` when `profile.streak` INCREASES while Progress is mounted, and `lastStreak` is seeded from the current streak on mount. Streaks only increment inside drills (store/app.ts:574 and recordDrillResult), which run on screens that replace Progress entirely (App.tsx:173 renders one screen at a time). The only live path is a second tab's `storage` rehydrate (store/app.ts:621-636). Worth fixing, but it is not "the app's biggest celebratory moment" in practice.

title: Full-screen streak celebration can't scroll, so its content is clipped on short phones
problem: The celebration is `fixed inset-0 … flex flex-col items-center justify-center … p-6` with no `overflow-y-auto`, and its footer is separately `fixed bottom-12` with no inline positioning. Its content stack (256px hero image + 32px, headline block + 40px, 40px day dots + 48px, note card + 40px) is roughly 700px before padding. On a 667px-tall device with browser chrome the top and bottom are cut off simultaneously, with `justify-center` splitting the overflow.
userImpact: On an iPhone SE-class phone the celebration hero and the "you've mastered N signs" note are partially cut off and there is no way to scroll to them. The `fixed bottom-12` footer, which has no `left`/`right`/`inset-x` and so falls back to static inline positioning, also hugs the screen edge instead of centring.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:904 `className="fixed inset-0 z-[100] flex select-none flex-col items-center justify-center bg-ink p-6 text-center focus:outline-none"` — no overflow property; content block :925-976; footer :978 `<footer className="fixed bottom-12 z-20 w-full max-w-md px-6">` with no horizontal inset.
proposedFix:
Add `overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain` and change `justify-center` to `justify-start` with `my-auto` on the inner block so short viewports scroll instead of clipping. Give the footer `inset-x-0 mx-auto` so it centres, and add bottom padding to the content equal to the footer height so they never overlap.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Two corrections. (1) The footer claim is wrong: the `fixed bottom-12 w-full max-w-md px-6` footer at :978 is an absolutely-positioned child of a flex container, so its auto inline offset resolves to the flex static position, which `items-center` centres — it does not hug the edge. Drop that part of the fix; only the missing scroll is the defect. (2) Same reachability caveat as the day-labels finding: Progress.tsx:125-131 means this overlay essentially never renders in normal single-tab use.

title: Every node on the Home learning path announces "Practise with camera", including locked nodes and the treasure chest
problem: All path-node buttons get one static label: `aria-label={`${node.title} — ${t("practiceCamera", lang)}`}`. The button does not open the camera — it opens a bottom sheet — and the label is identical for `current`, `done`, `locked` and `milestone` nodes. Locked/milestone nodes open a sheet whose only button is `disabled`.
userImpact: A screen-reader user hears "Unit 1 — Practise with camera" for a node that is locked and leads to a disabled dialog, and has no way to distinguish done, current and locked nodes at all — that state is conveyed purely by circle colour and glyph, all of which are inline styles with no text alternative. They tab through 6+ identical-sounding buttons and hit a dead end on most of them.
evidence: src/screens/Home.tsx:324-332 — a single `aria-label` for all statuses; `onClick={() => setOpenId(node.id)}` opens the sheet, not the camera. Status is only expressed visually via `circleStyle(node.status)` (:168-197) and `nodeGlyph(node.status)` (:199-230), both `aria-hidden`-free but text-free. The sheet's action button is `disabled={locked}` (:634).
proposedFix:
Build the label from the node's status: append the same string the sheet already computes — `t("pathNewSign")` / `t("pathDoneMeta")` / `t("pathLockedMeta")` / `t("pathChestMeta")` — instead of `practiceCamera`, and add `aria-disabled` (not `disabled`, so it stays focusable and explains itself) on locked nodes. Also set `aria-haspopup="dialog"` since the tap opens a sheet.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The 'dead end' framing is a bit strong — the sheet does announce state through its `meta` line (:629) and the locked path is recoverable. Also, the visible node title text at :343 means the node's identity is already announced; only its status and the camera claim are wrong.

title: Onboarding uses `min-h-screen` (100vh), pushing the primary CTA below the fold on iOS
problem: Both onboarding wrappers use `min-h-screen`. On iOS Safari `100vh` is the *large* viewport (toolbar retracted), so on first paint with the toolbar shown the visible area is 60–115px shorter. The layout is header → `flex-1` main → footer CTA, so the footer lands exactly at the 100vh mark. Every other full-height surface in the codebase uses `min-h-dvh`.
userImpact: The very first thing a new user sees — the "Get started" button on the splash, then "Continue" on every subsequent step — is partly or entirely below the fold on an iPhone, and the page must be scrolled to reach it. First-run drop-off from a CTA nobody can see.
evidence: src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:197 `className={`flex min-h-screen w-full justify-center …`}` and :198 `className="flex min-h-screen w-full max-w-md flex-col"`; footer CTA at :662-668. Compare src/components/ScreenShell.tsx:48 and :77 (`min-h-dvh`), src/components/NoProfileFallback.tsx:23, src/screens/FirstSign.tsx:117 — all `dvh`. src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:62 has the same `min-h-screen` slip.
proposedFix:
Replace `min-h-screen` with `min-h-dvh` at Onboarding.tsx:197 and :198 (and ErrorBoundary.tsx:62). Add `safe-bottom` to the footer wrapper at :663 so it clears the iOS home indicator.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The footer-only `safe-bottom` misses the name step, which owns its own submit button inside the form at :652-656 (`mt-auto pb-6 pt-6`) and is skipped by the `step !== "name"` guard at :662.

title: The onboarding and add-family name inputs have no label — only a placeholder
problem: The name field in the final onboarding step has `autoFocus`, `value`, `placeholder` and nothing else — no `<label>`, no `aria-label`, no `aria-labelledby`. The add-family-member input in Family.tsx:190-197 is identical. Settings' name field (Settings.tsx:147-157) does it correctly with `<label htmlFor="set-name">`.
userImpact: A screen-reader user reaching the last onboarding step (the only step that creates their profile) hears "edit text, blank" with no indication of what to type. Once they start typing the placeholder disappears in visual UI too, so the field loses its only hint. Same on the add-family flow, which is how a Deaf household member gets added.
evidence: src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:643-650 `<input autoFocus value={name} onChange={…} placeholder={lang === "ar" ? "اسمك" : "Your name"} maxLength={20} className="…" />`; src/screens/Family.tsx:190-197 `<input autoFocus value={newName} … placeholder={t("famName", lang)} … />`. Correct pattern at src/screens/Settings.tsx:147-157.
proposedFix: Add `aria-label={pick(lang, "Your name", "اسمك")}` on Onboarding.tsx:643 (or wrap in a visible `<label>` mirroring Settings), and `aria-label={t("famName", lang)}` on Family.tsx:190. Keep the placeholder as a hint, not the name.

title: Lesson buttons append a hardcoded "→" that points backwards in Arabic
problem: Three lesson CTAs concatenate a literal right-pointing arrow onto localized copy: `{t("lsContinue", lang)} →` (:379), `${t("lsContinue", lang)} →` (:575) and `{pick(lang, "Continue", "متابعة")} →` (:891). The i18n layer already handles this correctly elsewhere by shipping a mirrored glyph per language — `pathStartCta: { en: "Start →", ar: "ابدأ ←" }` (src/i18n.ts:219).
userImpact: In Arabic every "Continue" in the lesson flow shows an arrow pointing the wrong way — visually it reads as "go back" at the exact moment the app is asking the learner to move forward. It is inconsistent with the Home path buttons, which mirror correctly.
evidence: src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:379 `{t("lsContinue", lang)} →`, :575 `{picked === null ? t("lsCheck", lang) : `${t("lsContinue", lang)} →`}`, :891 `{pick(lang, "Continue", "متابعة")} →`. Correct precedent: src/i18n.ts:163 `celStreakCta: { en: "Keep it going →", ar: "واصل التقدّم ←" }`, :219-220, :375.
proposedFix: Replace the literal with `{lang === "ar" ? "←" : "→"}` at all three sites (the same one-liner already used at src/screens/InfoPages.tsx:147), or fold the arrow into the i18n string the way `pathStartCta` does.

title: The lesson's "Check" button is white-on-light-grey at 1.57:1 and further dimmed to 40% — its label is invisible
problem: Before an answer is picked, the footer button is forced to `!bg-[#C7D0CE] !text-white` while `Button` also applies `disabled:opacity-40`. White on #C7D0CE measures 1.57:1; at 40% opacity on top of that it is effectively blank.
userImpact: On every recognise/recall/review drill — the majority of the lesson — the only footer control is a grey slab with no readable text. The learner cannot tell whether it is a button, what it says, or that they need to pick an answer first. It reads as a broken/unfinished screen.
evidence: src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:568-576 `<Button full variant="secondary" disabled={picked === null} className={`h-[54px] rounded-[17px] ${picked === null ? "!bg-[#C7D0CE] !text-white" : ""}`}` combined with src/components/ui.tsx:108 `… disabled:opacity-40 disabled:shadow-none …`. Measured white on #C7D0CE = 1.57:1.
proposedFix:
Use a dark label on the disabled fill — `!bg-[#EDE3D2] !text-muted` (`muted` #566B68 gives ~4.4:1 on #EDE3D2) — and drop the extra `disabled:opacity-40` for this variant via `disabled:opacity-100` on the override, so the "Check" instruction stays legible while still reading as inactive.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: `disabled:opacity-100` will win (Tailwind emits the opacity scale ascending, so .disabled\:opacity-100 lands after .disabled\:opacity-40), so that half works. But the proposed colour does not clear AA: #566B68 on #EDE3D2 measures 4.47:1 and the label is 16px bold, which is small text — use `text-ink/70` or `text-teal-deep` on that fill instead.

title: Settings daily-goal rows show "3 min / 7 min / 15 min" in Latin digits and English inside the Arabic UI
problem: `goalOptions` hardcodes `min: "3 min"`, `"7 min"`, `"15 min"` and renders them raw at line 249, with no `pick()` and no `toLocaleDigits`. The localized equivalents already exist in the dictionary — `obCasual: { en: "Casual · 3 min", ar: "خفيف · ٣ دقائق" }` etc. — and onboarding uses them.
userImpact: An Arabic user in Settings sees "هادئ" beside a Latin "3 min" chip, while the same choice in onboarding read "خفيف · ٣ دقائق". The screen looks half-translated and the numerals are inconsistent with every other figure in the app, which uses Eastern-Arabic digits.
evidence: src/screens/Settings.tsx:224-228 `const goalOptions: { … min: string }[] = [ { v: "casual", en: "Casual", ar: "هادئ", min: "3 min" }, … ]` and :248-250 `{o.min}`. Localized source: src/i18n.ts:32-34 `obCasual/obRegular/obSerious`; digit helper `toLocaleDigits` already imported in this file at :19.
proposedFix: Add an `arMin` field ("٣ دقائق", "٧ دقائق", "١٥ دقيقة") and render `pick(lang, o.min, o.arMin)`, or split the existing `obCasual`/`obRegular`/`obSerious` strings on " · " and reuse the minute half so there is a single source.

title: The camera reference stage shows a gold play button that is decoration, not a control
problem: A `<span>` styled exactly like the app's spring buttons — gold circle, 40px, `boxShadow: "0 5px 0 #C89A3D"`, a ▶ glyph — is absolutely positioned in the bottom-end corner of the reference stage. It has `aria-hidden="true"`, no `onClick`, and no handler anywhere.
userImpact: Every learner on every camera drill sees what looks like a play button over the reference handshape, taps it expecting the demo to play, and gets nothing. It sits in exactly the corner where the Dictionary and LessonPlayer put their real replay buttons, so the affordance is learned and then broken.
evidence: src/components/CameraTrainer.tsx:460-466 `▶`. Compare the real replay controls at src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:763-772 and src/components/SignDemo.tsx:142-150, both `
proposedFix: Either make it real — a `<button>` with `aria-label={pick(lang, "Replay", "إعادة")}` that bumps a `replayKey` remounting `referenceChip` (matching SignDemo's replay) — or delete it and let the static reference stage read as static. Do not ship a button-shaped span.

title: Practise sub-screens disagree about where Back goes — two land on Home, one on the chooser
problem: `AppNav` treats `practiseChooser`, `camera`, `words` and `fingerspell` as one tab (src/components/AppNav.tsx:34). But CameraPractice's back button routes to `{ name: "home" }` (:107), Fingerspell's routes to `{ name: "home" }` (Fingerspell.tsx:130), and Words' routes to `{ name: "practiseChooser" }` (Words.tsx:83) — three sibling screens, two different behaviours.
userImpact: A learner taps Practise → Alphabet → Back and is thrown out of the Practise tab onto Learn, losing their place; the same gesture from Words correctly returns to the Practise hub. The bottom tab stays highlighted on Practise while the content is Home, so the nav state and the content disagree.
evidence: src/screens/CameraPractice.tsx:105-112 `onClick={() => go({ name: "home" })}` with `aria-label={t("back", lang)}`; src/screens/Fingerspell.tsx:128-135 same; src/screens/Words.tsx:81-88 `onClick={() => go({ name: "practiseChooser" })}`. Tab grouping at src/components/AppNav.tsx:33-37 `active: ["practiseChooser", "camera", "words", "fingerspell"]`.
proposedFix:
Point CameraPractice.tsx:107 and Fingerspell.tsx:130 at `{ name: "practiseChooser" }` so Back stays inside the Practise tab, matching Words. (Home's own "Practise the alphabet" card still deep-links straight to the camera; a one-tap return to the hub is the right landing either way.)

VERIFIER CORRECTION: One claim in the user-impact is false: `isActive` (AppNav.tsx:44) keys off `screen.name`, so navigating to `home` lights the Learn tab. The nav highlight and the content do NOT disagree; the defect is purely the inconsistent Back destination.

title: Sign-card status captions (Letter / Unit 1 / New) sit at 3.3:1 in 11px bold
problem: `STATUS_META` gives the `letter`, `unit` and `new` statuses the tone `text-teal-deep/60`. Composited, #0A4F4C at 60% over the card's `bg-white` is ~#6C9594 → 3.30:1. The caption renders at `text-[11px] font-bold uppercase tracking-widest`, which is small text and needs 4.5:1.
userImpact: The status caption under every unpractised sign — the line telling the learner whether an item is a letter, part of Unit 1, or brand new — is washed out on the majority of dictionary cards (`new` and `letter` are the default states for a fresh user).
evidence:
src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:35-37 `letter: { …, tone: "text-teal-deep/60" }, unit: { …, tone: "text-teal-deep/60" }, new: { …, tone: "text-teal-deep/60" }` rendered at :506-508 `

`, over `bg-white` (:483). Measured 3.30:1. The other tones (`text-gold-deep`, `text-coral-deep`) pass.
proposedFix: Change those three tones to `text-muted` (#566B68 → 5.3:1 on white) or full-opacity `text-teal-deep`. If the muting is wanted as hierarchy, express it with size/weight, not opacity on an already-small label.

title: The "practised" tick on word tiles is aria-hidden and the tile has no accessible name for it
problem: `WordCard` marks mastered words with a teal check badge that is `aria-hidden="true"`, and the button carries no `aria-label` or other text conveying the state. The only accessible content is the two gloss spans.
userImpact: A screen-reader user browsing the Words hub cannot tell which words they have already practised — the entire progress signal on that screen is visual-only. Sighted keyboard users are fine; anyone using speech gets an undifferentiated list of 19 words.
evidence: src/screens/Words.tsx:203-207 `{practised && ()}` on a `
proposedFix:
Add `aria-label={`${gloss} — ${practised ? t("prUnlocked", lang) : ""}`}` on the WordCard button (or an `sr-only` span next to the tick). Do the same for `LetterCell`, appending the cell's `state`.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: `aria-label` on the WordCard button works (no ancestor label there), but an `sr-only` span alongside the tick would NOT work if an aria-label is also added — pick one. Use `prUnlocked` (i18n.ts:331) as suggested, or better a distinct 'practised' string, since 'Unlocked' is achievement vocabulary.

title: The AI-transparency hero card double-flips in RTL, so it ends up un-mirrored
problem: The card carries both `md:flex-row` and `rtl:md:flex-row-reverse`. Under `dir="rtl"`, `flex-row` already lays children right-to-left; adding `flex-row-reverse` reverses that again, putting the illustration back on the left exactly as in LTR, while `md:text-start` still right-aligns the copy.
userImpact: On Arabic desktop the app's hero "You're always right about your hands" card is the one block on the page that does not mirror — the image leads from the left against a right-to-left reading flow, breaking the visual rhythm of the rest of the screen.
evidence: src/screens/InfoPages.tsx:183-186 `className="flex flex-col items-center gap-6 border-4 border-gold p-8 text-center motion-safe:animate-pop-in md:flex-row md:p-8 md:text-start rtl:md:flex-row-reverse"`. Tailwind 3.4.19 generates `.rtl\:md\:flex-row-reverse:where([dir=rtl],[dir=rtl] *)` (verified in node_modules/tailwindcss/src/corePlugins.js:211), which wins over the plain `md:flex-row` in the same media query.
proposedFix: Delete `rtl:md:flex-row-reverse`. `md:flex-row` alone mirrors correctly under `dir="rtl"`. (Nothing else in the file needs it — the arrow at :147 already mirrors via `lang === "ar" ? "←" : "→"`.)

title: The profile menu declares role="menu"/"menuitem" but supports no arrow-key navigation
problem: The dropdown is `role="menu"` with `role="menuitem"` children, which puts most screen readers into application mode where Up/Down arrows are expected to move between items. `useDialog` only handles Tab and Escape — arrows do nothing. The codebase explicitly avoids this trap elsewhere: AllSigns.tsx:194-195 and Progress.tsx:158-159 both carry an "L11" comment choosing `role="group"` + `aria-pressed` over ARIA tab/menu semantics for exactly this reason.
userImpact: A screen-reader user opening the profile menu (the only route to Progress and Settings) presses arrow keys as the role promises, nothing moves, and the menu feels stuck. Tab still works, so it is recoverable, but it violates the pattern the role announces.
evidence: src/components/AppNav.tsx:75-81 `<div ref={menuRef} role="menu" aria-label={t("navProfile", lang)} tabIndex={-1} …>` with items at :95-98 `role="menuitem"`. Key handling is entirely in src/components/useDialog.ts:32-50 — Escape and Tab only.
proposedFix: Simplest and consistent with the project's own L11 convention: drop `role="menu"`/`role="menuitem"`, keep `aria-haspopup="dialog"` on the trigger and give the panel `role="dialog" aria-label={t("navProfile", lang)}` — the existing Tab trap and Escape then match what is announced.

title: Per-learner mastery dots use aria-label on a bare <span>, which screen readers ignore
problem: Each flagged-sign row shows one coloured dot per household learner with `title` and `aria-label` on a plain `<span>` that has no role. `aria-label` is only exposed on elements with a role that supports naming; a generic span is not one, so assistive tech announces nothing.
