userImpact: The Deaf household member's key oversight signal — how far each family member has got on the sign they flagged — is colour-only and completely inaccessible to speech users, and it is also colour-only for anyone with a colour-vision deficiency (the four levels are four hues at similar lightness).
evidence: src/screens/Family.tsx:299-310 `<span key={p.id} title={`${p.displayName} · ${num(lvl, lang)}/3`} aria-label={`${p.displayName} · ${num(lvl, lang)}/3`} className="h-2.5 w-2.5 flex-none rounded-full" style={{ backgroundColor: dotColor(lvl) }} />`; `dotColor` at :272-273 is the only differentiator.
proposedFix:
Give the dot `role="img"` so the `aria-label` is exposed, and give the containing span at :298 `role="group"` with a label like "household progress". Add a non-colour cue (ring thickness or a small filled/hollow difference) so level is not hue-only.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Adding `role="img"` will NOT surface it: the whole row is a `<button>` carrying an explicit `aria-label` at Family.tsx:279, which replaces all descendant content in name computation — an inner label or sr-only span is ignored. The only working fix is to fold the per-learner levels into that button's own aria-label at :279 (the non-colour visual cue suggestion stands).

title: The learner-facing privacy chip prints an internal build id
problem: The always-visible on-device privacy chip appends `· build {__BUILD__}` to the trust copy. `__BUILD__` is a Vite define, not localized, and is rendered in Latin characters inside an otherwise Arabic string when the UI is Arabic.
userImpact: On the app's single most important trust surface — "100% on your device, no video leaves your phone" — the sentence ends with developer debug output. In Arabic it is a stray Latin token mid-line. It undercuts the polish of the exact message the product is staking its credibility on.
evidence: src/components/CameraTrainer.tsx:608-614 `{t("camPrivacy", lang)} · build {__BUILD__}`. Note the same file already gates other diagnostics behind `?debug` (`const DEBUG = … .has("debug")`, :46-47, used at :702 and :748).
proposedFix: Wrap the build span in the existing `DEBUG` gate — `{DEBUG && · build {__BUILD__}}` — matching how the grading readout and raw camera error are already handled in this file. The version is still discoverable via Settings' `aboutVersion` line.

title: There is no router: back button / back gesture exits the app from every screen
problem: Navigation is a single non-persisted Zustand field. `go()` does `set({screen}); window.scrollTo(...)` and nothing else — no `history.pushState`, no `popstate` listener, no hash, no URL change anywhere in `src/` (grep for pushState/popstate finds only `src/screens/Onboarding.test.tsx`). The app therefore has exactly one history entry for its entire lifetime.
userImpact: On an installed Android PWA (the stated target) the hardware Back button and the back-swipe gesture close Sawiyya from ANY screen — mid-lesson, mid-camera-drill, mid-onboarding. On desktop/mobile browsers Back leaves the site. A page refresh always dumps the user on Home, losing the screen they were on. Nothing can be linked, shared or bookmarked, even though the code repeatedly describes surfaces as "deep-linkable" (AllSigns.tsx:85 "Deep-linkable detail (H5)"). This is the root cause of most of the app's "I got lost" feeling: every screen has to invent its own hard-coded escape hatch, and they all disagree (see back-target-inconsistency).
evidence: src/store/ui.ts:26-32 — `export const useUi = create<UiState>((set) => ({ screen: { name: "home" }, go: (screen) => { set({ screen }); window.scrollTo({ top: 0 }); } }))`. src/App.tsx:149-189 renders a flat `screen.name ===` switch. `grep -rn "pushState|popstate|window.history|location.hash" src/` returns only test files.
proposedFix:
Make the URL the source of truth for `screen`. In `src/store/ui.ts`: serialise `Screen` to a hash (e.g. `#/camera/alpha-alif`, `#/lesson/review`, `#/signs/hello`) — hash keeps it GitHub-Pages-safe with `base: "./"` and needs no server rewrite. `go()` calls `history.pushState(screen, "", hash)` then `set({screen})`; add a module-level `window.addEventListener("popstate", e => set({screen: parse(location.hash) }))`; initialise `screen` from `location.hash` on store creation with a `home` fallback. Then delete every hard-coded `onClose`/back handler in ScreenShell consumers and replace with `history.back()`. This is the single structural change that fixes the most confusion in the app.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Hash routing is the right shape, but two gaps: (1) `history.back()` cannot replace the hard-coded `onClose` handlers wholesale — on a cold load straight into a screen (deep link, PWA start_url, or the first entry after install) there is no in-app entry to pop and back exits the site; each takeover screen needs a `back-or-parent` helper that falls through to its parent screen when `history.state` shows no in-app depth. (2) src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:164-169 runs its own 10-step machine with its own `back()`; unless those steps also push history, hardware Back still kills the app mid-setup, which is the worst instance of the bug.

title: Onboarding's "Arabic Alphabet" card silently ends setup at step 4 of 10 with default answers
problem: On the `learn` step (index 3 of a 10-step machine) the "Arabic Alphabet" card calls `finish({ destination: { name: "camera", targetSignId: "alpha-alif", autoStart: true } })`. `finish()` immediately calls `createProfile` + `completeOnboarding`. Because `overrides.skipAll` is undefined it uses the untouched React state defaults: `persona = "parent"`, `hand = "R"`, `goal = "regular"`, and `name = ""` which falls back to the literal string "Me" / "أنا". The header progress bar is showing 4/10 at that moment (`progressPct` = (3+1)/10 = 40%).
userImpact: A user who taps the card the screen visually pushes hardest (it is the only one badged "Ready") never sees the handedness, daily-goal, reminder or name steps, and never finds out they were skipped. Home then greets them "Marhaba, Me" forever (Home.tsx:257-260), their household member card shows the initial "M", and their role is silently "parent" — which is load-bearing for Family Mode. The progress bar actively lied about how much was left.
evidence: src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:337-339 (the onClick), 125-141 (`finish` — `role: overrides?.skipAll ? "parent" : persona`, `displayName = name.trim() || (lang === "ar" ? "أنا" : "Me")`), 150-172 (`STEP_ORDER` of 10, `progressPct`).
proposedFix:
Do not finish onboarding from the `learn` step. Store the choice (`const [track, setTrack] = useState<"alphabet"|"words">("alphabet")`), call `advance()`, and let the `name` step's `finish()` route to `{ name: "camera", targetSignId: "alpha-alif", autoStart: true }` when `track === "alphabet"`. If the fast-path must stay, at minimum jump straight to the `name` step first so the profile gets a real name, and drop the progress bar to a 4-step count for that branch.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The proposed 'store a track, finish at the name step' is right, but it collides with ob-learn-step-is-inert — fix both in one change or the second edit will re-touch the same handlers. Also note the fast path is deliberate (the comment at :138-139 calls it 'practice-first'), so the minimal honest fix is to route the alphabet card to the `name` step and finish from there, not to delete the fast path.

title: Onboarding "Skip" discards choices the user already made, including the Deaf role
problem: The "Skip" affordance renders on every step after the splash and calls `finish({ skipAll: true })`, which hard-codes `role: "parent"`, `dominantHand: "R"`, `dailyGoal: "regular"` — overwriting whatever the user has already selected. A user who picks "أنا أصم — أهيّئ عائلتي" (persona `deaf`, presented with a "Special Path" badge) on the `why` step and then taps Skip on the next screen is written to the store as `parent`.
userImpact: The persona choice is the whole premise of the product ("the Deaf member directs the curriculum"), and `role === "deaf"` gates: who can deactivate a flag (store/app.ts:507), whether flagging counts as an active day (store/app.ts:570), and who is excluded from the shared board and household streak (store/app.ts:716, 741). A user who explicitly selects the Deaf path and then skips the remaining chrome ends up in a household where they cannot own their own flags and the Family screen tells them nobody has flagged anything. There is no in-app way to change role afterwards — Settings exposes name, language, hand and goal only.
evidence: src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:238-248 (Skip button, rendered whenever `step !== "splash"`), 125-141 (`finish` overrides). src/store/app.ts:507 `const canDeactivate = existing.raisedByProfileId === byProfileId || by?.role === "deaf"`; 570 `by?.role === "deaf" ? ...`; 716 `const hearing = s.profiles.filter((p) => p.role !== "deaf")`. src/screens/Settings.tsx:69 — the `set()` patch type has no `role`.
proposedFix:
Change `finish({skipAll:true})` to keep whatever the user has already touched: drop the `skipAll` branch entirely and let `finish()` always use the live `persona`/`hand`/`goal` state (the initial values are already sensible defaults). Separately, add a role row to Settings' Account group so the choice is recoverable.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Dropping the `skipAll` branch is correct and safe (the initial state values are identical to the hard-coded ones), but `skipAll` is also what makes Skip meaningfully different from Continue — after the change the flag is unused and should be deleted from the signature at :125-128, not left dangling.

title: "What do you want to learn?" records nothing — every answer ends on the letter Alif
problem: The `learn` step offers three cards. "Everyday signs (Hello, milk, more, thank you…)" and "Other Gulf dialects — coming soon" both do exactly the same thing: `onClick={() => setStep("why")}`. Neither stores any state, and `finish()`'s default destination is `{ name: "firstSign" }`, which hard-codes `signById("alpha-alif")`. The footer CTA on that step also just calls `setStep("why")`, so there is no distinction between answering and not answering.
userImpact: A user who says "I want to learn everyday signs — hello, milk, thank you" is dropped, three screens later, into a graded camera drill for the Arabic letter ا. The "coming soon" card is not disabled and gives exactly the same feedback as a real choice, so it reads as a selectable option that was accepted. The first question the app asks has no consequence anywhere in the codebase — the single clearest instance of the app promising something it does not deliver.
evidence: src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:364 (`onClick={() => setStep("why")}` for Everyday signs), 382-384 (identical handler for Other Gulf dialects), 183 (footer CTA also `setStep("why")`), 140 (`go(overrides?.destination ?? { name: "firstSign" })`), src/screens/FirstSign.tsx:75 (`const sign = signById("alpha-alif")`).
proposedFix:
Store the answer (`track`) and honour it in `finish()`: `alphabet` → camera on `alpha-alif`; `words` → `{ name: "words" }` (the Words hub already exists and works). Render the dialects card with `disabled` and `aria-disabled`, or remove it from the choice list and show it as a non-interactive note like PractiseChooser.tsx:167-179 already does.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Routing `words` to `{name:'words'}` works (src/screens/Words.tsx renders SignDemo and a self-mark path), but the Words hub is `chrome='tabs'` and its only in-content back arrow goes to `practiseChooser` (Words.tsx:83) — a user finishing onboarding there lands one tap from a screen they never saw. Pair this with the back-target fix or send the words track to `{name:'allSigns'}` instead.

title: Every "Watch" control in the Dictionary is a no-op — it only relabels itself
problem: `DetailPanel` has three separate watch affordances — the centred "Watch" chip, the gold play button, and (for every non-camera-gradable sign) the primary full-width "Watch & practise" CTA. All three call `handleWatch`, defined as `const handleWatch = () => setWatched(true)`. `watched` is read in exactly two places, both of which are the button's own label text. The panel renders a static `<SignGlyph>` medallion; it never mounts `<SignDemo>`, which is the component every other screen uses to actually show the sign.
userImpact: The Dictionary is one of the four bottom-nav tabs and the app's main browse surface. Tapping the biggest button on a sign's detail page changes the word "Watch" to "Watch Again" and nothing else happens. For the 19 non-gradable word signs this is worse: the camera CTA is correctly hidden and replaced by "Watch & practise" as the sole primary action, so those signs have literally no working action on their detail page. This is almost certainly a large part of "Sawiyya doesn't make sense".
evidence: src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:544 `const [watched, setWatched] = useState(false)`; :568 `const handleWatch = () => setWatched(true)`; :639-646 (chip, `onClick={handleWatch}`, label `{watched ? "Watch Again" : "Watch"}`); :649-657 (gold play button, `onClick={handleWatch}`); :724-727 (`<SpringButton variant="gold" ... onClick={handleWatch}>{t("signWatchPractise", lang)}`). Contrast src/screens/Words.tsx:133 `<SignDemo sign={selected} lang={lang} />`, src/screens/LessonPlayer.tsx:336, src/screens/FirstSign.tsx:246.
proposedFix:
Replace the static medallion frame in `DetailPanel` (AllSigns.tsx:620-658) with `<SignDemo sign={sign} lang={lang} />` — it already renders real signer photos, hand skeletons, the instruction stage for footage-less words, and owns its own working Replay chip. Delete `watched`/`handleWatch` and the two duplicate play buttons. Point the non-gradable primary CTA at the same thing (or make it a self-mark, matching Words.tsx:41-48).

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Swapping in `<SignDemo sign={sign} lang={lang} />` needs two guards the fix omits. (1) SignDemo prints the hint inside its own stage for footage-less words (`demoShowsHint`, SignDemo.tsx:11-14), so AllSigns' 'How to sign' block at :698-720 must be wrapped in `!demoShowsHint(sign)` exactly as Words.tsx:135 does, or the hint prints twice. (2) For the 19 word signs SignDemo renders the instruction stage with its Replay chip suppressed, so 'Watch & practise' would still have nothing to trigger — those signs need the Words-style self-mark action (Words.tsx:40-47) as the primary CTA, not a watch button.

title: "Which hand do you sign with?" is collected, stored, editable — and read by nothing
problem: `dominantHand` is a full onboarding step, a persisted Profile field, and a two-card Settings control with a mirrored left-hand icon. Grepping the whole of `src/` shows it is only ever written (Onboarding.tsx:133, Family.tsx:93, Settings.tsx:196) and normalised on rehydrate (store/app.ts:235). No recognizer, renderer or layout code reads it. CameraTrainer determines chirality at runtime from MediaPipe's own detection: `const mirror = frame.detectedHand === "Left"`.
userImpact: A left-handed learner taps "Left" in Settings, sees the card highlight, and nothing anywhere in the app changes — no mirrored reference hand, no different grading, no different demo. Worse, the AI-transparency page markets this exact capability as something you configure: "The camera learns your hands — left or right…". A control that visibly responds but has zero effect is the classic "this app doesn't make sense" signal.
evidence: `grep -rn dominantHand src/` → writes only (src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:133, src/screens/Family.tsx:93, src/screens/Settings.tsx:196, src/store/app.ts:235/323/331) and test fixtures; zero reads. src/components/CameraTrainer.tsx:179 `const mirror = frame.detectedHand === "Left"; // canonicalise both hands (§6.8)`. src/screens/InfoPages.tsx:64 markets "left or right".
proposedFix:
Either wire it or cut it. Wiring is cheap and visible: pass `profile.dominantHand` into `HandSkeleton`/`SignDemo` and apply `scaleX(-1)` to the reference handshape when it is `"L"`, so a left-handed learner sees a left reference hand. If that is deferred, delete the `hand` step from `STEP_ORDER` (Onboarding.tsx:150-161) and the `HandCards` block (Settings.tsx:185-222) rather than shipping a lever with nothing on the other end.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The 'mirror the reference with scaleX(-1)' half of the fix conflicts with an invariant the codebase states repeatedly: handshape glyphs and photos never mirror (src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:97-98, src/components/SignGlyph.tsx header, Home.tsx:201/334). Flipping an ArSL21L signer photo also produces a synthetic image still labelled 'Real signer photo' (SignDemo.tsx:186-196), which breaks the app's provenance rule. Prefer the second option — cut the step and the Settings cards — or mirror only the vector HandSkeleton, never the photo, and only as a deliberate documented exception.

title: Three screens in the same tab have three different hard-coded back targets, none respecting entry point
problem: Words, Fingerspell and CameraPractice all render `chrome="tabs"` (so the bottom bar is visible with Practise highlighted, per AppNav.tsx:34) AND each draws its own in-content circular back arrow with a fixed destination: Words → `practiseChooser`, Fingerspell → `home`, CameraPractice → `home`. The other four tab screens (Home, PractiseChooser, AllSigns, Family) have no back arrow at all.
userImpact: Home links straight to Words and Fingerspell (Home.tsx:369, 385). Enter Words from the Learn tab, press Back — you land in the Practise tab you never visited. Enter Fingerspell from the Practise chooser, press Back — you are thrown out of Practise onto Home. Enter the camera from the Practise chooser, press Back — same. The user cannot form a model of what the arrow does, and it competes with a bottom tab bar that is already on screen.
evidence: src/screens/Words.tsx:83 `onClick={() => go({ name: "practiseChooser" })}`; src/screens/Fingerspell.tsx:130 `onClick={() => go({ name: "home" })}`; src/screens/CameraPractice.tsx:107 `onClick={() => go({ name: "home" })}`. All three: `<ScreenShell lang={lang} chrome="tabs">` (Words.tsx:76, Fingerspell.tsx:122, CameraPractice.tsx:99). src/components/AppNav.tsx:34 `active: ["practiseChooser", "camera", "words", "fingerspell"]`.
proposedFix: Once history routing exists (nav-no-url-no-history), replace all three with `history.back()`. Until then, make the target uniform — all three should return to `practiseChooser`, since that is the tab AppNav says you are in — or remove the arrow from all three and rely on the tab bar, matching the other four tab screens.

title: "Review" on a completed word lesson opens the camera on the letter Alif
problem: In the path node sheet, a `done` lesson routes to `go({ name: "camera", targetSignId: lessonCameraTarget(openNode.lesson) })`. `lessonCameraTarget` returns the first `cameraGradable` sign in the lesson, or `undefined`. Every one of the 19 A1 word signs is constructed with `cameraGradable: false`, so for all four word lessons the target is `undefined`, and `CameraPractice` falls back to `useState(initialSignId ?? "alpha-alif")`.
userImpact: A learner who finishes "First connections" (I love you, hello, yes, no), taps that node again and presses "Review" is dropped into a graded camera drill for the Arabic letter ا — a completely unrelated sign. This is the exact wrong-target bug the codebase fixes everywhere else (the H5 gate at Home.tsx:432-436, Family.tsx:73-76, FlagPicker.tsx:324-328 all branch to `allSigns` when a sign is not gradable); this call site was missed.
evidence: src/screens/Home.tsx:38-39 `const lessonCameraTarget = (lesson) => lesson.signIds.map(signById).find((s) => s?.cameraGradable)?.id;` :588-590 `} else if (st === "done" && openNode.lesson) { go({ name: "camera", targetSignId: lessonCameraTarget(openNode.lesson) }); }`. src/screens/CameraPractice.tsx:30 `useState(initialSignId ?? "alpha-alif")`. src/content/signs.ts:94-158 — every `S(...)` call for A1 passes `false` for `cameraGradable`.
proposedFix:
Apply the same H5 gate used elsewhere: `const target = lessonCameraTarget(openNode.lesson); go(target ? { name: "camera", targetSignId: target } : { name: "lesson", lessonId: openNode.lesson.id })` — replaying the lesson is the honest review for a watch-only word lesson. Alternatively route to `{ name: "words" }`.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Routing to `{name:'lesson', lessonId}` is right, but note Home.tsx:593-594 already suppresses the secondary camera button when `cameraTarget` is undefined — the cleanest change is to compute the target once above `onAction` and reuse it in both places, otherwise the sheet keeps two divergent notions of whether a camera target exists.

title: "Add to Daily Review" is invisible on phones — the review queue cannot be seeded from a phone
problem: The `Add to Daily Review` button in `DetailPanel` carries `className="hidden gap-2 md:inline-flex"`, so it renders only at ≥768px. The mobile branch below it (`<div className="flex gap-3 md:hidden">`) offers Flag and Share instead. `addToReview` is the only action in the app that seeds an SRS card without drilling, and it has no other call site.
userImpact: Sawiyya is a portrait-locked, standalone-display PWA (vite.config.ts manifest). On the device it is designed for, a learner browsing the dictionary has no way to say "remind me about this sign". The desktop panel and the mobile sheet render from the same component but expose different capabilities, so the app behaves differently depending on screen width with no explanation.
evidence: src/screens/AllSigns.tsx:736-745 `<SpringButton ... onClick={onAddReview} className="hidden gap-2 md:inline-flex">`; :748 `<div className="flex gap-3 md:hidden">` (Flag + Share). `grep -rn addToReview src/` → declared store/app.ts:92/476, wired AllSigns.tsx:78/349/393 only.
proposedFix: Move `Add to Daily Review` above the mobile Flag/Share row and drop the `hidden md:inline-flex` classes so it renders at all widths — the sheet already scrolls. If vertical space is tight on mobile, demote Share (which is already duplicated by the OS share sheet) rather than the only SRS entry point.

title: Home's unit banner names one unit while the trail below it lists both units' lessons
problem: `pathNodes` is built from `LESSONS.map(...)` — all 8 lessons, 4 from `alpha-u1` and 4 from `a1-u1`. The banner directly above the trail is derived from a single unit: `unitIdx = UNITS.findIndex(u => u.id === nextLesson.unitId)`, rendering "UNIT 1 / The Arabic Alphabet". There is no divider, header or visual break between the alphabet lessons and the word lessons in the node list.
userImpact: A new learner sees a banner reading "Unit 1 · The Arabic Alphabet" and, immediately under it as part of the same trail, four locked nodes called "First connections", "Everyday needs", "Home & people" and "People around you" — which are Unit 2 word lessons, not alphabet content. The label does not match what is beneath it, so the trail reads as an eight-lesson alphabet unit whose last four lessons have nothing to do with letters.
evidence: src/screens/Home.tsx:117-119 `const unitIdx = Math.max(0, UNITS.findIndex((u) => u.id === nextLesson.unitId)); const unit = UNITS[unitIdx];` :123-129 `const pathNodes = nodes.map(...)` where `nodes = LESSONS.map(...)` (:108). src/content/signs.ts:189 `UNITS = [UNIT_ALPHA, UNIT_A1_U1]`; :202-236 `LESSONS` — 4 `alphaLesson()` entries then 4 `a1-u1-*` entries.
proposedFix: Group the trail by unit: iterate `UNITS`, and for each render the teal banner followed only by `LESSONS.filter(l => l.unitId === u.id)`. Style the not-yet-reached unit's banner as muted. This is presentational only and preserves every existing node handler.

title: The treasure chest closing the learning path is permanently un-openable
problem: `nextMilestone` returns the first ladder rung the learner has NOT reached (`ladder.find(l => l.value < l.at)`), so `ms` is by construction always an unreached milestone. Home appends it as a node with `status: "milestone"`, and the node sheet computes `const locked = st === "locked" || st === "milestone"`, giving it a disabled button labelled `t("pathLocked")` and `cursor: default`.
userImpact: The gold treasure chest sits at the visual end of the learning path — the most rewarding-looking object on the Learn tab. Tapping it always opens a sheet whose only button is greyed out and says "Locked", at every level of progress, forever. There is no state in which it ever becomes tappable, and the sheet gives no route to the thing that would advance it.
evidence: src/lesson/milestones.ts:55 `const next = ladder.find((l) => l.value < l.at); if (!next) return null;`. src/screens/Home.tsx:131 `if (ms) pathNodes.push({ id: "__milestone", status: "milestone", title: ms.label, off: 0 });` :567 `const locked = st === "locked" || st === "milestone";` :634-637 `disabled={locked} onClick={locked ? undefined : onAction}`.
proposedFix:
Give the milestone sheet a real action: show `ms.progress` as a bar plus a live CTA that routes to whatever advances it (camera for the mastery rungs, `{name:"family"}` for the family rungs, `{name:"flagPicker"}` when the household has no flags). If a milestone genuinely has no next step, render it as a non-interactive node (drop the `<button>` wrapper at Home.tsx:324) so it never invites a tap.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: The mastery rungs cannot all be advanced by 'the camera' — 'All the word unit mastered' (milestones.ts:53) covers 19 signs that are `cameraGradable:false` and cap at mastery 2, so a camera CTA there would be the same wrong-target bug as home-done-lesson-opens-alif. Route mastery rungs to the lesson/Words path, family rungs to `{name:'family'}`, and prefer the non-interactive-node option for anything else.

title: Seven brand images use root-absolute paths and 404 under the GitHub Pages project path
problem: `vite.config.ts` sets `base: "./"` because the app is served from `https://theshumba.github.io/sawiyya/`. Most image references are relative (`"brand/stitch-34.png"`) and resolve correctly, but `InfoPages.tsx` (six references) and `Progress.tsx` (one) use `"/brand/stitch-XX.png"`. Vite does not rewrite string literals in JS, so these ship verbatim — confirmed in the built bundle: `dist/assets/index-BOu8oRIr.js` contains both `"/brand/stitch-02.png"` and `"brand/stitch-34.png"`.
userImpact: On the live site every illustration on the "How the AI works" page (four storybook cards plus the gold hero band), the Privacy page's hero illustration, and the streak-celebration hero all resolve to `theshumba.github.io/brand/...` and 404. The AI-transparency page — the trust and awards-entry surface — renders as five cards with empty 160px holes where the artwork should be, and the streak celebration shows an empty 256px box above the headline.
evidence: vite.config.ts:8 `base: "./"`. src/screens/InfoPages.tsx:51, 60, 69, 78, 91, 317 — all `"/brand/stitch-*.png"`. src/screens/Progress.tsx:927 `src="/brand/stitch-46.png"`. Built output: `grep -o '"[./]*brand/stitch-[0-9]*\.png"' dist/assets/index-*.js` yields `"/brand/stitch-02.png"` … alongside the correct relative `"brand/stitch-34.png"`. src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:84 confirms the deploy path: `"URL:https://theshumba.github.io/sawiyya/"`.
proposedFix: Strip the leading slash from all seven references so they match the rest of the codebase (`"brand/stitch-21.png"` etc.). Safer still, `import stitch21 from "../../public/brand/stitch-21.png"` so Vite emits a base-correct hashed URL and a missing file becomes a build error.

title: The profile button's request badge opens a menu that does not contain the requests
problem: `requests` counts pinned flags raised by someone other than the active profile and renders as a numeric `<Badge>` on the profile button. That button's only behaviour is toggling a menu containing exactly two items: Progress and Settings. Neither shows flags. The flagged signs live on the Family tab (Family.tsx:252-337) and on Home (Home.tsx:398-440).
userImpact: A learner sees "3" on their avatar, taps it expecting to see what three things need attention, and gets Progress and Settings. The badge never clears from that menu, so it reads as a notification the app will not let them resolve.
evidence: src/components/AppNav.tsx:60-62 `const requests = profile ? pinnedFlagSigns(app, profile.id).filter((f) => f.raisedByProfileId !== profile.id).length : 0;` :124-128 renders `<Badge count={requests} .../>` on the profile button; :91-108 the menu contains only `{name:"progress"}` and `{name:"settings"}`. The same count is surfaced correctly on the Family tab at src/screens/Family.tsx:252-337.
proposedFix: Move the badge onto the Family tab button (`TABS[3]`), where the flags actually live, or add a third menu item `{ name: "family" }` labelled with the request count above Progress/Settings.

title: Home's milestone and daily-goal cards are buttons that open an unrelated generic camera
problem: The milestone card (`ms.label` + a progress bar) and the `GoalCard` are both wrapped in `ScreenCard`/`GoalCard` with an `onClick`, which `ScreenCard` renders as a full-width `<button>`. Both handlers are `() => go({ name: "camera" })`, which lands on the default `alpha-alif`. The milestone may be "10 signs your whole family can do", which camera practice on Alif does not advance.
userImpact: Two cards on the Learn tab look like progress readouts, behave like buttons, and take the user somewhere unrelated to what they display. Combined with the Practise card and the empty-state card, Home has four separate tappable routes to the same untargeted camera screen, each with different copy — so the user cannot tell which cards are informational and which are actions.
evidence: src/screens/Home.tsx:539-543 `<ScreenCard variant="elevated" ... onClick={() => go({ name: "camera" })}>` around the `ms.label` + progress bar; :534 `<GoalCard ... onClick={() => go({ name: "camera" })} />`; :353 and :509 two more `go({ name: "camera" })` cards. src/components/ui.tsx:146-157 — `ScreenCard` with `onClick` renders a `<button>`.
proposedFix:
Drop `onClick` from the milestone card and the GoalCard so they render as plain `<div>`s (ScreenCard already falls through to a div when `onClick` is omitted), leaving the coral "Practise" card as the single camera entry point on Home. If the milestone should be actionable, route it to what actually advances it (`{name:"family"}` for family rungs, camera for mastery rungs), matching the fix for home-treasure-node-always-locked.

VERIFIER CORRECTION: Do not strip GoalCard's onClick. Routing a daily-goal card to practice is deliberate (GoalCard.tsx:25 'optional tap target (practice-first: routes to camera)') and it is the warm CTA when the goal is unmet; removing it leaves the goal widget inert. Limit the change to the milestone card, and note it duplicates the treasure node on the same screen — both render the same `ms` (Home.tsx:131 and :539), so fix them together or Home will show one tappable and one dead copy of the same milestone.

title: Progress.tsx calls hooks after a conditional return, and every screen's no-profile fallback is unreachable
problem: `Progress` returns `<NoProfileFallback />` at line 66 and then calls `useState` (71), `useMemo` (97, 99, 115), `useState`/`useRef` (125-126) and `useEffect` (127). That is a Rules-of-Hooks violation: any render where `profile` flips from null to non-null throws "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render". It is dormant only because `App.tsx` refuses to render the screen tree unless a profile exists — which also means `NoProfileFallback` is dead code in all ten screens that guard with it.
userImpact: No user-visible symptom today, but it is a landmine: any future change that renders a screen before the profile resolves (lazy profile load, a route restored from a URL, a profile-switch race) turns the Progress tab into a white screen behind the error boundary. Meanwhile ~60 lines of "escape hatch" UI that the team believes protects against dead ends can never run.
evidence: src/screens/Progress.tsx:65-71 — `const profile = activeProfile(app); if (!profile) return <NoProfileFallback />; ... const [tab, setTab] = useState<Tab>("oasis");` then :97 `useMemo`, :127 `useEffect`. src/App.tsx:128-135 `if (!onboarded || !profile) { return <Onboarding /> }` — the gate that makes the guard unreachable. Contrast the correct ordering in src/screens/Words.tsx:28-34 and src/screens/Family.tsx:64-68, where all hooks precede the guard.
proposedFix: Move the `if (!profile) return <NoProfileFallback />;` in Progress.tsx below every hook call (after the `useEffect` at line 127), matching Words/Family. Then decide about `NoProfileFallback`: either keep it and have `App.tsx` render screens optimistically, or delete the guard from all ten screens and keep the single check in App.tsx.
